algorithm.title: Interpreting standard deviation and confidence intervals

nodes.text: Evaluate sample data: check sample size, mean, and standard deviation
Standard deviation reflects dispersion of individual values around the mean
**Larger standard deviation:** wider variability in individual response
Standard error of the mean (SE = SD / √n) reflects precision of sample mean
Calculate 95% confidence interval: mean ± 1.96 × SE
**Confidence intervals do not overlap:** statistically significant difference between group means
**Confidence intervals overlap:** difference between group means may not be significant

algorithm.title: Interpreting relative risk and confidence intervals

nodes.text: Point estimate relative to null value of 1.0 indicates direction of association
Examine 95% confidence interval boundaries for inclusion of 1.0
**CI entirely below 1.0 (RR < 1.0):** statistically significant decreased risk or protection
**CI entirely above 1.0 (RR > 1.0):** statistically significant increased risk
**CI includes 1.0:** no statistically significant association observed

Require two concurrent effective forms of contraception (e.g. oral contraceptive + barrier method)
**Contraception timeline:** maintain dual methods 1 month prior to, during, and 1 month after therapy
Avoid concomitant tetracyclines (doxycycline, minocycline) due to risk of idiopathic intracranial hypertension
**Laboratory monitoring:** obtain baseline and monthly liver function tests and fasting lipid panel

UWSA2:Q128.boardCall: 6 weeks post-allopurinol + morbilliform rash + facial edema + 15% eosinophilia + transaminitis -> DRESS syndrome -> withdraw allopurinol.
UWSA2:Q128.hinge: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) mandates immediate withdrawal of the offending agent (allopurinol).
UWSA2:Q128.trap: Heterophile antibody testing evaluates mononucleosis, but allopurinol exposure 6 weeks ago and marked eosinophilia confirm DRESS.

A.clue: Anti-parasitic agent targeting helminthic infection
A.fit: Not here: eosinophilia is from drug hypersensitivity, not an intestinal nematode infection

B.clue: Empiric broad-spectrum antibacterial regimen
B.fit: Not here: fever and rash are drug-induced; unnecessary antibiotics can worsen hypersensitivity

C.clue: Mononucleosis heterophile antibody detection assay
C.fit: Not here: EBV causes pharyngitis and atypical lymphocytosis; patient has allopurinol DRESS syndrome

D.clue: Immediate cessation of causative pharmaceutical agent
D.fit: Here: 6 weeks post-allopurinol, morbilliform rash, facial edema, 15% eosinophilia, transaminitis

E.clue: Serologic testing for hepatitis B and C viruses
E.fit: Not here: acute transaminitis is part of multi-organ DRESS syndrome from allopurinol

F.clue: Serologic antibody assay for Treponema pallidum
F.fit: Not here: secondary syphilis causes palm/sole rash and mucous patches; lacks marked eosinophilia

nodes.text: Fever, diffuse rash, and eosinophilia weeks after starting allopurinol suggest DRESS.
Stop allopurinol immediately.
Check CBC with differential, transaminases, bilirubin, creatinine, and urinalysis. Trend abnormal results.
**Hepatitis with substantial transaminase elevation, nephritis, or myocarditis:** admit and initiate systemic corticosteroids with specialist input.
**Organ injury progresses despite drug withdrawal and corticosteroids:** seek specialist guidance on cyclosporine or other rescue treatment.
Document the reaction and avoid re-exposure.

UWSA2:Q129.hinge: Advanced cervical carcinoma invades laterally into parametria, encasing ureters and causing bilateral hydronephrosis in untreated HIV.
UWSA2:Q129.trap: Ovarian cancer causes pelvic masses and ascites, but does not present as a lateral lower uterine segment mass obstructing both ureters.

A.clue: Urothelial carcinoma arising from bladder mucosa
A.fit: Not here: causes gross painless hematuria; CT shows primary lower uterine mass, not bladder mass

B.clue: Invasive HPV-mediated cervical squamous cell malignancy
B.fit: Here: untreated HIV, irregular spotting, lower uterine mass extending laterally, bilateral hydronephrosis

C.clue: Adenocarcinoma arising from colonic mucosa
C.fit: Not here: causes hematochezia and bowel obstruction; does not present as lateral lower uterine mass

D.fit: Not here: causes bulky retroperitoneal adenopathy and B symptoms; AIDS-defining malignancy here is cervical cancer

E.fit: Not here: presents as adnexal mass with peritoneal carcinomatosis and ascites, not lower uterine mass

F.clue: Malignant epithelial neoplasm originating in renal cortex
F.fit: Not here: causes flank mass and hematuria; hydronephrosis here is secondary to extrinsic pelvic obstruction

G.clue: Primary transitional cell carcinoma of the ureter
G.fit: Not here: rare unilateral tumor causing hematuria; bilateral obstruction is caused by lateral pelvic invasion

H.clue: Benign uterine myometrial smooth muscle neoplasm
H.fit: Not here: benign leiomyomas rarely cause lateral pelvic sidewall invasion and bilateral hydronephrosis

algorithm.title: Management of advanced invasive cervical cancer

nodes.text: Untreated HIV: abnormal bleeding, back pain, bilateral hydronephrosis
Cervical mass invading parametria to pelvic sidewall, encasing ureters → cervical cancer
Cervical biopsy; MRI/PET-CT for extent
**Hydronephrosis with rising creatinine:** percutaneous nephrostomy or ureteral stent
**Locally advanced (IIB–IVA):** cisplatin chemoradiation + brachytherapy
**Microinvasive, fertility desired:** conization
Start antiretroviral therapy

UWSA2:Q130.hinge: Chalazion is a chronic granulomatous lipogranuloma arising from obstruction of meibomian (tarsal) tear glands.
UWSA2:Q130.trap: External hordeolum (stye) is an acute, painful, erythematous bacterial infection of an eyelash follicle, unlike a painless chalazion.

A.clue: Acute staphylococcal abscess of eyelash follicle
A.fit: Not here: causes an acute, exquisitely painful, erythematous pustular eyelid margin nodule

B.clue: Acute bacterial inflammation of lacrimal sac
B.fit: Not here: causes painful erythematous swelling over the medial canthal lacrimal sac with purulence

C.clue: Pyogenic infection extending posterior to orbital septum
C.fit: Not here: causes proptosis, ophthalmoplegia, pain with eye movement, and fever; absent here

D.fit: Here: 1 month painless rubbery nodule in lower eyelid tarsal plate

E.fit: Not here: causes tiny, dome-shaped, umbilicated papules; not a solitary deep rubbery tarsal nodule

F.fit: Not here: pediatric lateral eyebrow mass, not adult tarsal plate nodule

G.fit: Not here: soft, yellowish, velvety plaques on medial upper eyelids, not deep rubbery tarsal swelling

algorithm.title: Evaluation and management of eyelid nodules

nodes.text: Localized eyelid nodule: examine with lid eversion
**Acute tender pustule at lash margin:** external hordeolum; warm compresses
**Chronic painless firm tarsal nodule:** chalazion from meibomian gland occlusion; warm compresses, massage
**Persists > 1–2 months despite compresses:** incision and curettage or intralesional triamcinolone
**Recurrent at same site or lash loss:** biopsy for sebaceous carcinoma
**Pain with eye movement or proptosis:** orbital cellulitis; contrast CT, IV antibiotics
**Umbilicated pearly papules:** molluscum contagiosum

UWSA2:Q131.boardCall: Vertebral arch defect with bulging neural tissue (myelomeningocele) -> maternal folate vitamin deficiency.
UWSA2:Q131.hinge: Folate deficiency is the single most significant preventable risk factor for neural tube defects, compounded by carbamazepine.
UWSA2:Q131.trap: Family history of trisomy 21 increases aneuploidy risk, but confers no increased risk for structural neural tube defects.

A.clue: Chromosomal nondisjunction risk from oocyte senescence
A.fit: Not here: confers risk for trisomy 21, 18, and 13, not neural tube defects

B.clue: Inhaled tobacco combustion products causing fetal hypoxia
B.fit: Not here: causes fetal growth restriction and placental abruption, not primary myelomeningocele

C.clue: Sympathomimetic uteroplacental vasoconstriction
C.fit: Not here: causes placental abruption, preterm birth, and growth restriction; not myelomeningocele

D.fit: Not here: sibling with Down syndrome does not increase risk of structural neural tube defects

E.fit: Not here: causes cardiac Ebstein anomaly and neonatal nephrogenic DI, not neural tube defects

F.clue: Maternal folate depletion impairing neural tube closure
F.fit: Here: myelomeningocele on ultrasound, compounded by carbamazepine folate antagonism

algorithm.title: Etiology and prevention of neural tube defects

nodes.text: Fetal ultrasound at 12-20 weeks reveals open neural tube defect (myelomeningocele)
Inadequate periconceptional folate (vitamin deficiency) is the primary modifiable risk factor
**Antiepileptic drug use (carbamazepine, valproate):** impairs folate metabolism and increases NTD risk
Screen pregnant women with maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein (MSAFP) at 15-20 weeks
**High-risk pregnancy (antiepileptic use, prior NTD):** treat with high-dose preconceptional folic acid
Offer multidisciplinary counseling: pediatric neurosurgery, fetal therapy, and neonatology

UWSA2:Q132.hinge: Tdap vaccine is recommended during every pregnancy between 27-36 weeks to optimize passive maternal pertussis antibody transfer.
UWSA2:Q132.trap: Rubella antibody IgG not detected tempts MMR vaccination, but MMR is a live virus vaccine strictly contraindicated in pregnancy.

A.fit: Not here: patient is already immune (Hepatitis B surface antibody positive)

B.fit: Not here: strictly contraindicated in pregnancy due to theoretical congenital rubella risk

C.clue: Pneumococcal polysaccharide or conjugate immunization
C.fit: Not here: indicated for high-risk conditions (asplenia, chronic disease), not routine pregnancy

D.fit: Not here: indicated only for Rh-negative women; this patient is Blood type O, Rh-positive

E.clue: Inactivated toxoid and acellular pertussis booster
E.fit: Here: 28 weeks gestation, universal recommendation between 27-36 weeks to protect infant

F.clue: Live attenuated varicella-zoster virus immunization
F.fit: Not here: strictly contraindicated during pregnancy; administer postpartum if seronegative

nodes.text: Routine prenatal care at 27–36 weeks
Review maternal immunization status
Tdap to all pregnant patients at 27–36 weeks regardless of prior Tdap
**Influenza season:** inactivated influenza vaccine at any gestational age
**Rh-negative, unsensitized:** Rho(D) immune globulin at 28 weeks
Avoid live vaccines (MMR, varicella, intranasal influenza) in pregnancy
**Rubella or varicella nonimmune:** MMR and varicella immediately postpartum

UWSA2:Q133.boardCall: Pregnant woman with fever + flank tenderness + hypotension + ARDS lung infiltrates -> acute pyelonephritis.
UWSA2:Q133.hinge: High fever, costovertebral tenderness, and preterm contractions complicated by septic shock and ARDS indicate severe pyelonephritis.
UWSA2:Q133.trap: Preterm contractions and fever tempt chorioamnionitis, but the uterus is nontender and right flank tenderness points to kidney infection.

A.clue: Ascending upper urinary tract infection causing septic ARDS
A.fit: Here: 31 weeks gestation, right flank tenderness, fever 38.9 C, hypotension, lung infiltrates

B.clue: Catastrophic entry of amniotic fluid into circulation
B.fit: Not here: presents during labor with sudden cardiovascular collapse, DIC, and arrest, not flank pain

C.clue: Viral orthomyxovirus respiratory infection
C.fit: Not here: causes dry cough, coryza, and myalgias; cannot explain right flank tenderness

D.clue: Polymicrobial intraamniotic infection of fetal membranes
D.fit: Not here: causes uterine tenderness and purulent amniotic fluid; uterus is nontender with intact membranes

E.clue: Dilated cardiomyopathy developing in peripartum window
E.fit: Not here: causes heart failure without high fever, flank tenderness, or acute septic shock

F.clue: Concealed retroplacental hemorrhage with uterine detachment
F.fit: Not here: causes severe continuous abdominal pain and hypertonic tender uterus, not flank tenderness

nodes.text: Pregnant: fever, flank pain, CVA tenderness → acute pyelonephritis
Admit; urine culture; IV ceftriaxone
**Hypoxemia + bilateral infiltrates:** pyelonephritis-associated ARDS → oxygen, ICU, cautious fluids
**Hypotension despite fluids:** norepinephrine; cefepime or piperacillin-tazobactam if Pseudomonas risk
**Preterm contractions < 34 weeks:** antenatal corticosteroids
**Fever beyond 48–72 h of antibiotics:** renal ultrasound for obstruction or abscess
Complete 14 days; suppressive antibiotics for rest of pregnancy

UWSA2:Q134.boardCall: Metastatic cancer with severe persistent pain wearing off on short-acting opioids -> add extended-release morphine.
UWSA2:Q134.hinge: Uncontrolled baseline cancer pain requires conversion to or addition of an around-the-clock extended-release opioid formulation.
UWSA2:Q134.trap: Increasing short-acting morphine frequency to every 2 hours disrupts sleep and fails to provide steady baseline analgesia.

A.clue: Around-the-clock long-acting baseline opioid formulation
A.fit: Here: metastatic cancer with severe constant pain waking from sleep on short-acting opioids

B.clue: Escalation of immediate-release opioid dosing frequency
B.fit: Not here: impractical and disrupts sleep; persistent pain requires around-the-clock long-acting agent

C.clue: Referral to peer psychoeducational cancer support group
C.fit: Not here: beneficial psychosocial adjunct, but fails to address severe unmanaged physical cancer pain

D.clue: Initiation of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor
D.fit: Not here: distress is secondary to uncontrolled physical pain; opioid optimization is immediate priority

E.clue: Psychostimulant administration for fatigue and alertness
E.fit: Not here: used for opioid-induced somnolence; patient suffers from waking pain, not opioid sedation

nodes.text: Cancer patient presenting with severe, progressive baseline pain despite short-acting opioids
Calculate total 24-hour baseline opioid requirement from regular and breakthrough doses
Initiate an around-the-clock extended-release opioid (extended-release morphine or transdermal fentanyl)
Prescribe short-acting immediate-release opioid for breakthrough pain
**Focal bone metastases with localized bone pain:** add external beam radiation therapy or bisphosphonate
**Neuropathic pain component (burning, radiating):** add gabapentinoid or duloxetine
Co-prescribe prophylactic bowel regimen (stimulant laxative + stool softener) to prevent constipation

UWSA2:Q135.boardCall: Acute scrotal pain + nausea/vomiting + absent cremasteric reflex -> testicular torsion from inadequate tunica vaginalis fixation.
UWSA2:Q135.hinge: Inadequate fixation of the testis to the tunica vaginalis (bell-clapper deformity) allows free twisting of the spermatic cord and acute ischemia.
UWSA2:Q135.trap: Sexually active history tempts epididymo-orchitis, but acute morning onset and absent cremasteric reflex confirm testicular torsion.

A.clue: Ascending retrograde bacterial infection of epididymis
A.fit: Not here: causes gradual onset of pain with preserved cremasteric reflex; reflex is absent here

B.clue: Blood extravasation within tunica vaginalis sac
B.fit: Not here: typically follows significant blunt scrotal trauma; torsion is spontaneous with absent cremasteric reflex

C.clue: Patent embryonic peritoneal outpouching
C.fit: Not here: causes communicating hydrocele or indirect inguinal hernia, not acute testicular ischemia

D.clue: Congenital lack of posterior testicular fixation
D.fit: Here: 16-year-old with sudden severe scrotal pain, vomiting, absent cremasteric reflex

E.clue: Ischemic twisting of vestigial mullerian remnant
E.fit: Not here: produces localized blue-dot sign and upper pole tenderness; cremasteric reflex is preserved

nodes.text: Adolescent: sudden severe unilateral scrotal pain with vomiting
High-riding horizontal testis, absent cremasteric reflex → torsion (bell-clapper deformity)
**Classic findings:** immediate detorsion + bilateral orchiopexy; no imaging delay
**Equivocal findings:** emergent color Doppler ultrasound
**Surgery unavoidably delayed:** manual outward detorsion as bridge
**Gradual pain, dysuria, intact cremasteric reflex:** epididymo-orchitis → ceftriaxone + doxycycline
**Blue dot sign, upper-pole tenderness:** torsed appendix testis → supportive care

UWSA2:Q136.trap: Primary syphilitic chancre is a painless indurated ulcer, but spontaneously resolves within 3-6 weeks rather than persisting for months.

D.fit: Not here: causes exquisitely painful deep ulcers with undermined borders and purulent buboes

nodes.text: Older smoker with chronic indurated penile ulcer and firm inguinal nodes
Exclude infectious ulcers: syphilis serology, HSV PCR
**Nonhealing indurated ulcer with negative syphilis and HSV tests:** punch or excisional biopsy
Squamous cell carcinoma: examine both groins; MRI if corporal invasion uncertain
**Lesion confined to glans or foreskin:** organ-preserving excision or glansectomy
**Corpora cavernosa invaded:** partial penectomy
**Palpable inguinal nodes:** ultrasound-guided FNA; inguinal lymphadenectomy if positive
**Tumor stage T1b or higher with nonpalpable nodes:** sentinel node biopsy

nodes.text: Young man: painless firm intratesticular mass, no transillumination
Scrotal ultrasound with Doppler
**Solid intratesticular mass:** AFP, β-hCG, LDH, then radical inguinal orchiectomy
**Transilluminating fluid around testis:** hydrocele; observe
**Bag of worms worse when standing:** varicocele
**Cystic mass above testis:** spermatocele; reassure
CT chest/abdomen/pelvis for staging; offer sperm banking
**Metastatic germ cell tumor:** cisplatin-based BEP

UWSA2:Q138.hinge: Palpable prostate nodule on DRE and elevated PSA (> 4.0 ng/mL) mandate prostate biopsy to rule out adenocarcinoma.

B.fit: Not here: diuretic increases voiding frequency, but cannot account for palpable prostate nodule or PSA 7.4

C.clue: Ultrasound-guided transrectal core needle tissue sampling
C.fit: Here: 66-year-old with palpable prostate nodule and elevated PSA 7.4 ng/mL

D.fit: Not here: appropriate for benign prostatic hyperplasia; must rule out prostate cancer first with biopsy

nodes.text: Man with lower urinary tract symptoms: digital rectal exam + serum PSA
**Palpable nodule or induration on DRE:** prostate biopsy (MRI-targeted + systematic cores)
**Elevated PSA with normal DRE:** repeat PSA after transient causes resolve, then prostate MRI
**Smooth symmetric enlargement, normal PSA:** BPH → tamsulosin ± finasteride
**Biopsy shows adenocarcinoma:** Gleason grade group + PSA + clinical stage for risk
Finasteride halves PSA; start BPH drugs only after cancer is excluded

D.fit: Not here: psychogenic ED preserves spontaneous nocturnal and morning erections; absent here

nodes.text: Erectile dysfunction with vascular risk factors and normal libido
Ask about nocturnal and morning erections to separate organic from psychogenic
**Loss of nocturnal erections + vascular risk factors:** vasculogenic ED from pelvic arterial insufficiency
**Situational ED with preserved nocturnal erections:** psychogenic; sex therapy
**Penile curvature with palpable plaque:** Peyronie disease
Smoking cessation, BP and lipid control; morning testosterone, A1c
Oral PDE-5 inhibitor (sildenafil, tadalafil)
**Taking nitrates or riociguat:** PDE-5 inhibitors contraindicated; vacuum device or alprostadil

**Subperiosteal abscess, coalescent disease, or progression despite IV antibiotics:** arrange surgical drainage with ENT.
**Intracranial extension on imaging:** involve neurosurgery urgently.

nodes.text: Acute onset of psychotic symptoms (delusions, hallucinations, disorganized thinking): evaluate duration

E.fit: Not here: causes hemodynamic instability, back pain, and flank ecchymosis without local pulsatile mass

nodes.text: Pain or swelling at femoral puncture site following arterial catheterization
Physical examination: evaluate for pulsatile mass, thrill, and auscultate for bruits
**Pulsatile mass with systolic bruit:** suspected femoral artery pseudoaneurysm
**No pulsatile mass, continuous thrill and continuous bruit:** suspected arteriovenous fistula
Perform duplex Doppler ultrasound of the groin to confirm diagnosis and measure defect size
**Small pseudoaneurysm (< 2 cm):** observe with serial duplex ultrasound
**Large (>= 2 cm) or expanding pseudoaneurysm:** perform ultrasound-guided thrombin injection or surgical repair

triggers.text: persistent right groin pain after cardiac catheterization 3 days ago
pulsatile mass at the catheter insertion site in the right inguinal region
Auscultation over the mass reveals a systolic bruit
swelling has developed at the right groin

UWSA2:Q090.boardCall: Post-cholecystectomy fever + peritonitis + elevated bilirubin + normal biliary ducts -> biliary leakage.
UWSA2:Q090.hinge: Post-cholecystectomy fever and peritonitis with normal-sized biliary ducts indicate cystic duct stump bile leakage.
UWSA2:Q090.trap: Retained gallstone causes choledocholithiasis and biliary duct dilation on ultrasound; here ducts are normal.

A.clue: Extravasation of bile from cystic duct stump
A.fit: Here: post-op day 4 cholecystectomy, fever 38.2 C, peritonitis, normal-sized biliary ducts

B.clue: Hepatocellular necrosis from drug toxicity
B.fit: Not here: acetaminophen-hydrocodone at therapeutic doses does not cause chemical peritonitis

C.clue: Benign unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia from glucuronidation deficiency
C.fit: Not here: causes mild unconjugated jaundice; does not cause fever, leukocytosis, or peritonitis

D.fit: Not here: causes transaminases > 1,000 U/L following profound prolonged shock, not peritonitis

E.fit: Not here: causes biliary ductal dilation on ultrasound; ultrasound here shows normal-sized ducts

F.clue: Mechanical obstruction of small intestinal lumen
F.fit: Not here: causes diffuse distension, hyperactive bowel sounds, and obstipation without focal biliary leak

nodes.text: Fever and abdominal pain days after laparoscopic cholecystectomy
RUQ ultrasound or CT: fluid collection, duct caliber
**Normal ducts + fluid collection:** cystic duct stump bile leak; HIDA confirms extravasation
**Dilated CBD with jaundice:** retained stone; ERCP extraction
Bile leak: ERCP sphincterotomy + biliary stent
**Biloma with fever or peritonitis:** percutaneous drainage + IV antibiotics
**Isolated unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, normal liver enzymes:** Gilbert syndrome; reassurance

triggers.text: laparoscopic cholecystectomy 4 days ago
Right upper quadrant tenderness with guarding and rebound tenderness
Right upper quadrant ultrasonography demonstrates normal-sized biliary ducts
healing surgical incisions without erythema

abnormal-uterine-bleeding.name: Abnormal uterine bleeding
abnormal-uterine-bleeding.scope: Adenomyosis, leiomyomas, endometrial polyps, ovulatory dysfunction, PALM-COEIN classification, endometrial biopsy
abnormal-uterine-bleeding.core: Abnormal uterine bleeding requires pregnancy exclusion, hemodynamic assessment and evaluation for structural disease or unopposed endometrial estrogen.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Perimenopause, PCOS, obesity, anticoagulants; lifelong heavy bleeding suggests inherited coagulopathy
Adenomyosis often multiparous; fibroids common during reproductive years

rows.label: Clues
items: Bleeding affecting quality of life, prolonged/heavy menses, intermenstrual or irregular bleeding
Tachycardia, orthostasis or syncope → clinically important blood loss
Postmenopausal bleeding requires malignancy evaluation even with a single episode

rows.label: Pathophys
items: PALM: Polyp, Adenomyosis, Leiomyoma, Malignancy/hyperplasia → structural causes
COEIN: Coagulopathy, Ovulatory dysfunction, Endometrial, Iatrogenic, Not otherwise classified
Anovulation → absent cyclic progesterone, unopposed proliferation and unstable shedding
Combined OCPs → uniform estrogen/progestin exposure **synchronizes endometrium**, preventing irregular shedding

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pregnancy test and CBC** first; pelvic examination localizes uterine versus cervical/vaginal bleeding
**Transvaginal ultrasound** evaluates structural lesions; saline sonohysterography/hysteroscopy for intracavitary disease
★ **Endometrial biopsy ≥45 years**; younger with persistent bleeding, unopposed estrogen or failed treatment
Postmenopausal bleeding: endometrial thickness >4 mm → sampling; persistent bleeding → biopsy regardless of thickness
TSH for suspected endocrine disease; coagulation/vWF testing for suggestive bleeding history

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable → IV access, blood resuscitation, urgent gynecology; tamponade or operative control if needed
Stable → high-dose combined OCP, progestin, tranexamic acid; no estrogen if prior VTE, hypertension, smoker >35
★ Long-term → **levonorgestrel IUD**, OCP/progestin; family complete, normal cavity → **ablation**; copper worsens
Fibroids: asymptomatic → **observation, any size**; symptomatic → myomectomy/embolization; hysterectomy if childbearing done
Polyp → hysteroscopic removal; adenomyosis refractory to hormones → hysterectomy

rows.label: Complications
items: Iron deficiency anemia; chronic anovulation → endometrial hyperplasia/cancer; structural lesions can impair fertility

rows.label: Prevention
items: Regular progestin exposure for chronic anovulation; replace iron and address metabolic drivers

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pregnancy complication: positive hCG; exclude ectopic pregnancy
Cervicitis: friable cervix and postcoital bleeding

table.title: Cause clues
rows: Firm irregular enlarged uterus; pressure symptoms
Labor-like pain, dilated os, beefy prolapsing tissue
Tender uterus; biopsy **plasma cells**, not neutrophils

acne-vulgaris.name: Acne vulgaris
acne-vulgaris.scope: Comedonal, inflammatory, and nodulocystic acne, topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide, oral antibiotics, isotretinoin, photosensitivity counseling
acne-vulgaris.core: Open or closed comedones with variable inflammatory papules, pustules, or nodules reflect pilosebaceous inflammation; severity and scarring determine treatment intensity.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Pubertal androgen activity, family history, occlusive products, friction
Exogenous androgens, glucocorticoids, lithium may provoke eruptions; irregular menses/hirsutism suggests androgen excess

rows.label: Clues
items: Face, chest, back commonly involved; mixed lesion types distinguish acne from monomorphic drug eruptions
Deep painful nodules, scars, or substantial psychosocial impairment justify early treatment escalation
Rapid virilization or severe sudden adult onset → assess endocrine/tumor cause

rows.label: Pathophys
items: **Androgens (testosterone, DHT) → sebum** + follicular hyperkeratinization + Cutibacterium acnes-driven inflammation
Topical retinoids normalize follicular shedding; benzoyl peroxide is bactericidal without antibiotic resistance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical morphology**; no routine culture or hormone testing for typical adolescent acne
Hyperandrogenic findings → pregnancy test and targeted testosterone/DHEAS evaluation
Before isotretinoin → pregnancy assessment when applicable, baseline lipids and liver enzymes; monitor during treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Combine topical mechanisms** and match intensity below; improvement requires weeks, maintenance prevents relapse
★ **Antibiotics require the topical backbone below**; never antibiotic monotherapy; limit systemic course
Adult hormonally driven acne → combined contraceptive or spironolactone when suitable; avoid spironolactone in pregnancy
★ Isotretinoin → **strict pregnancy prevention/testing**; avoid pregnancy during treatment and 1 month afterward
Pregnancy → azelaic acid/benzoyl peroxide options; avoid retinoids and tetracyclines

rows.label: Complications
items: Permanent scars, postinflammatory hyperpigmentation, depression; assess suicidal symptoms when present
Doxycycline → esophagitis/photosensitivity; isotretinoin → cheilitis, hypertriglyceridemia, hepatotoxicity
Avoid simultaneous isotretinoin + tetracycline because intracranial hypertension risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Noncomedogenic skin products, sunscreen**, gentle cleansing; avoid picking lesions
Doxycycline: water and remain upright; retinoids: gradual introduction to reduce irritation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Rosacea: flushing/telangiectasia without comedones
Folliculitis: monomorphic follicular pustules, often pruritic
Perioral dermatitis: periorificial papules, vermilion sparing, steroid exposure

acute-coronary-syndromes.name: Acute coronary syndromes
acute-coronary-syndromes.scope: Unstable angina, NSTEMI, STEMI, cardiac biomarkers, risk stratification (HEART/TIMI), antiplatelet and anticoagulation, reperfusion
acute-coronary-syndromes.core: Acute myocardial ischemia from coronary plaque disruption: distinguish occlusive infarction needing immediate reperfusion from non-ST-elevation syndromes needing risk-guided invasive management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CKD, age, premature family CAD
Cocaine/stimulants, anemia, tachyarrhythmia may provoke ischemia; distinguish supply-demand injury from plaque rupture

rows.label: Clues
items: Pressure with arm/jaw radiation, diaphoresis, nausea; older adults/diabetes may have dyspnea or epigastric pain alone
Inferior MI with hypotension, clear lungs, raised JVP → suspect RV infarction
★ New murmur, pulmonary edema, shock after MI → **mechanical complication**, urgent echo
Unexplained crash/syncope + ischemic ECG → primary MI; troponin over trauma imaging

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Platelet activation and thrombin-mediated clot reduce coronary perfusion; necrosis releases troponin
Type 2 MI: oxygen mismatch without acute atherothrombosis; treat precipitating cause

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG within 10 minutes**, repeat if nondiagnostic; serial high-sensitivity troponin using validated pathway
Posterior suspicion → V7–V9; inferior MI → right-sided leads; new LBBB alone insufficient for STEMI
★ **Do not wait for troponin before STEMI reperfusion**; bedside echo if diagnosis/complications uncertain
HEART ≤3 + negative serial troponins → low risk; TIMI/GRACE stratifies NSTE-ACS
STE: **V1–V6 → LAD**; **II, III, aVF + bradycardia → RCA**; I, aVL → circumflex

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Chewed aspirin**, P2Y12 inhibitor, anticoagulant such as heparin, high-intensity atorvastatin; oxygen only if hypoxemic
Nitroglycerin (**venodilation** → ↓preload) for pain unless hypotension, RV infarction, recent PDE5 inhibitor; avoid NSAIDs
★ STEMI → **primary PCI** within 90 minutes at PCI center, ≤120 minutes including transfer
IF PCI delay >120 minutes, symptoms <12 hours, no contraindication → fibrinolysis promptly, then transfer

rows.label: Complications
items: VT/VF, AV block, HF, cardiogenic shock; free-wall rupture
Later aneurysm/thrombus, embolism, Dressler syndrome; antithrombotics → bleeding
Post-MI murmur: **papillary rupture** → apical, no O₂ step-up; **septal rupture** → left sternal, RA→RV step-up

rows.label: Prevention
items: DAPT usually 12 months after ACS unless bleeding risk changes plan; cardiac rehabilitation, smoking cessation
ACE inhibitor/ARB for LV dysfunction; beta-blocker when stable, avoid in shock or acute decompensation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aortic dissection: abrupt tearing pain/pulse deficit; anticoagulation or lysis dangerous
Pericarditis: positional pleuritic pain, diffuse changes
PE: hypoxemia, thrombotic risk, RV strain

table.title: Syndrome branches
rows: Urgent catheterization if unstable; otherwise risk-guided angiography
Regional ST elevation or occlusion equivalent
Prior intracranial hemorrhage, active bleeding, suspected dissection
Stress or perfusion testing within 72 hours

acute-kidney-injury.name: Acute kidney injury
acute-kidney-injury.core: Abrupt loss of renal filtration: separate impaired perfusion, parenchymal injury, and urinary obstruction before treating the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Volume depletion, sepsis, cirrhosis, low-output heart failure (prerenal despite overload); baseline CKD increases vulnerability
NSAIDs constrict afferent arterioles; ACE inhibitors/ARBs reduce efferent tone during hypoperfusion
Aminoglycosides, pigment (dipstick blood, few RBCs), prolonged ischemia → tubular damage; antibiotics/PPIs → tubulointerstitial inflammation

rows.label: Clues
items: Oliguria, edema, uremic nausea; urine output may remain normal
AIN: fever, rash, eosinophilia sometimes present; classic triad often absent
★ Pulmonary edema, severe hyperkalemia, encephalopathy, pericarditis → **urgent renal support**
Anuria despite patent catheter after pelvic surgery + hydronephrosis → ureteral injury/ligation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced glomerular pressure, tubular epithelial injury, or backpressure → declining GFR

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ AKI: creatinine ↑≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 h, ≥1.5-fold within 7 days, or oliguria
Oliguria criterion: urine <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥6 h; trend creatinine, electrolytes, fluid balance
★ **Urinalysis + microscopy**, medication review; bladder scan → renal ultrasound if obstruction possible
FeNa unreliable with diuretics, CKD, early obstruction; urine eosinophils neither sensitive nor specific
Unexplained persistent injury or suspected glomerulonephritis → nephrology, possible kidney biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe hyperkalemia → **IV calcium**, insulin/dextrose; refractory electrolyte disturbance → dialysis
Hypovolemia (postoperative oliguria, high urine specific gravity) → saline bolus; congestion → loop diuretic; no reflex fluids in overload
Stop nephrotoxins, all NSAIDs including celecoxib (intra-articular steroid for joint pain); persistent AIN → glucocorticoids; renal-dose drugs
★ Obstruction → **catheter or ureteral decompression**; monitor postobstructive diuresis
Dialysis: refractory acidosis, hyperkalemia, intoxication, overload, symptomatic uremia; no isolated creatinine threshold

rows.label: Complications
items: Arrhythmias, acidosis, volume overload; subsequent CKD
Recovery diuresis → dehydration and electrolyte losses

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain perfusion during illness; review nephrotoxic combinations and monitor renal function
Contrast in high-risk CKD → **periprocedural IV isotonic saline**; diuretics, mannitol, metformin stop don't protect
ACR now limits contrast prophylaxis mainly to eGFR <30; older exam questions may expect wider hydration

rows.label: Mimics
items: CKD: longstanding abnormalities, small echogenic kidneys, chronic anemia
Trimethoprim effect: creatinine rise without true GFR decline

acute-kidney-injury.evidence: Not checked online; established KDIGO diagnostic criteria and renal teaching.

acute-liver-failure.name: Acute liver failure
acute-liver-failure.scope: Diagnostic criteria (encephalopathy, coagulopathy with INR >= 1.5, transaminitis), etiologies, complications (cerebral edema, sepsis), liver transplantation indications
acute-liver-failure.core: Abrupt hepatic decompensation in a previously noncirrhotic patient after an initially nonspecific prodrome.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Acetaminophen overdose, idiosyncratic drug injury, shock, Amanita ingestion
Acute viral hepatitis (HAV, HBV, HEV, HSV), autoimmune hepatitis, Wilson disease
Late pregnancy: acute fatty liver or HELLP. Hepatic venous thrombosis: Budd–Chiari

rows.label: Clues
items: New transaminitis, asterixis, sleep–wake reversal, jaundice
Late intracranial hypertension: pupillary changes, posturing, Cushing response
Very high AST/ALT with modest bilirubin → acetaminophen or ischemia

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hepatocyte loss → impaired synthesis and ammonia clearance → astrocyte swelling

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **INR ≥ 1.5** plus any encephalopathy within 26 weeks establishes syndrome
★ Acetaminophen level regardless of history. Send viral serologies, autoimmune markers, pregnancy test
Doppler US for hepatic vessels. Hemolysis with disproportionately low ALP → evaluate for Wilson disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ ICU and **early transplant-center transfer**. Intubate grade III–IV encephalopathy, correct hypoglycemia
★ Start **IV N-acetylcysteine** empirically while evaluating etiology, even with delayed presentation
Raised ICP → elevate head, hypertonic saline or mannitol. Suspected HSV → IV acyclovir
★ Poor prognosis or Wilson failure → **urgent transplant**. Uncontrolled sepsis or herniation may preclude
Reserve plasma for active bleeding or invasive procedures

rows.label: Complications
items: Cerebral edema → herniation. Also sepsis, AKI, multiorgan failure

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid stacking acetaminophen-containing products. Vaccinate against HBV routinely and HAV for at-risk travelers

rows.label: Mimics
items: Decompensated cirrhosis: prior portal hypertension, nodular liver, splenomegaly
Acute hepatitis without failure: preserved mentation

table.title: King's College poor-prognosis thresholds
rows: Unfavorable cause, e.g. idiosyncratic drug injury

acute-liver-failure.evidence: Checked AASLD acute liver failure guidance, O’Grady’s King’s College study and CDC vaccine guidance, Nov 2026.

acute-otitis-media.name: Acute otitis media
acute-otitis-media.scope: Bulging erythematous tympanic membrane, impaired mobility, oral amoxicillin first-line, amoxicillin-clavulanate, tympanostomy indications
acute-otitis-media.core: Acute otalgia with middle-ear effusion and a bulging tympanic membrane identifies acute otitis media; age, laterality, and severity guide antibiotics.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young age, daycare, viral URI, tobacco smoke exposure, absent breastfeeding
Craniofacial abnormalities and eustachian tube dysfunction increase recurrence

rows.label: Clues
items: Ear tugging, fever, irritability, poor feeding; spontaneous perforation causes new otorrhea
★ **Postauricular swelling/tenderness, protruding pinna** → mastoiditis
Erythematous membrane alone, especially during crying, insufficient for diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: URI-related eustachian edema traps fluid; pneumococcus, nontypeable H influenzae, Moraxella commonly infect middle ear

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pneumatic otoscopy**: reduced mobility supports effusion; moderate/severe bulging or nonexternal otorrhea diagnostic
Mild bulging requires recent otalgia or intense erythema; no effusion → no AOM diagnosis
Tympanometry if effusion uncertain; no routine imaging/cultures; suspected mastoiditis → **contrast CT temporal bones/head**
Failure after 48–72 h → repeat examination; persistent effusion alone does not mean antibiotic failure

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Acetaminophen or ibuprofen** for pain regardless of antibiotic decision
★ When treating → **amoxicillin 80–90 mg/kg/day**; 10 days if <2 years or severe
Recent amoxicillin within 30 days, purulent conjunctivitis, or amoxicillin failure → amoxicillin-clavulanate
Selected older nonsevere cases → 5–7 days; severe illness/complication or oral intolerance changes regimen
★ Recurrent AOM **≥3/6 months or ≥4/12 months** → tube evaluation; effusion required at candidacy assessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Conductive hearing loss, membrane perforation, mastoiditis, rare intracranial infection
Effusion ≥3 months → hearing assessment; tubes considered for bilateral persistent fluid with hearing difficulty

rows.label: Prevention
items: Pneumococcal/influenza vaccination, breastfeeding, smoke avoidance; no routine prophylactic antibiotics
Observe speech/hearing development in recurrent disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Otitis media with effusion: fluid, retracted gray membrane, no acute inflammation → **observe, no antibiotics**
Otitis externa: canal inflammation, pain with tragus/pinna movement
Referred dental/TMJ pain: normal middle-ear examination

adolescent-confidentiality-and-care.name: Adolescent confidentiality and care
adolescent-confidentiality-and-care.scope: Confidentiality principles, exceptions to parental notification, parental requests for drug testing, encouraging family involvement
adolescent-confidentiality-and-care.core: Provide adolescents private, developmentally appropriate care; explain confidentiality and its safety limits before sensitive questions.

rows.label: Principle
items: Confidentiality supports honest disclosure; consent authority and parental access vary by jurisdiction
Assent: involve the adolescent even when guardian permission remains necessary
Contraception: minors generally consent confidentially; no parental notice or pelvic exam required

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Interview alone** for sexual health, substance use, mood, violence, and safety
★ Explain permitted confidential services; protect portals, billing, and result notifications
Encourage trusted-adult involvement; never require disclosure for legally confidential services

rows.label: Don't
items: ★ Parental request for **drug testing** → discuss concern, interview teen; avoid covert testing
Do not promise absolute secrecy or automatically send sensitive findings to parents
Do not breach for experimental substance use without impairment → counsel, schedule **follow-up visit**

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Imminent danger, suspected **abuse/neglect/exploitation** → protective disclosure and reporting
Emergency treatment when delay risks serious harm; involve guardians when feasible
Emancipated minors generally self-consent; pregnancy alone does not universally confer emancipation

rows.label: Traps
items: Minor consent varies: STI, contraception, pregnancy, mental health, substance; **elective surgery** → parents
Mandatory reporting thresholds for consensual sexual activity depend on ages and local law
Disclose minimum necessary information; explain safety-driven disclosure to adolescent whenever feasible

adolescent-confidentiality-and-care.evidence: Not checked online; established ethics principles; jurisdiction-specific consent/reporting law must be verified locally.

adolescent-preventive-care.name: Adolescent preventive care
adolescent-preventive-care.scope: Leading causes of death, injury prevention, HEADSS psychosocial screening, adolescent screening tests
adolescent-preventive-care.core: Private, developmentally appropriate preventive visits identify injury risk, mental illness, substance use, sexual health needs, and barriers to healthy development.

rows.label: Who
items: All adolescents annually; explain confidentiality and safety exceptions, with some time alone
Leading death cause: **unintentional injury**, then suicide, homicide; risk varies by age and population

rows.label: Start/stop
items: HEADSS: Home, Education, Activities, Drugs, Sexuality, Suicide/depression; include strengths and safety
★ Annual **depression and suicide-risk screening from 12**; assess younger patients when concerned
HIV once during adolescence, repeat with ongoing risk; lipids once at 17–21 years

rows.label: Test
items: ★ BP, BMI, development; **chlamydia/gonorrhea annually** for sexually active females <25
Exposure-site STI testing for MSM; syphilis/TB/anemia testing by risk
Assess sleep, nutrition, eating disorders, substances/vaping, violence, school, sexual coercion

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Positive suicide screen → **brief safety assessment**, urgent evaluation for imminent risk
Post-menarche → pregnancy/STI prevention, contraception; treat STIs; substance-use counseling; accessible follow-up
Counsel seat belts, helmets, no impaired/distracted driving; secure firearms unloaded and locked

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **No routine Pap before 21**, even with sexual activity; STI screening uses separate tests
Depression screening alone misses some suicide risk; ask directly about thoughts and plans
Early post-menarche: irregular cycles normal, no hormone testing; update HPV, MenACWY, Tdap

adrenal-insufficiency.name: Adrenal insufficiency
adrenal-insufficiency.scope: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease), secondary adrenal insufficiency, cosyntropin stimulation test, morning serum cortisol, hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone replacement, adrenal crisis
adrenal-insufficiency.core: Weight loss, fatigue, orthostasis, and hyponatremia, or unexplained pressor-resistant shock after illness or interruption of glucocorticoids.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Primary: autoimmune destruction, TB, bilateral hemorrhage, metastases; associated autoimmune thyroid disease
★ Secondary: **prolonged glucocorticoids**, pituitary disease/surgery/apoplexy; abrupt withdrawal risks crisis
Crisis triggers: infection, trauma, surgery, missed replacement, vomiting

rows.label: Clues
items: Anorexia, abdominal pain, nausea, weakness; hypoglycemia, eosinophilia
Crisis: fever, confusion, severe volume depletion; symptoms may worsen rapidly during intercurrent illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cortisol deficiency reduces vascular catecholamine response and increases ADH
Primary gland failure removes mineralocorticoids; secondary disease retains renin–angiotensin-driven aldosterone

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **8 AM cortisol + ACTH**; very low cortisol supports, clearly high values argue against insufficiency
★ Equivocal basal cortisol → **cosyntropin (ACTH) stimulation**; inadequate assay-specific peak confirms impaired reserve
Traditional stimulated cutoff ≈18 µg/dL; newer assays may use ≈14–15; interpret laboratory standard
Primary → 21-hydroxylase antibodies, selected adrenal CT; secondary → pituitary evaluation/MRI
Recent pituitary injury may initially show normal cosyntropin response; clinical suspicion still matters

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Crisis → draw blood if feasible, **IV hydrocortisone + isotonic saline**, dextrose for hypoglycemia
Do not wait for confirmatory results; treat precipitant and correct electrolytes carefully
Coexisting hypothyroidism → glucocorticoid replacement before levothyroxine to avoid decompensation

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated crisis → arrhythmia, circulatory collapse, death; chronic undertreatment → impaired function
Excess replacement → osteoporosis, diabetes, Cushingoid features

rows.label: Prevention
items: Stress-dose plan, emergency injectable hydrocortisone, medical alert ID; taper prolonged systemic steroids
Vomiting prevents absorption → parenteral replacement and urgent evaluation; teach sick-day plans to caregivers

rows.label: Mimics
items: SIADH: euvolemia, normal potassium and cortisol reserve
Sepsis: infection may coexist and trigger crisis
Hypothyroidism: bradycardia, cold intolerance, weight gain

table.title: Primary versus secondary
rows: Low/inappropriately normal ACTH; potassium usually normal

adrenal-insufficiency.evidence: Not checked online; established endocrine teaching; cortisol cutoffs are assay dependent.

adrenal-masses.name: Adrenal masses
adrenal-masses.scope: Adrenal incidentaloma, adrenocortical carcinoma, functional vs nonfunctional evaluation, pheochromocytoma, hyperaldosteronism, Cushing syndrome, hyperandrogenism (DHEA-S), adrenal CT imaging, adrenalectomy indications
adrenal-masses.core: An incidental adrenal lesion requires two decisions: malignant potential on imaging and clinically important hormone secretion.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Incidental detection increases with age; known extra-adrenal cancer raises metastatic risk
MEN2/VHL/NF1 predispose to pheochromocytoma; most incidental lesions are benign cortical adenomas

rows.label: Clues
items: Often asymptomatic; weight loss, flank pain, rapid growth, or mixed steroid excess suggest carcinoma
Episodic headache/palpitations/diaphoresis → catecholamines; proximal weakness/easy bruising → cortisol excess
Resistant hypertension/hypokalemia → aldosterone; rapid virilization → adrenal androgen secretion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cortical tumors may secrete cortisol, aldosterone, or androgens; medullary tumors secrete catecholamines
Autonomous cortisol suppresses ACTH and contralateral adrenal function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Noncontrast adrenal CT** first; assess density, homogeneity, size, invasion; indeterminate → dedicated imaging
★ **1 mg overnight dexamethasone**: cortisol >1.8 µg/dL suggests autonomy; confirm ACTH independence
Plasma free or urinary fractionated metanephrines if lesion not clearly benign or pheochromocytoma symptoms
Hypertension/hypokalemia → aldosterone/renin; virilization/possible carcinoma → DHEA-S, precursors; **high DHEA-S** → adrenal source
★ **Never biopsy before excluding pheochromocytoma**; biopsy rarely distinguishes adenoma from cortical carcinoma

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Clinically significant unilateral hormone excess → **adrenalectomy**; suspected carcinoma requires preoperative staging
Pheochromocytoma: **phenoxybenzamine** alpha blockade, volume repletion before surgery; beta blockade only after alpha
Mild cortisol autonomy: individualize surgery by diabetes, hypertension, skeletal disease, and operative risk
Indeterminate unoperated lesion → repeat CT/MRI in 6–12 months; growth prompts reassessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Pheochromocytoma manipulation → hypertensive crisis; carcinoma → metastases
Postoperative adrenal insufficiency after cortisol-producing tumor removal → perioperative glucocorticoid coverage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Address cortisol-associated cardiometabolic and bone risk; genetic counseling for syndromic catecholamine tumors

rows.label: Mimics
items: Myelolipoma: macroscopic fat on CT
Adrenal metastasis: cancer history, often bilateral; biopsy only if management changes
Adrenal hemorrhage: acute pain, anticoagulation/trauma context, evolving imaging appearance

table.title: Imaging changes the answer
rows: Benign; no further imaging regardless of size

adult-immunizations.name: Adult immunizations
adult-immunizations.scope: Routine adult vaccines, immunocompromised and HIV, pregnancy, live-vaccine contraindications, chronic medical conditions (COPD, diabetes, liver disease), vaccine counseling and addressing hesitancy
adult-immunizations.core: Match vaccination to age, prior doses, pregnancy, immune status, and exposure risk; missed series resume without restarting.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **HepB**: all 19–59; ≥60 with risk/request; health worker anti-HBs negative post-series → revaccinate
**HIV any CD4**, liver disease/alcohol, COPD, diabetes, smoking → pneumococcal <50; liver → HepA/HepB
Asplenia → pneumococcal, MenACWY, MenB, Hib; HIV → MenACWY

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Pregnancy: **Tdap each pregnancy at 27–36 wk**; inactivated influenza any trimester
Maternal RSV: Abrysvo at 32–36 wk, September–January; previous pregnancy dose → infant antibody instead
RSV once: all ≥75; ages 50–74 with increased severe-disease risk

rows.label: Test
items: Anti-HBs/anti-HAV/VZV IgG positive → immune, skip; otherwise **do not delay vaccination** for serology
★ Immunocompromised ≥19 → recombinant zoster; HIV CD4 ≥200 permits MMR/varicella if nonimmune
HPV started <15 → two doses; ≥15 or immunocompromised → three

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **No live MMR, varicella, intranasal influenza**: severe immunosuppression, pregnancy (nonimmune → postpartum)
PCV15 → PPSV23: ≥8 weeks immunocompromised; older exams: PPSV23 alone; mild illness/antibiotics: no deferral
Hesitancy → elicit concern; inactivated influenza cannot cause flu, coincidental virus; refusal → document, revisit

table.title: Routine adult schedule
rows: Annual influenza; updated COVID-19 for all adults
Tdap once, then either every 10 years
PCV20/21 alone; PCV15 → PPSV23 after 1 year

amenorrhea.name: Amenorrhea
amenorrhea.scope: Primary amenorrhea (Turner syndrome, Mullerian agenesis, AIS), secondary amenorrhea (pregnancy, functional hypothalamic, hyperprolactinemia, thyroid, premature ovarian insufficiency, Asherman), diagnostic algorithm
amenorrhea.core: Absent menses requires pregnancy exclusion, then assessment of anatomy, estrogen status, thyroid function, prolactin, and the hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian axis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Weight loss, intense exercise, psychosocial stress; pituitary disease, dopamine-blocking drugs, thyroid dysfunction
Uterine instrumentation, chemotherapy, autoimmune disease; congenital reproductive tract or chromosomal abnormalities

rows.label: Clues
items: Primary: no menarche by 15; absent breast development by 13 also warrants evaluation
Secondary: ≥3 months absent previously regular cycles, or ≥6 months previously irregular
Galactorrhea/headache, visual symptoms, hot flashes, hirsutism, cyclic pelvic pain guide localization
Galactorrhea, hypothyroid signs → TSH first (TRH raises prolactin); unexplained prolactin → pituitary MRI

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Amenorrhea results from axis suppression, ovarian failure, chronic anovulation, or absent/obstructed outflow
Functional: energy deficit disrupts pulsatile GnRH → irregular, low gonadotropins, low estrogen

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **hCG first**, even if unlikely or premenarchal (ovulation precedes menarche); ultrasound assesses uterus, ovaries
★ TSH, prolactin, **FSH/estradiol**; low estradiol: high FSH → ovarian failure; low/normal FSH → hypothalamic/pituitary
**Progestin challenge**: bleed → anovulation (estrogen, outflow intact); no bleed → low estrogen/outflow defect, check FSH
POI before 40: ≥4 months irregular/absent cycles with FSH >25 IU/L; repeat if uncertain
Post-instrumentation amenorrhea with otherwise normal endocrine testing → saline sonography/hysteroscopy for adhesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Functional hypothalamic → **restore energy intake**, reduce excessive exercise, address eating disorder/stress
Prolactinoma → cabergoline; thyroid disease → correct thyroid function; Asherman → hysteroscopic adhesiolysis
★ POI → **estrogen replacement plus progestogen if uterus present**, usually until natural menopause age
Chronic anovulation → endometrial protection with cyclic progestogen or combined contraception; treat underlying cause
Hematocolpos → **transvaginal incision, drainage**; imperforate hymen → **cruciate hymenotomy**; ultrasound if anatomy unclear

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → infertility, low bone density; prolonged unopposed estrogen → endometrial hyperplasia
Absent uterus differs from absent ovaries: fertility options depend on anatomy and gonadal function

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, avoid overtraining/uterine injury; intermittent ovulation still requires contraception

rows.label: Mimics
items: Imperforate hymen: cyclic pain, bulging bluish hymen, hematocolpos
PCOS: hyperandrogenism with chronic anovulation, estrogen generally preserved

table.title: Primary amenorrhea: high FSH or absent uterus → karyotype

anorectal-disorders.name: Anorectal disorders
anorectal-disorders.scope: Anal fissure, internal and external hemorrhoids, anorectal abscess, fistula-in-ano, pruritus ani, topical vasodilators, fiber, sitz baths
anorectal-disorders.core: Anal pain, bleeding, swelling, or drainage requires inspection and focused examination; pain pattern distinguishes fissure, thrombosis, and infection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Constipation, straining, pregnancy, prolonged sitting; Crohn disease, diabetes, immunosuppression increase infection risk
Irritant soaps, moisture, fecal seepage contribute to pruritus ani

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Pain out of proportion, fever, spreading erythema, crepitus** → evaluate necrotizing perineal infection urgently
Posterior midline fissure common; lateral/multiple fissures suggest Crohn disease, infection, or malignancy
Internal hemorrhoids lie above dentate line; prolapse may require manual reduction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fissure causes internal sphincter spasm and local ischemia; hemorrhoids represent enlarged vascular cushions
Cryptoglandular infection creates abscess; persistent epithelialized tract can become a fistula

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Inspection first**, gentle DRE/anoscopy when tolerable; do not force painful fissure examination
Deep pain without visible lesion → CT/MRI for occult abscess; recurrent fistula → pelvic MRI
Rectal bleeding with anemia, weight loss, bowel change, or screening indication → colon evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Fiber, fluids, stool softening, **sitz baths**; fissure → topical anesthetic, nitroglycerin or diltiazem
Refractory chronic fissure → botulinum toxin or lateral internal sphincterotomy after continence-risk assessment
Internal hemorrhoids persisting despite conservative measures → rubber-band ligation; advanced prolapse → surgery
★ Abscess → **incision and drainage**; antibiotics added for cellulitis, systemic illness, or immunosuppression
Fistula → colorectal surgery; painful thrombosed external hemorrhoid within 72 hours → consider excision

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess recurrence, fistula, sepsis; sphincter injury → fecal incontinence
Chronic bleeding → iron deficiency; pruritus → excoriations and secondary infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid straining and prolonged toilet sitting; gentle cleansing, dry skin, barrier ointment for seepage

rows.label: Mimics
items: Anal cancer: persistent irregular ulcer/mass or large wart-like lesion, biopsy required
Proctitis: urgency, tenesmus, mucous discharge
Pinworm: nocturnal itch, especially children; tape test

table.title: Local patterns
rows: Tearing defecation pain; bright blood on paper
Recurrent purulent drainage from external opening

anorectal-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established colorectal teaching.

antidepressants.name: Antidepressants
antidepressants.scope: SSRIs, SNRIs, bupropion, mirtazapine, tricyclic antidepressants (anticholinergic toxicity, urinary retention, arrhythmia), MAO inhibitors, adverse effects (serotonin syndrome)
antidepressants.core: SSRIs usually start depression treatment; choose alternatives by accompanying symptoms, adverse effects, and overdose risk.

rows.label: Use
items: SSRIs/SNRIs: depression, anxiety; duloxetine also neuropathic pain
Bupropion: smoking cessation; mirtazapine: poor appetite with insomnia
TCAs/MAOIs: resistant depression; TCAs also neuropathic pain

rows.label: Mechanism
items: SSRIs: serotonin reuptake blockade; SNRIs/TCAs: serotonin + norepinephrine reuptake blockade
Bupropion: norepinephrine/dopamine reuptake blockade; mirtazapine: α2 antagonism
MAOIs: reduced monoamine degradation

rows.label: Adverse
items: SSRIs: GI upset, SIADH, bleeding; SNRIs: ↑BP; mirtazapine: sedation/weight gain; bupropion: activating
★ SSRI **sexual dysfunction** → **lower dose** first; other SSRIs rarely help; bupropion minimal
TCAs: constipation, urinary retention, conduction toxicity; MAOIs: orthostatic hypotension

rows.label: Avoid
items: ★ Bupropion lowers seizure threshold: **seizure or eating disorders**; CYP inhibitors raise levels
TCAs: urinary retention, glaucoma, conduction disease; anticholinergic delirium in older adults
TCA therapy with QTc/QRS prolongation → **stop TCA**, no waiting for levels

rows.label: Interactions
items: MAOI + tyramine/sympathomimetics → hypertensive crisis → **phentolamine** (α-blocker)
MAOI + SSRI/tramadol → serotonin syndrome; washout generally 14 days, after fluoxetine 5 weeks
Fluoxetine/paroxetine inhibit CYP2D6 → ↑TCA levels, toxicity

rows.label: Monitor
items: Mood, suicidality early in young adults; monitor adherence and functioning
Abrupt stop → **discontinuation**: flu-like aches, headache, dizziness, electric paresthesias, nausea, tremor
Response over 4–6 weeks; taper to stop, especially paroxetine and venlafaxine

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Serotonin syndrome**: clonus, fever/agitation → stop drugs, benzodiazepines; cyproheptadine
★ TCA overdose: Na⁺-channel blockade → **wide QRS**, arrhythmia, seizures → IV sodium bicarbonate
Bipolar depression: antidepressant monotherapy may provoke mania

antidepressants.evidence: Not checked online; established pharmacology and prescribing safety.

antiphospholipid-syndrome.name: Antiphospholipid syndrome
antiphospholipid-syndrome.scope: Vascular thrombosis (arterial, venous), pregnancy morbidity (recurrent early loss, fetal demise, severe preeclampsia), lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, anti-beta-2-glycoprotein I, anticoagulation management
antiphospholipid-syndrome.core: Acquired autoimmune hypercoagulability causes venous/arterial thrombosis or characteristic pregnancy morbidity with persistent antiphospholipid antibodies.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: SLE or primary APS without another autoimmune disease; estrogen, smoking, surgery increase event risk
Triple-antibody positivity and lupus anticoagulant confer greater thrombotic risk

rows.label: Clues
items: DVT/PE, ischemic stroke in young adult, livedo reticularis, mild thrombocytopenia
★ Paradoxical **prolonged aPTT with thrombosis**, not bleeding; screening aPTT may also be normal
Recurrent losses or early severe placental disease without another explanation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Antibodies promote endothelial/platelet activation, complement-mediated placental injury, and coagulation
Lupus anticoagulant interferes with phospholipid-dependent assays despite prothrombotic effects in vivo

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical event plus **persistent antibodies on two tests ≥12 weeks apart**
Order lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin IgG/IgM, anti-β2-glycoprotein I IgG/IgM
Medium/high anticardiolipin or >99th-percentile antibodies meaningful; isolated low transient titers insufficient
Lupus anticoagulant mixing study fails correction; excess phospholipid corrects; anticoagulants can confound testing
Classic obstetric criteria guide board questions; newer research classification scores do not replace clinical judgment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute thrombosis → heparin, then **warfarin**, usually long-term after unprovoked APS-associated VTE
Avoid DOACs with triple-positive or arterial APS; recurrent events need specialist intensity review
★ Obstetric APS without thrombosis → **low-dose aspirin + prophylactic LMWH** during pregnancy
Prior thrombotic APS in pregnancy → therapeutic LMWH + aspirin; postpartum anticoagulation required
Catastrophic multiorgan APS → urgent heparin, glucocorticoids, plasma exchange/IVIG, trigger treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent embolism/stroke, placental insufficiency, FGR, stillbirth; catastrophic APS → multiorgan failure

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid estrogen, stop smoking, optimize cardiovascular risks; plan perioperative/pregnancy anticoagulation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Inherited thrombophilia: primarily venous events, no antiphospholipid antibodies
Factor deficiency: prolonged aPTT corrects with mixing; usually bleeding phenotype

table.title: Classic obstetric clinical criteria: any one
rows: Premature birth from severe preeclampsia/placental insufficiency

antiphospholipid-syndrome.evidence: Anticoagulation checked 2026-10-30: [EULAR APS recommendations](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/11034817/); diagnostic patterns established teaching.

antipsychotics.name: Antipsychotics
antipsychotics.scope: First-generation vs second-generation, extrapyramidal symptoms (acute dystonia, akathisia, parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia), neuroleptic malignant syndrome, metabolic syndrome, hyperprolactinemia, QTc prolongation
antipsychotics.core: Dopamine-modulating drugs treat psychosis and mania; selection depends on motor, metabolic, endocrine, cardiovascular, and hematologic risks.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ Psychosis, mania, agitation; **SGA first-line**; **clozapine** if resistant or recurrent suicidality
FGA: mainly D2 antagonism; SGA: D2/5-HT2 effects, varying by agent
Quetiapine sedation → switch to aripiprazole; obesity → ziprasidone, not olanzapine/clozapine

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Nigrostriatal blockade → movement disorders; tuberoinfundibular blockade → prolactin elevation
Aripiprazole: partial D2 agonist; haloperidol high-potency FGA, chlorpromazine low-potency FGA
Chronic D2 blockade → receptor supersensitivity → tardive dyskinesia; can worsen after stopping

rows.label: Adverse
items: ★ Fever, **lead-pipe rigidity**, autonomic instability, high CK → NMS; stop drug, supportive ICU care
Severe NMS: dantrolene/bromocriptine; olanzapine/clozapine: weight gain, diabetes, dyslipidemia
Risperidone: ↑prolactin; ziprasidone: ↑QT; clozapine: neutropenia, myocarditis, ileus, seizures

rows.label: Avoid
items: Lewy body/Parkinson disease: severe sensitivity; specialist-selected quetiapine/clozapine if essential
Dementia: ↑mortality, falls; dangerous behavior after safer measures → low-dose **quetiapine**/risperidone, not benzodiazepines

rows.label: Interactions
items: Other QT-prolonging drugs, electrolyte depletion → torsades; sedatives/alcohol increase CNS depression
Metoclopramide, prochlorperazine block dopamine: same EPS, tardive dyskinesia, NMS; avoid after NMS

rows.label: Monitor
items: ★ Weight/BMI, BP, glucose/A1c, lipids; movement examinations; **ANC with clozapine**
ECG for cardiac/QT risks; prolactin when symptomatic; ask about bowel function
Clozapine + ANC <1000 → **hold clozapine**, not dose reduction; ANC 1000–1499 → continue, closer monitoring

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Anticholinergics worsen tardive dyskinesia**; valbenazine/deutetrabenazine are VMAT2 inhibitors
Akathisia can mimic worsening agitation; increasing antipsychotic dose can worsen it
Low-potency FGAs: more orthostasis/anticholinergic effects; high-potency FGAs: more EPS

table.title: Extrapyramidal syndromes
rows: Stop/switch culprit first; benztropine or amantadine

antipsychotics.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [FDA clozapine monitoring update](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-removes-risk-evaluation-and-mitigation-strategy-rems-program-antipsychotic-drug-clozapine); other effects established teaching.

appendicitis.name: Appendicitis
appendicitis.scope: Acute appendicitis, clinical presentation, pediatric and pregnancy considerations, imaging (ultrasound, CT), surgical management
appendicitis.core: Periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant, followed by anorexia and nausea, suggests appendiceal inflammation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Adolescents/young adults; luminal obstruction by lymphoid hyperplasia or fecalith
Older adults may have obstructing neoplasm; immunosuppression can blunt findings

rows.label: Clues
items: McBurney tenderness, guarding, fever; Rovsing, psoas, or obturator signs depend on position
★ **Diffuse peritonitis, toxicity, hypotension** → perforation/sepsis until proven otherwise
Young children: nonspecific symptoms and rapid progression; pregnancy: displaced appendix, less reliable examination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Luminal obstruction → distention, venous congestion, bacterial invasion → ischemia/perforation
Visceral midgut pain precedes focal parietal peritoneal irritation

rows.label: Dx
items: CBC, urinalysis, **pregnancy test** in reproductive-age patients; pyuria does not exclude appendicitis
★ Stable nonpregnant adult → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast** when diagnosis uncertain
★ Child/pregnancy → **ultrasound first**; nondiagnostic → MRI without gadolinium, or CT in nonpregnant child
Noncompressible enlarged appendix >6 mm with periappendiceal inflammation supports diagnosis
Clear peritonitis → surgical evaluation; do not delay necessary operation for repeated imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ NPO, **IV fluids, IV opioids, ceftriaxone + metronidazole**, surgical consultation; opioids do not obscure exam
Laparoscopic appendectomy definitive; do not withhold necessary surgery during pregnancy
Selected uncomplicated cases → antibiotics after shared decision; recurrence/failure higher, especially with appendicolith
Localized abscess/phlegmon in stable patient → antibiotics ± image-guided drainage; follow-up based on age/risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Perforation, abscess, peritonitis, sepsis, ileus
Postoperative wound infection, intra-abdominal collection, adhesional obstruction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG, adnexal findings
Ovarian torsion: sudden unilateral pelvic pain; gastroenteritis: diarrhea prominent before diffuse cramping
Mesenteric adenitis: viral prodrome, normal appendix on imaging

appendicitis.evidence: Not checked online; established general-surgery evaluation and treatment principles.

autoimmune-biliary-diseases.name: Autoimmune biliary diseases
autoimmune-biliary-diseases.scope: Primary sclerosing cholangitis, primary biliary cholangitis, bead-like strictures on MRCP, AMA, ursodeoxycholic acid
autoimmune-biliary-diseases.core: Chronic cholestasis with pruritus and fatigue suggests immune-mediated bile-duct disease; anatomy and serology distinguish the major types.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Coexisting autoimmune disease; family susceptibility
PSC strongly associated with ulcerative colitis, progresses despite colectomy; PBC usually middle-aged women

rows.label: Clues
items: Disproportionate ALP/GGT elevation; bilirubin may remain normal early
Excoriations, jaundice, hepatomegaly; xanthelasma and fat malabsorption with prolonged cholestasis
★ Fever, RUQ pain, new jaundice → **acute bacterial cholangitis**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Chronic duct injury → impaired bile flow, progressive fibrosis and biliary cirrhosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Cholestatic labs → **RUQ ultrasound** first to exclude mechanical obstruction
PBC usually diagnosed with cholestasis plus disease-specific antibodies; biopsy if atypical/seronegative
PSC with normal cholangiogram and persistent suspicion → biopsy for small-duct disease
New dominant/relevant stricture → ERCP with sampling for cholangiocarcinoma; not routine diagnostic ERCP

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Ursodeoxycholic acid** first-line PBC; inadequate response/intolerance → seladelpar or elafibranor
PSC: no established disease-modifying drug; avoid high-dose ursodeoxycholic acid
Bacterial cholangitis → antibiotics and biliary drainage; obstructive stricture → endoscopic intervention
Cholestyramine for itch; advanced decompensation or refractory symptoms → liver transplant
Obeticholic acid withdrawn in US 2025 → not a current second-line choice

rows.label: Complications
items: Portal hypertension, hepatic failure, fat-soluble vitamin deficiency, osteoporosis
PSC → cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder cancer, colorectal cancer with IBD

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Bone-density assessment, vitamin replacement when deficient; hepatitis A/B vaccination
PSC → colonoscopy for occult IBD and ongoing cancer surveillance; cirrhosis → HCC surveillance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Choledocholithiasis: discrete obstructing stone; IgG4 cholangitis: pancreatic disease, steroid responsiveness
Drug cholestasis: temporal drug exposure without characteristic chronic duct findings

benign-breast-conditions.name: Benign breast conditions
benign-breast-conditions.scope: Fibroadenoma, fibrocystic changes, intraductal papilloma, breast cyst, fat necrosis, galactocele, breast abscess
benign-breast-conditions.core: Breast symptoms require age-directed imaging and clinical–radiologic concordance; a benign-appearing examination alone cannot exclude malignancy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive hormonal cycling; milk stasis; breast trauma or prior surgery
Smoking predisposes to recurrent subareolar abscess
**Cracked, excoriated nipples** → main portal of entry for lactational mastitis

rows.label: Clues
items: Galactocele: cystic lactational/postlactational mass, no inflammation, varies with feeds; fat–fluid level on imaging
Mastitis: focal tender erythema, fever, no fluctuance; abscess adds **fluctuance**; often Staphylococcus aureus
★ Spontaneous unilateral **bloody single-duct discharge** → usually **papilloma**; exclude malignancy, persistent → surgical evaluation
Nonbloody discharge only on expression, normal exam → **physiologic**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hormone-responsive stromal/glandular tissue produces cyclic changes; duct obstruction causes retained secretions
Adipose injury causes inflammatory necrosis and calcification that can resemble cancer

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Palpable mass **<30 years → ultrasound**; ≥30 → diagnostic mammography with targeted ultrasound
Suspicious solid lesion or imaging–exam discordance → **core needle biopsy**
Simple cyst: anechoic, thin-walled, posterior enhancement; no solid component
Nonlactational abscess or persistent inflammation after antibiotics → exclude underlying carcinoma
Cyclic bilateral nodularity, no dominant mass → **reexamine after menses**, before imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Painful simple cyst → aspiration; nonbloody fluid + full collapse → benign; bloody fluid/residual mass → **biopsy**
Fibroadenoma → observe when concordant; excise if rapidly enlarging, large or symptomatic
Breast pain, no mass, young, normal exam → **reassurance**; fibrocystic pain → supportive bra, topical/oral NSAID
★ Mastitis → **dicloxacillin/cephalexin**, keep breastfeeding/pumping; abscess → add needle/incision drainage; MRSA → clindamycin
Tender lactating lump, no erythema/fever → **warm compresses**, keep nursing; persistent galactocele → aspiration

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent periductal abscess → fistula; incomplete drainage → persistent infection
Proliferative lesions with atypia increase future cancer risk; simple cysts do not

rows.label: Prevention
items: Effective breast emptying during lactation; smoking cessation for recurrent periductal disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cancer: irregular fixed mass, retraction or suspicious nodes
Phyllodes: rapidly enlarging fibroepithelial mass requiring excision

table.title: Common benign findings
rows: Early postpartum; bilateral tense tender breasts, low fever

benign-breast-conditions.evidence: Not checked online; established breast diagnostic principles.

bone-tumors.name: Bone tumors
bone-tumors.scope: Osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, chondrosarcoma, giant cell tumor of bone, osteochondroma, osteoid osteoma, bone metastases, biopsy
bone-tumors.core: Persistent focal bone pain, a growing mass, or a destructive radiographic lesion requires planned evaluation before biopsy or fixation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Osteosarcoma: adolescence, hereditary retinoblastoma (RB1), prior radiation, Paget disease; chondrosarcoma: older adults
Hereditary multiple exostoses predispose to osteochondromas; most adult malignant bone lesions are metastases

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Night/rest pain**, enlarging mass, constitutional symptoms or pathologic fracture → concerning lesion
Osteoid osteoma: nocturnal pain relieved by NSAIDs; small cortical nidus
Osteochondroma: painless metaphyseal exostosis with medullary continuity; new growth after maturity concerning
Known cancer + constant back pain, vertebral point tenderness → **spinal metastasis**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tumor lineage determines osteoid, cartilage or primitive-cell production; aggressive growth destroys cortex
Giant cell tumor: neoplastic stromal cells recruit osteoclast-like giant cells, causing locally aggressive osteolysis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Plain radiographs first**; assess location, margins, periosteal reaction and matrix
Aggressive lesion → MRI entire involved bone/adjacent joint; chest CT for lung metastases
★ **Orthopedic oncology plans biopsy tract**; core biopsy after imaging, before definitive treatment
CBC, ESR/CRP if infection suspected; normal labs do not exclude malignancy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Osteosarcoma → **neoadjuvant chemotherapy + wide resection**, then postoperative chemotherapy
Ewing → systemic chemotherapy plus surgery and/or radiation
Chondrosarcoma → wide surgical excision; conventional tumors relatively chemo/radioresistant
Symptomatic osteoid osteoma → radiofrequency ablation; asymptomatic osteochondroma → observation
Giant cell tumor → curettage/reconstruction; selected unresectable lesions → denosumab

rows.label: Complications
items: Pathologic fracture, neurovascular compromise, pulmonary metastases; limb surgery and chemotherapy morbidity
Mandible metastasis → mental nerve anesthesia (**numb chin**)

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteomyelitis: infection markers, cultures; may closely resemble Ewing
Bone metastases: older adult, multiple lesions; myeloma: anemia, monoclonal protein
Unicameral bone cyst: child, lucent expansile proximal humerus lesion; pathologic fracture after minor trauma

bone-tumors.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

bowel-obstruction.name: Bowel obstruction
bowel-obstruction.scope: Small bowel obstruction (adhesions, hernia), large bowel obstruction (volvulus, malignancy), paralytic ileus, NG decompression, surgical management
bowel-obstruction.core: Colicky abdominal pain, vomiting, distention, and obstipation suggest mechanical obstruction; constant pain or systemic toxicity raises concern for strangulation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior abdominal surgery (**adhesions**, leading cause), incarcerated hernia, Crohn strictures → small-bowel obstruction
Colorectal malignancy, chronic constipation, institutionalization → large-bowel obstruction or sigmoid volvulus
Recent surgery, opioids, hypokalemia, severe systemic illness → ileus

rows.label: Clues
items: Early high-pitched sounds may become absent; proximal obstruction causes earlier vomiting, distal disease greater distention
★ **Peritonitis, fever, tachycardia, rising lactate**, or continuous severe pain → ischemia/perforation
Complete → **obstipation**, no flatus; partial may still pass stool/diarrhea, not excluding obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Luminal blockage → upstream dilation, third spacing; closed loop compromises venous then arterial supply
Adynamic ileus reflects impaired motility without an anatomic transition point

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast** defines transition point, cause, and ischemic signs
CBC, electrolytes, creatinine, lactate; normal lactate cannot exclude early ischemia
Radiograph may show dilated loops/air-fluid levels, no rectal gas; CT more definitive if diagnosis uncertain
★ Massive colonic distention + **coffee-bean (inverted-U) loop** on radiograph → sigmoid volvulus
Pregnancy: plain radiograph acceptable first (minimal fetal dose); MRI if unclear; do not delay

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **NPO, IV isotonic fluids, electrolyte correction**; NG decompression for significant vomiting/distention
★ Strangulation, perforation, closed loop, or incarcerated hernia → **urgent surgery** + ceftriaxone/metronidazole
Uncomplicated adhesive SBO → surgical observation, serial examination; water-soluble contrast helps predict resolution
Failure to improve during a short monitored trial, commonly up to 72 h → operation
Ileus → correct trigger, reduce opioids, mobilize; no operation solely for absent sounds

rows.label: Complications
items: Dehydration, AKI, hypokalemic alkalosis; bowel necrosis, perforation, sepsis
Recurrent adhesions; short-bowel syndrome after extensive resection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early postoperative ambulation, opioid-sparing analgesia, electrolyte correction; elective repair of symptomatic hernias

rows.label: Mimics
items: Gastroenteritis: prominent diarrhea, no focal transition point
Mesenteric ischemia: pain out of proportion before peritoneal signs
Ileus: hypoactive/absent sounds, gas throughout bowel including rectum
Diabetic autonomic neuropathy: dysmotility, dilated loops without transition point

table.title: Large-bowel branches
rows: Sigmoidoscopic detorsion, rectal tube → same-admission resection
