bowel-obstruction.evidence: Not checked online; established acute surgical management principles.

breast-neoplasia.name: Breast neoplasia
breast-neoplasia.scope: Ductal carcinoma in situ, invasive ductal and lobular carcinoma, receptor status (ER, PR, HER2), metastatic disease (bone, visceral), surgical management, endocrine and chemotherapy
breast-neoplasia.core: A suspicious breast lesion requires core biopsy, assessment of invasion and ER/PR/HER2 status to guide local and systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, BRCA-related syndromes, close-relative family history (distant relative adds little), prior chest irradiation
**Combined estrogen-progestin therapy**, prolonged estrogen, postmenopausal obesity, alcohol; atypical proliferative lesions

rows.label: Clues
items: Painless hard irregular mass, skin/nipple retraction, unilateral bloody discharge or axillary node
★ Peau d’orange, diffuse erythema and edema → **inflammatory breast cancer**, even without discrete mass
Persistent unilateral eczematous nipple lesion → Paget disease; **full-thickness biopsy**, investigate underlying carcinoma

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Invasion through basement membrane enables lymphatic/hematogenous metastasis
ER/PR signaling and HER2 amplification create actionable tumor drivers; triple-negative tumors lack these targets

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Diagnostic mammography + targeted ultrasound** → core biopsy of suspicious lesion; pregnancy → **ultrasound first**
Pathology: invasion, grade, **ER/PR/HER2**; assess regional nodes clinically and with targeted imaging
Clinically node-negative invasive disease, including microinvasion ≤1 mm → sentinel node biopsy during definitive surgery
Distant staging scans for advanced disease or suspicious symptoms; not every small asymptomatic cancer
Axillary node adenocarcinoma, normal mammogram → occult breast primary; breast MRI

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early: lumpectomy + radiation or mastectomy; **positive margins → reexcision** before adjuvant therapy
ER-positive → tamoxifen or postmenopausal aromatase inhibitor; chemotherapy based on stage/biology
★ HER2-positive → **trastuzumab-based** treatment, monitor LVEF; triple-negative → chemotherapy ± pembrolizumab if higher-risk
Locally advanced → neoadjuvant treatment, then surgery/radiation; large residual + palpable nodes → **mastectomy + axillary dissection**
Bone metastases → **zoledronate/denosumab**; systemic treatment by receptors, chemotherapy for visceral crisis

rows.label: Complications
items: Metastases to bone (often **mixed lytic–blastic**), lung, liver, brain; surgery/radiation → lymphedema
Tamoxifen → VTE/endometrial cancer; aromatase inhibitors → bone loss; trastuzumab → cardiomyopathy
Prior cancer + severe hypercalcemia, lytic lesions → recurrence; thiazide/calcium supplements cause only mild elevation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Age/risk-based screening, genetic counseling for suggestive pedigree; selected high-risk patients → chemoprevention
BRCA-related very high risk → discuss risk-reducing surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mastitis: lactation-associated tenderness/fever, improves with antibiotics
Fat necrosis: trauma/surgery history; biopsy if discordant imaging

table.title: Histologic distinctions
rows: Bilateral risk marker; discohesive lobular cells
Surveillance/risk reduction if concordant; later cancer usually ductal

breast-neoplasia.evidence: Not checked online; established breast-oncology management principles.

bronchiectasis.name: Bronchiectasis
bronchiectasis.scope: Cystic fibrosis, post-infectious, high-resolution CT, airway clearance, pseudomonas colonization, acute exacerbation
bronchiectasis.core: Chronic productive cough with recurrent respiratory infections and permanently dilated bronchi on high-resolution CT.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cystic fibrosis, prior severe pneumonia/TB, primary ciliary dyskinesia, aspiration, immunodeficiency
ABPA, rheumatoid arthritis, obstructing endobronchial lesion; some cases remain idiopathic

rows.label: Clues
items: Copious purulent sputum, coarse crackles, recurrent focal infections, hemoptysis, sometimes clubbing
Exacerbation: increased sputum volume/purulence, cough, dyspnea, fatigue; hypoxemia or sepsis → severe disease
Early lifelong infections, sinusitis, infertility, or situs inversus suggest impaired ciliary clearance
Child: chronic cough refractory to bronchodilators, steroids, antibiotics + persistent focal collapse/consolidation → localized bronchiectasis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired mucus clearance → persistent infection and neutrophilic inflammation → irreversible airway wall destruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **High-resolution chest CT**: signet-ring bronchi, absent tapering, airways visible near pleura, cystic spaces ± air-fluid levels
Sputum bacterial and mycobacterial cultures; spirometry measures associated airflow limitation
Quantitative immunoglobulins; total IgE/Aspergillus testing for ABPA; sweat chloride if CF suspected
Localized disease → bronchoscopy for tumor/foreign body; diffuse disease → investigate systemic cause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Daily **airway clearance**, exercise; bronchodilator for obstruction; no routine inhaled steroids or non-CF dornase alfa
★ Exacerbation → sputum culture then antibiotics guided by prior isolates; often **14 days**
Pseudomonas susceptible → ciprofloxacin; severe infection → IV cefepime or piperacillin-tazobactam
★ ≥2 yearly or ≥1 severe exacerbation → azithromycin after NTM exclusion; chronic Pseudomonas → inhaled tobramycin
Massive hemoptysis → airway protection and bronchial artery embolization; focal refractory disease → resection evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic Pseudomonas colonization, resistant infection, respiratory failure, pulmonary hypertension
Antibiotic toxicity/resistance; macrolides can cause QT prolongation and hearing impairment

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, influenza/pneumococcal vaccination, aspiration management, treatment of underlying immunodeficiency
New Pseudomonas isolation → specialist eradication regimen, often ciprofloxacin followed by inhaled antibiotic

rows.label: Mimics
items: Chronic bronchitis: smoking-related sputum without characteristic bronchial dilation
Lung abscess: solitary cavity with air-fluid level; no lifelong productive cough
Pulmonary TB: constitutional illness and compatible imaging; mycobacterial testing confirms

burn-injuries.name: Burn injuries
burn-injuries.scope: Superficial, partial-thickness, full-thickness burns, total body surface area (Rule of Nines), fluid resuscitation (Parkland), smoke inhalation and airway edema, carbon monoxide/cyanide toxicity
burn-injuries.core: Burn severity depends on depth, affected surface area, location, and inhalation injury; airway threats and hypovolemia take priority over wound care.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Flames/scalds, electricity, chemicals; closed-space fires increase toxic inhalation risk
Older adults, children, impaired mobility/sensation; inconsistent injury history raises abuse concern

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Hoarseness, stridor, oropharyngeal edema, soot** → threatened airway; skin burns may appear minor
CO: headache, confusion, syncope despite normal pulse oximetry
Cyanide: enclosed-fire exposure with cardiovascular collapse and severe lactic acidosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Capillary leak → intravascular depletion and edema; swelling progresses after initial presentation
CO impairs oxygen transport; cyanide blocks mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TBSA excludes superficial burns**; adult Rule of Nines: head/each arm 9%, each leg 18%
Anterior/posterior trunk 18% each, perineum 1%; own palm including fingers ≈1%; children → Lund-Browder
★ Inhalation/toxin concern → **ABG with co-oximetry**, lactate; normal PaO2 does not exclude CO
Electrical burn → ECG, CK, urinalysis for rhabdomyolysis; small surface injury may hide deep damage

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Airway threat → **intubate**; burn center: full-thickness, ≥10% partial, critical-site, inhalation/electrical/chemical
CO → 100% oxygen; severe neurologic/cardiac toxicity or pregnancy → consider hyperbaric oxygen; cyanide → hydroxocobalamin
Lactated Ringer, no early colloid: **Parkland = 4 mL × kg × %TBSA** over 24 hours
Half by 8 hours from injury, remainder over 16; ABA now starts adults at 2 mL/kg/%TBSA

rows.label: Complications
items: Shock, AKI, infection, contractures, compartment syndrome; overresuscitation worsens edema
Restrictive chest/limb eschar → escharotomy; true compartment syndrome → fasciotomy
Prognosis: **inhalation injury** often raises mortality more than moderate TBSA or comorbidities

rows.label: Prevention
items: Titrate fluids to urine output ≥0.5 mL/kg/hour in adults; formula only starting estimate
Small burn: cleaning, **bacitracin**, nonadherent dressing, tetanus, analgesia, no IV bolus; no routine systemic antibiotics
★ **Stop exposure, remove jewelry, cool water**, prevent hypothermia; no ice
Smoke/CO detectors, safe water temperature, fire escape plan; early rehabilitation and range of motion

rows.label: Mimics
items: SJS/TEN: medication exposure, mucosal erosions, widespread epidermal detachment
Cellulitis: spreading warmth/erythema without immediate thermal exposure

table.title: Depth
rows: Moist blisters, brisk blanching, very painful

burn-injuries.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ABA burn resuscitation guideline 2024](https://academic.oup.com/jbcr/article/45/3/565/7458089); classic Parkland contrasted with current initial estimate.

bursitis.name: Bursitis
bursitis.scope: Prepatellar bursitis (housemaid knee), olecranon bursitis (student elbow), greater trochanteric pain syndrome, septic vs aseptic bursitis, bursal fluid aspiration, compressive wraps, antibiotics
bursitis.core: Focal periarticular swelling or tenderness with relatively preserved passive joint motion suggests bursal rather than intra-articular disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Repetitive focal pressure, local trauma; gout and rheumatoid arthritis
Skin breaks, diabetes, immunosuppression predispose to infection, usually S. aureus

rows.label: Clues
items: Localized fluctuant superficial swelling; joint range usually maintained, with discomfort from adjacent compression
★ **Warmth, erythema, fever, or skin wound** raises concern for septic bursitis; absent fever insufficiently reassuring
Aseptic disease generally lacks systemic illness; repetitive minor trauma can produce relatively painless swelling

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Bursal irritation → synovial inflammation and fluid accumulation; superficial bursae readily inoculated through skin
Greater trochanteric pain often reflects gluteal tendinopathy with or without associated bursal inflammation

rows.label: Dx
items: Clinical diagnosis for typical aseptic cases; ultrasound if uncertain whether bursal collection or joint effusion
★ Suspected infection or crystal disease → **bursal aspiration** for cell count, Gram stain, culture, crystals
Crystals do not exclude concurrent infection; aspirate through uninfected skin when feasible
Severe pain with passive motion → evaluate joint by arthrocentesis, not bursal sampling alone

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Aseptic superficial disease → **rest, ice, NSAIDs, compression**, pressure avoidance
Persistent aseptic symptoms → selected steroid injection after infection excluded; avoid routine superficial injections
★ Septic disease → **cephalexin/dicloxacillin**; MRSA risk → TMP-SMX or doxycycline; severe/systemic → IV vancomycin
Drain persistent infected collections; recurrent/refractory disease may need bursectomy
Trochanteric pain → hip abductor strengthening and physical rehabilitation; injection for persistent focal symptoms

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic recurrence, reduced function; septic disease → cellulitis or bacteremia
Aspiration/injection → iatrogenic infection; corticosteroid injection → skin atrophy, tendon injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Knee/elbow padding, ergonomic changes, gradual activity increases; treat skin wounds promptly
Avoid repeated unnecessary aspiration of uncomplicated aseptic superficial swelling

rows.label: Mimics
items: Septic arthritis: marked restriction and pain throughout passive movement
Cellulitis: diffuse skin inflammation without discrete bursal collection
Tendinopathy: pain with resisted tendon loading rather than fluctuant swelling

bursitis.evidence: Not checked online; established bursal evaluation and treatment.

candidiasis.name: Candidiasis
candidiasis.scope: Oropharyngeal candidiasis (thrush), diaper candidiasis, intertrigo, vulvovaginal candidiasis, cell-mediated vs neutrophil immunity, nystatin, fluconazole
candidiasis.core: Opportunistic yeast overgrowth on mucosa or moist skin; distribution and host immune defects determine evaluation and antifungal route.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent antibiotics, diabetes, pregnancy, inhaled/systemic steroids, HIV; infants, dentures, skin occlusion
Neutropenia, central venous catheters, parenteral nutrition → invasive infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Odynophagia or dysphagia with immunosuppression** → esophageal involvement, even without visible oral lesions
Persistent/recurrent thrush outside infancy → evaluate HIV, diabetes, or other immune defects
Sepsis in neutropenic or catheterized host → consider candidemia rather than isolated superficial disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **T-cell/IL-17 dysfunction → mucocutaneous disease; neutrophil defects → invasive candidiasis**
Candida albicans: budding yeast and pseudohyphae; overgrowth of endogenous flora rather than routine sexual transmission

rows.label: Dx
items: Typical oral/cutaneous disease → clinical diagnosis; uncertain lesions → KOH microscopy
★ Vaginal symptoms → wet mount/KOH; **pH usually <4.5**; negative microscopy with suspicion → culture
Complicated/recurrent vaginitis → culture/speciation; asymptomatic colonization alone needs no treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: Esophageal disease → **systemic fluconazole 14–21 days**; refractory symptoms → endoscopy with biopsy
★ Pregnancy → **7-day intravaginal clotrimazole**; systemic triazoles contraindicated
Recurrent vaginitis ≥3 episodes/year → extended induction then weekly fluconazole for 6 months
Candidemia → IV micafungin and blood cultures; investigate/remove infected catheter

rows.label: Complications
items: Poor oral intake, painful fissures, recurrent vaginitis; invasive disease → endophthalmitis, endocarditis, organ abscesses
Azoles: hepatotoxicity, QT prolongation, CYP interactions

rows.label: Prevention
items: Rinse mouth after inhaled steroids; clean dentures, keep folds dry, change wet diapers promptly
Optimize glucose control and HIV ART; routine partner treatment unnecessary for uncomplicated vaginitis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Leukoplakia/oral hairy leukoplakia: white plaques do not scrape off
Irritant diaper dermatitis: spares folds; bacterial vaginosis: fishy odor, elevated vaginal pH

table.title: Superficial presentations
rows: Beefy erythema, satellite pustules; folds involved
Topical azole or single-dose oral fluconazole

cardiomyopathies.name: Cardiomyopathies
cardiomyopathies.scope: Dilated cardiomyopathy, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, restrictive cardiomyopathy, stress (Takotsubo) cardiomyopathy, viral myocarditis, diagnostic evaluation, management
cardiomyopathies.core: Myocardial disease causes pump failure, impaired filling, dynamic obstruction, or arrhythmias; echocardiography defines the phenotype.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dilated: familial disease, alcohol, anthracyclines, peripartum state, **viral myocarditis**
Hypertrophic: autosomal dominant sarcomeric variants; restrictive: amyloid, hemochromatosis, radiation
Takotsubo: emotional/physical stress; myocarditis: recent viral illness, immune checkpoint inhibitors

rows.label: Clues
items: Exertional dyspnea, edema, elevated JVP; **displaced PMI**, S3 → dilated LV; syncope/ventricular arrhythmia signals danger
★ Obstructive HCM murmur **↑Valsalva/standing**, ↓squatting/handgrip; exertional presyncope
Myocarditis: chest discomfort, tachycardia disproportionate to fever, acute heart failure

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Sarcomere dysfunction or myocardial injury → remodeling; infiltration → reduced ventricular compliance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG, troponin, BNP → transthoracic echo**; assess coronary ischemia when suspected
Cardiac MRI: inflammation, scar, infiltrative patterns; iron studies or monoclonal protein testing when relevant
Endomyocardial biopsy: selected fulminant unexplained failure, malignant arrhythmias, suspected giant-cell myocarditis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ HFrEF: **ARNI, evidence-based beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2 inhibitor**; loop diuretic for congestion
Obstructive HCM: nonvasodilating beta-blocker (propranolol, metoprolol); alternative verapamil/diltiazem
Refractory obstruction → myosin inhibitor, disopyramide, or septal reduction; avoid dehydration and vasodilators
Restrictive disease: cautious diuresis, treat cause; Takotsubo: supportive care after excluding ACS
Myocarditis with shock → ICU, circulatory support; no routine antiviral or immunosuppression

rows.label: Complications
items: Sudden cardiac death, atrial fibrillation, thromboembolism; advanced failure → transplantation evaluation
★ HCM with cardiac arrest or major sudden-death risk → **ICD** consideration

rows.label: Prevention
items: Screen first-degree relatives in inherited disease; avoid cardiotoxins
Myocarditis: restrict strenuous exercise until clinical recovery and reassessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ischemic cardiomyopathy: obstructive coronary disease explains dysfunction
Constrictive pericarditis: pericardial disease, respiratory ventricular interdependence
Aortic stenosis: murmur softer with standing/Valsalva, unlike obstructive HCM

table.title: Echo phenotype
rows: Enlarged ventricles, diffuse hypokinesia, reduced EF
Transient apical ballooning beyond coronary territory

cardiomyopathies.evidence: HCM checked 2026-10-30: [AHA/ACC 2024](https://www.acc.org/latest-in-cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2024/05/06/15/12/2024-hypertrophic-cardiomyopathy-gl); other content established teaching.

cerebellar-disorders.name: Cerebellar disorders
cerebellar-disorders.scope: Acute cerebellar ataxia, cerebellar signs, toxic cerebellar degeneration (cytarabine, phenytoin, alcohol), paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration, Friedreich ataxia, imaging
cerebellar-disorders.core: Dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia, intention tremor, and a broad-based gait localize dysfunction to the cerebellum or its connections.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent viral infection in children; chronic alcohol exposure or malnutrition
Phenytoin toxicity, high-dose cytarabine, occult malignancy; inherited recessive disease

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Abrupt ataxia with **headache, vomiting, focal deficits** → posterior circulation emergency
Midline lesions: truncal instability; hemispheric lesions: ipsilateral limb incoordination
Scanning dysarthria, gaze-evoked nystagmus; imbalance persists with eyes open

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired timing and error correction; lateral cerebellum coordinates ipsilateral extremities
Alcohol predominantly damages anterior vermis; paraneoplastic disease causes immune-mediated Purkinje cell loss

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Acute focal or persistent unexplained ataxia → **brain MRI**, especially posterior fossa
Acute vomiting, suspected hemorrhage/mass → **CT first**; negative CT does not exclude cerebellar infarction
Check glucose, toxic exposures, phenytoin level; consider B12, thyroid testing
Subacute progressive course → paraneoplastic antibodies and malignancy search; hereditary pattern → genetic testing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected nutritional deficiency → **IV thiamine** promptly; give glucose immediately if hypoglycemic
★ Toxic **cytarabine/phenytoin** → stop culprit; cytarabine toxicity requires urgent oncology review
Postinfectious acute cerebellar ataxia: observation/support after exclusion of dangerous causes
Paraneoplastic syndrome: treat tumor, consider immunotherapy; rehabilitation for all persistent deficits

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, aspiration; cerebellar infarction/edema → obstructive hydrocephalus and herniation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Alcohol cessation, nutritional repletion; review anticonvulsant levels and interactions

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sensory ataxia: impaired proprioception, marked worsening with eye closure
Vestibular disease: vertigo predominates, no limb dysmetria

table.title: Progressive syndromes
rows: GAA expansion; areflexia, extensor plantars, cardiomyopathy
Weeks–months; breast/ovarian or small-cell lung cancer

cerebellar-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established neurologic localization and toxicology teaching.

cervical-neoplasia.name: Cervical neoplasia
cervical-neoplasia.scope: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, invasive cervical cancer, squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, colposcopy
cervical-neoplasia.core: Persistent high-risk HPV drives cervical precancer and cancer; abnormal screening needs risk-based evaluation, while visible symptomatic lesions require biopsy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HPV 16/18 persistence, smoking, HIV/immunosuppression, limited screening access

rows.label: Clues
items: CIN usually asymptomatic; invasive disease → postcoital/intermenstrual bleeding, watery discharge
Friable cervical mass, pelvic pain; hydronephrosis or leg edema suggests advanced spread

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Viral E6 degrades p53; E7 inactivates Rb → transformation-zone dysplasia
Squamous carcinoma most common; adenocarcinoma arises in endocervical glands

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Visible lesion → biopsy**, regardless of prior normal Pap/HPV result
★ HPV 16/18 positivity, ASC-H or AGC → **colposcopy**, even with otherwise reassuring screening
AGC → endocervical sampling; add endometrial biopsy at ≥35 or with endometrial risk factors
Colposcopy-directed biopsy diagnoses CIN; invasive cancer → pelvic examination, MRI/PET-CT for extent
Pregnancy → risk-based colposcopy; no endocervical curettage or expedited excision

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ CIN 3 → **cone/LEEP** outside pregnancy; unseen SCJ → no ablation; fertility concerns → observe CIN 2
CIN 1 → observation; select nonpregnant patients ≥25 with very high risk → expedited excision
AIS → diagnostic excision; hysterectomy after childbearing if margins adequately assessed
Microinvasive → conization if preserving fertility, else **simple hysterectomy**; other early invasive → radical hysterectomy
Locally advanced → cisplatin-based chemoradiation plus brachytherapy

rows.label: Complications
items: Ureteral obstruction, fistulas, metastases; cervical excision increases subsequent preterm-birth risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **HPV vaccination** plus age-based screening; vaccination does not eliminate screening
After treated CIN 2/3/AIS: initial intensive HPV surveillance, then every 3 years for ≥25 years

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervicitis: mucopurulent discharge and positive STI testing
Endometrial cancer: uterine-source bleeding; benign ectropion: smooth eversion without destructive lesion

table.title: Histologic grade
rows: More than two-thirds; basement membrane intact

child-growth-and-development.name: Child growth and development
child-growth-and-development.scope: Normal growth velocity, weight doubling and tripling milestones, WHO/CDC growth chart interpretation, developmental surveillance, normal toddler behavioral variants (head banging, temper tantrums)
child-growth-and-development.core: Interpret serial growth and developmental progress against age, family pattern, and corrected gestational age; a trajectory matters more than one percentile.

rows.label: Definition
items: Weight doubles by 4–6 months, triples by 12 months, quadruples near 24 months
Length increases about 25 cm during year 1; prepubertal height velocity about 5–6 cm/year
★ **WHO charts before 2 years; CDC charts from 2 years** in US practice

rows.label: Interpret
items: Nutrition failure: weight falls first; endocrine disease: height slows with preserved/increased weight
★ Falling **2 major percentile channels**, well child → **diet diary, calorie counts** before labs
Correct prematurity through about 2 years; track infant head circumference

rows.label: Use when
items: Developmental surveillance every visit; standardized general screens at 9, 18, and 30 months
★ **Regression/missed milestones → early intervention**; language delay → **audiometry** before speech testing
BMI-for-age from 2 years; weight-for-length younger; consider parental heights and pubertal timing

rows.label: Compare
items: Tantrums, picky eating, bedtime separation distress → reassure, routines, calm limits; no sedatives
Head banging at sleep onset or frustration, normal development → self-soothing; assess injuries
Preschool restlessness, good function → no stimulants; overwhelmed parent → **parenting classes**

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **One percentile cannot diagnose disease**; stable tracking + normal exam → reassure
Persistent skill loss needs evaluation; never wait for school failure
Short parents, normal bone age → familial; average parents, delayed puberty → **constitutional delay**

rows.label: Adolescence
items: ★ Moodiness, privacy, family detachment, rule-questioning, late bedtimes, good function → reassure, educate parents
Parental-pressure conflict, occasional experimentation, no impairment → not ODD, substance use disorder
Weight worry, stable percentile, normal BMI, regular menses → normal; not eating disorder

table.title: Normal by age
rows: Holds head up; not yet reaching
Sits unsupported; bangs blocks, self-feeds finger foods
Walks; scribbles; non-walker at 14 months normal
Balances on one foot; copies circle
Same-sex parent preference; involve other parent otherwise

child-growth-and-development.evidence: Checked screening ages 2026-10-30: [AAP surveillance/screening](https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/developmental-surveillance-and-screening-patient-care/); growth facts established pediatric teaching.

chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.name: Chromosomal and genetic disorders
chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.scope: Down syndrome (trisomy 21), Turner syndrome (45,X0), Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY), Fragile X syndrome (FMR1 trinucleotide repeat), Prader-Willi and Angelman syndromes, DiGeorge syndrome (22q11 deletion)
chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.core: Recognize syndromic combinations of growth, cognition, gonadal function, dysmorphism, and congenital malformations; confirm with the correct genetic test.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Advanced maternal age: meiotic nondisjunction; balanced parental translocation: recurrent aneuploid pregnancy
Family expansion history: repeat disorders; microdeletions often de novo

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Down** (trisomy 21): hypotonia, upslanting fissures, epicanthal folds, macroglossia, single palmar crease, AV septal defect
DiGeorge: conotruncal defect, cleft palate, absent thymus, hypocalcemic tetany
Turner: newborn hand/foot lymphedema, redundant nuchal skin; later nevi
**Williams** (7q11.23 deletion): overfriendly, elfin facies, hyperacusis, intellectual disability, supravalvular stenosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **Genomic imprinting**: parent-specific expression; deletion or uniparental disomy can disrupt the active copy
22q11 deletion disrupts pharyngeal pouch development → T-cell deficiency and hypoparathyroidism

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected Down, Turner, Klinefelter → **karyotype**; prenatal screening alone never establishes diagnosis
Microarray: microdeletion; targeted repeat analysis: fragile X; methylation testing: imprinting disorders
Down: assess heart, hearing, vision, thyroid; DiGeorge: calcium and lymphocyte subsets

rows.label: Tx
items: Early developmental services, speech support; repair congenital defects
Turner: growth hormone then estrogen/progestin; Klinefelter: testosterone after endocrine assessment
Prader-Willi: supervised food access; Angelman: seizure management; DiGeorge: calcium and infection management

rows.label: Complications
items: Down: duodenal atresia (double bubble), leukemia, early Alzheimer disease, atlantoaxial instability
Turner: coarctation, bicuspid valve, aortic dissection; Klinefelter: infertility, breast cancer
Prader-Willi: severe obesity; DiGeorge: severe infections and later psychiatric disease

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Genetic counseling**: recurrence depends on nondisjunction, translocation, imprinting mechanism, or repeat expansion
Avoid live vaccines with severe T-cell deficiency; use irradiated blood for profound immunodeficiency

rows.label: Mimics
items: Noonan syndrome: Turner-like habitus, normal chromosomes; either sex, pulmonic stenosis
Congenital hypothyroidism: hypotonia and delayed development; abnormal newborn thyroid screen
Constitutional delay: delayed bone age; no edema or nevi
Rett: girls with regression; MECP2 variant

table.title: Distinctive genotype–phenotype pairs
rows: Short female, webbed neck, streak ovaries, primary amenorrhea
Tall male, small firm testes, gynecomastia, high FSH/LH
FMR1 CGG expansion at X fragile site; silencing
Long face, large ears, macroorchidism, autism-like behavior
IUGR, clenched overlapping fingers, prominent occiput, micrognathia, VSD

chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established genetics teaching.

cirrhosis-and-portal-hypertension.name: Cirrhosis and portal hypertension
cirrhosis-and-portal-hypertension.scope: Ascites, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, hepatic encephalopathy, esophageal varices, hepatorenal syndrome, hepatocellular carcinoma screening
cirrhosis-and-portal-hypertension.core: Cirrhosis produces portal hypertension and synthetic failure; new ascites, bleeding, confusion or kidney injury signals decompensation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Alcohol, chronic HBV/HCV, metabolic steatotic liver disease; autoimmune/cholestatic disorders

rows.label: Clues
items: Splenomegaly, thrombocytopenia, spider angiomas, jaundice, muscle wasting
Encephalopathy: **asterixis**; triggers GI bleeding, infection, constipation, sedatives, hypokalemia, protein load
SBP may present only with subtle confusion or renal deterioration; fever/pain can be absent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fibrosis raises intrahepatic resistance; splanchnic vasodilation lowers effective arterial volume
Portal collaterals bleed; impaired toxin clearance causes neuropsychiatric dysfunction
SBP: **intestinal bacterial translocation** into ascitic fluid

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ New/worsening or hospitalized ascites → **diagnostic paracentesis**; PMN **≥250/µL** → treat SBP
SAAG ≥1.1 g/dL supports portal hypertension; send ascitic culture in bedside blood-culture bottles
HRS-AKI: exclude shock, nephrotoxins, obstruction and structural injury; assess volume response
MELD-Na/MELD 3.0 guides prognosis/transplant assessment
Encephalopathy clinical: **ammonia** not diagnostic; older exam questions may expect serum ammonia after normal head CT

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Variceal bleed → resuscitate, **octreotide + ceftriaxone**, urgent endoscopic banding; refractory → TIPS
Ascites → sodium restriction, spironolactone ± furosemide; tense ascites → paracentesis, albumin if >5 L
★ SBP → **ceftriaxone**, albumin for high-risk renal/liver dysfunction; reassess response
Encephalopathy → lactulose to 2–3 soft stools/day, rifaximin (add for recurrence); correct trigger; no sedatives
HRS → stop diuretics/nephrotoxins, **terlipressin + albumin** after volume assessment; monitor hypoxia; transplant evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: HCC, recurrent infection, malnutrition, hepatopulmonary syndrome; TIPS can worsen encephalopathy
Avoid NSAIDs, sedatives and unnecessary fluid loading; INR alone poorly predicts procedural bleeding

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Ultrasound + AFP every 6 months** for HCC surveillance in eligible cirrhosis
Carvedilol for clinically significant portal hypertension when tolerated; banding if indicated and beta blocker unsuitable
After SBP → antibiotic prophylaxis; alcohol abstinence, hepatitis vaccines, adequate protein intake

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cardiac ascites: high SAAG with ascitic protein ≥2.5 g/dL
Malignant/TB ascites: usually low SAAG

congenital-heart-disease.name: Congenital heart disease
congenital-heart-disease.scope: Cyanotic heart disease (5 Ts: Tetralogy of Fallot, TGA, truncus, tricuspid atresia, TAPVR), acyanotic heart disease (VSD, ASD, PDA, coarctation of aorta), hyperoxia test, prostaglandin E1
congenital-heart-disease.core: Neonatal cyanosis or shock as the ductus closes demands urgent assessment for duct-dependent congenital heart disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Maternal diabetes, congenital rubella, family history; Down syndrome → AV septal defects
Prematurity → PDA; Turner syndrome → coarctation

rows.label: Clues
items: Poor feeding, diaphoresis, tachypnea, hepatomegaly → infant heart failure
VSD: harsh holosystolic lower-left sternal murmur; ASD: **fixed split S2**, pulmonic flow murmur, RV volume overload
PDA: continuous machinery murmur, bounding pulses; coarctation: weak femoral pulses, arm–leg BP gradient
Central cyanosis: blue lips/tongue, warm extremities → **low arterial saturation**; peripheral: cold extremities

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Left-to-right shunts (VSD, ASD, extracardiac PDA) increase pulmonary flow; remodeling can reverse flow → Eisenmenger syndrome
Duct-dependent lesions require pulmonary/systemic flow or mixing through fetal communications
High neonatal PVR limits VSD shunt → murmur appears/louder over weeks as **PVR falls**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Preductal/right-hand and postductal/foot oxygen saturation; **echocardiography** defines anatomy
★ Hyperoxia test: little PaO2 rise with 100% oxygen suggests cardiac shunting; echo preferred
ECG and chest radiograph support diagnosis; normal murmur does not exclude critical disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected duct-dependent lesion → **prostaglandin E1** immediately; monitor for apnea
★ Tet spell (agitation, softer murmur) → knee–chest, oxygen, fluids, morphine; refractory → phenylephrine or propranolol
TGA with inadequate mixing → balloon atrial septostomy, then arterial switch
Large shunts → diuretics, closure; premature PDA → ibuprofen; **obstructed TAPVR → emergency repair**
Coarctation → repair; post-repair paradoxical hypertension → **IV beta-blocker**; Eisenmenger → **do not close shunt**

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, failure to thrive, arrhythmias, infective endocarditis
Right-to-left shunting → brain abscess, paradoxical emboli, secondary erythrocytosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Pulse-ox newborn screening; rubella immunization before pregnancy; maternal glycemic control
Endocarditis prophylaxis for selected unrepaired cyanotic or prosthetic-material lesions during dental procedures

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lung disease: substantial oxygen response, pulmonary findings
PPHN: elevated pulmonary resistance with structurally normal heart

table.title: Five cyanotic lesions
rows: RV obstruction, VSD, overriding aorta, RVH; boot-shaped heart
Parallel circuits; single S2; egg-on-string silhouette
Pulmonary veins drain systemically; obstruction → edema

congenital-heart-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric cardiology teaching.

congenital-infections.name: Congenital infections
congenital-infections.scope: Cytomegalovirus (sensorineural hearing loss, periventricular calcifications), Toxoplasmosis (chorioretinitis), Parvovirus B19 (hydrops), Rubella, Varicella, Zika, screening and diagnosis
congenital-infections.core: Congenital infection causes growth restriction, hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice, thrombocytopenia, or hydrops; organ-specific patterns identify the pathogen.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: CMV: toddler saliva/urine; toxoplasma: undercooked meat, cat feces; B19: child with slapped-cheek rash
Absent rubella/varicella immunity; mosquito exposure or sexual transmission in Zika-risk areas

rows.label: Clues
items: Petechiae/blueberry-muffin lesions, abnormal fetal ultrasound; many infected newborns initially appear well
★ B19 hydrops: cardiomegaly, ascites, edema without red-cell alloantibodies
Maternal rash: B19 → slapped cheek, then reticular limb rash; rubella → descending rash, postauricular nodes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transplacental infection disrupts organogenesis; later exposure may cause inflammation or marrow suppression
Toxoplasma transmission increases with gestational age; earlier infection causes more severe injury

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Maternal exposure → pathogen-specific **IgG/IgM**, paired titers or avidity; isolated IgM needs confirmation
★ CMV newborn diagnosis: saliva PCR then confirm urine PCR **within 21 days**
Suspected fetal infection → targeted ultrasound, pathogen-specific amniotic-fluid PCR; B19 → serial MCA Doppler
Prenatal rubella IgG routinely; no universal US maternal CMV, toxoplasma, or B19 screening

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic congenital CMV → **valganciclovir**, monitor CBC and liver tests
Congenital toxoplasmosis → pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + leucovorin; maternal regimen depends on fetal infection
B19 severe fetal anemia → intrauterine transfusion; rubella/Zika structural injury → supportive care
Maternal varicella exposure without immunity → varicella-zoster immune globulin; maternal pneumonia → IV acyclovir
Maternal varicella onset 5 days before to 2 days after delivery → **newborn VZIG**

rows.label: Complications
items: Stillbirth, neurodevelopmental disability; delayed/progressive hearing loss requires longitudinal audiology

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Rubella/varicella vaccination before pregnancy or postpartum; **live vaccines contraindicated during pregnancy**
Handwashing after diapers; cook meat, avoid litter handling; mosquito precautions and Zika exposure counseling
Term newborn of varicella-immune mother: transplacental IgG protects → no prophylaxis after exposure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aneuploidy: abnormal genetic testing rather than pathogen testing
Rh disease: positive maternal antibody screen with fetal anemia

table.title: Discriminating congenital patterns
rows: Periventricular calcifications, microcephaly, sensorineural hearing loss, chorioretinitis
Severe microcephaly, subcortical calcifications, ocular abnormalities

congenital-infections.evidence: CMV testing checked 2026-10-30: [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/cytomegalovirus/hcp/clinical-overview/index.html); remaining pathogen patterns established teaching.

contraception.name: Contraception
contraception.scope: Combined oral contraceptives, progestin-only pills, implant, intrauterine devices, tubal sterilization
contraception.core: Choose contraception through shared decisions about efficacy, bleeding, reversibility, adherence, and estrogen-related vascular risk.

rows.label: Who
items: Anyone seeking pregnancy prevention; adolescents and nulliparous patients can use IUDs or implants
Healthy patient: blood pressure suffices; **no pelvic exam** needed before oral contraceptives

rows.label: Schedule
items: Pills daily; depot medroxyprogesterone every 3 months; implants/IUDs last years (product-dependent)
★ Emergency contraception ≤**5 days**: copper IUD/ulipristal; levonorgestrel ≤72 h, no medical contraindications
Progestin-only pills: daily timing crucial; norethindrone less forgiving than drospirenone

rows.label: Special groups
items: Breastfeeding (estrogen lowers milk volume, protein) or estrogen contraindication → progestin-only or copper IUD
Current breast cancer → copper IUD; avoid hormonal methods
Prior VTE, poor adherence → **IUD/implant** (depot raises VTE risk); older exams: depot, avoid IUD after STI

rows.label: Choice
items: Combined pills: suppress ovulation, improve acne/cramps, reduce endometrial/ovarian cancer risk
★ **LARC** minimizes adherence failures; condoms add STI protection
Tubal sterilization: permanent; counsel regret, alternatives, surgical risk, ectopic risk after failure

rows.label: Contraindications
items: ★ Estrogen: **migraine with aura, prior VTE/thrombophilia**, hypertension (stop pill), early postpartum
Smoking age ≥35: combined methods usually avoid; ≥15 cigarettes/day → absolute contraindication
IUD: pregnancy, cervicitis/PID, distorted cavity (non-distorting fibroid OK); copper: also Wilson disease

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Same-day STI screening need not delay insertion without cervicitis; prior PID alone permits IUD
Sterilization: voluntary informed consent; no required partner approval, parity, or marital status
After ulipristal, wait 5 days before progestin; backup contraception needed after hormonal restart

table.title: Long-acting choices
rows: Treats heavy menses; atrophy → expected benign amenorrhea

copd.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
copd.scope: Stable COPD, acute exacerbation (AECOPD), oxygen-induced hypercapnia, noninvasive ventilation (NIV/BiPAP), indications for intubation, bronchodilators and glucocorticoids
copd.core: Persistent airflow obstruction after inhalational exposure causes progressive exertional dyspnea and episodic infectious or inflammatory exacerbations.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Tobacco, biomass smoke, occupational dusts; alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with early/basilar emphysema

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic cough/sputum, prolonged expiration, wheeze, hyperinflation
★ **Somnolence, exhaustion, silent chest, worsening acidosis** → impending respiratory failure
Exacerbation: ↑dyspnea, purulent sputum, rhonchi, **no infiltrate** → acute bronchitis, not pneumonia

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Small-airway inflammation + alveolar destruction → expiratory collapse, air trapping, impaired diffusion
Excess oxygen worsens CO₂ retention mainly through V/Q mismatch and Haldane effect

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Postbronchodilator FEV₁/FVC <0.70** confirms persistent obstruction in compatible clinical setting
Exacerbation: pulse oximetry; ABG for severe distress/altered mentation; radiograph for pneumonia, edema, pneumothorax
Consider ECG, troponin, BNP, or PE evaluation when symptoms exceed expected exacerbation pattern

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **albuterol + ipratropium**, prednisone for 5 days; titrate oxygen to 88–92%
Antibiotics: purulence + increased dyspnea/sputum volume, or ventilatory support; doxycycline/azithromycin options
★ Hypercapnic acidosis, pH ≤7.35 → **BiPAP** unless aspiration risk, arrest, instability, inability to cooperate
Intubate for failed NIV, severe encephalopathy, refractory hypoxemia, or inability to protect airway
Long-term oxygen if stable PaO₂ ≤55 or saturation ≤88%; selected cor pulmonale/polycythemia with PaO₂ 56–59

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, cor pulmonale, secondary polycythemia, cachexia
Pneumonia risk with inhaled steroids; ventilation → dynamic hyperinflation, auto-PEEP, barotrauma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Smoking cessation**, influenza/COVID/pneumococcal/RSV vaccination when eligible, pulmonary rehabilitation
Check inhaler technique/adherence; offer alpha-1 antitrypsin testing at least once

rows.label: Mimics
items: Asthma: variable symptoms and reversible obstruction
Heart failure: orthopnea, edema, vascular congestion; bronchiectasis: copious sputum, dilated bronchi

table.title: Stable inhaled treatment
rows: Exacerbations with eosinophilia or concurrent asthma

copd.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [GOLD 2026](https://goldcopd.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/GOLD-REPORT-2026-v1.3-8Dec2025_WMV2.pdf); acute ventilatory care: established teaching.

dementia.name: Dementia
dementia.scope: Alzheimer, vascular, Lewy body, frontotemporal, reversible causes, normal cognitive aging vs MCI, Parkinson disease dementia
dementia.core: Acquired cognitive decline interfering with independent daily function; distinguish dementia from normal aging and mild cognitive impairment by functional consequences.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Advanced age: strongest Alzheimer risk; early-onset first-degree family history; Down syndrome (APP triplication)
Vascular risk factors, prior stroke, Parkinson disease
Anticholinergics, sedatives, alcohol, hearing loss, sleep apnea may worsen cognition

rows.label: Clues
items: Collateral history: missed bills/medications, getting lost, unsafe cooking or driving
Personality, language, executive, visuospatial, memory, motor symptoms help establish phenotype
Abrupt change, fluctuating attention, fever, focal deficits → evaluate acute superimposed illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alzheimer: amyloid plaques/tau tangles; Lewy/Parkinson: alpha-synuclein; vascular disease: ischemic neuronal injury
Alzheimer: hippocampal loss → poor delayed/episodic recall; **nucleus basalis of Meynert** loss → acetylcholine deficit
Frontotemporal degeneration affects frontal/anterior temporal networks, often before typical late-life onset

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Patient/informant history, cognition, function**; MoCA/MMSE support diagnosis, cannot establish it alone
★ **CBC, CMP, TSH, B12**, depression/medication review; HIV/syphilis testing if risk
Brain MRI or noncontrast CT → infarcts, mass, subdural, hydrocephalus; avoid routine PET as first test
Normal aging: slower retrieval, preserved independence → reassurance; MCI: objective deficit, independence preserved
Typical Alzheimer: clinical diagnosis after routine labs/imaging; **APOE genotyping not indicated**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Alzheimer/Lewy/Parkinson dementia → **donepezil or rivastigmine**; moderate/severe Alzheimer → add memantine
Vascular disease → BP/lipid/diabetes control, stroke prevention; frontotemporal behavioral symptoms → consider SSRI
★ Agitation → seek pain/infection, routines/redirection first; **avoid typical antipsychotics in Lewy/Parkinson disease**
Early biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer: specialist-selected antiamyloid drugs; baseline/serial MRI for ARIA
Parkinson dementia psychosis/agitation → **quetiapine** over haloperidol; clozapine needs agranulocytosis monitoring

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, aspiration, malnutrition, wandering, caregiver burnout; antipsychotics → increased mortality
Cholinesterase inhibitors → bradycardia, syncope, GI effects; antiamyloid antibodies → edema/microhemorrhage
Parkinson disease: dementia strongest predictor of nursing home placement and mortality

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Driving/home safety, advance planning**, caregiver support; assess decision-specific capacity
Visuospatial deficit, e.g., failed pentagon copy → **no car keys** until formal driving assessment
Exercise, hearing correction, social engagement, vascular risk reduction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Delirium: hours–days, impaired attention, fluctuating awareness
Depression: prominent distress, variable effort, potentially reversible cognitive deficits
Normal-pressure hydrocephalus: gait-first decline, incontinence, ventriculomegaly; tap test may predict shunt response

table.title: Phenotype clues
rows: Insidious episodic-memory decline, later multidomain deficits
Stroke-related or stepwise decline, focal findings
Early hallucinations, fluctuation, REM behavior, parkinsonism
Early disinhibition/apathy or progressive aphasia; memory spared
Established motor disease >1 year before dementia

dementia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [Alzheimer's Association diagnostic guidance 2024](https://www.alz.org/news/2024/clinical-practice-guideline-evaluation-alzheimers), [NICE dementia](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng97/chapter/Recommendations/); established subtype teaching.

depressive-disorders.name: Depressive disorders
depressive-disorders.scope: Major depressive disorder criteria, depression in older adults, bereavement vs MDD, pharmacotherapy, psychotherapy, suicide risk
depressive-disorders.core: Persistent low mood or loss of pleasure with neurovegetative and cognitive symptoms, causing clinically significant distress or impaired function.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior episodes, family history, chronic illness/pain, substance use, postpartum period, social isolation
Older adults: disability, bereavement, polypharmacy; somatic presentations

rows.label: Clues
items: SIGECAPS: sleep, interest, guilt, energy, concentration, appetite, psychomotor change, suicidality
Psychotic depression: delusions/hallucinations only during mood episodes, often guilt or nihilism
★ **Suicide risk**: prior attempt, intent, plan, means, agitation, psychosis, intoxication
Youth: **irritable mood** qualifies; academic decline, withdrawal, somatic complaints; not normal teenage behavior

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Multifactorial mood-circuit dysfunction involving monoamines, **HPA hyperactivity with raised cortisol**, and neuroplasticity

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ MDD: **≥5 symptoms for ≥2 weeks**, including depressed mood or anhedonia; exclude mania/hypomania
Screen all adults, even asymptomatic: PHQ-2, PHQ-9 for severity; older adults: **Geriatric Depression Scale**
Interview establishes diagnosis; assess substances, drugs, TSH/CBC when clinically suspected
★ **Ask directly about suicide**, access to firearms, protective factors; questioning does not increase risk
Post-CABG anhedonia, withdrawal, fatigue → depression screen; vein-harvest leg edema expected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Imminent danger or **severe malnutrition** → **observation, psychiatric hospitalization**; remove lethal means
Mild: CBT/interpersonal therapy; moderate/severe: sertraline + psychotherapy; pregnancy → shared risk–benefit discussion
★ Urgent suicidality/catatonia/anorexia → **ECT**; psychotic depression → ECT or antidepressant + antipsychotic
Alternatives: **bupropion** (fatigue/hypersomnia, smoking cessation), **mirtazapine** (poor appetite, insomnia)
Continue antidepressant ≥6 months after remission; recurrent/severe episodes → longer maintenance

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, malnutrition, functional decline, recurrence
SSRIs: sexual dysfunction, GI effects, hyponatremia; early activation/suicidality monitoring, especially age <25
Bupropion: seizures; avoid with eating disorders, seizure disorders or brain tumor; mirtazapine: weight gain/sedation
Benzodiazepines in older adults: worsen depression, sedation, falls → stop, use antidepressant

rows.label: Prevention
items: Safety plan, early follow-up after drug changes
Taper antidepressants to reduce discontinuation symptoms; avoid antidepressant monotherapy in bipolar disorder

rows.label: Mimics
items: Dementia: insidious consistent deficits; **pseudodementia**: subacute, "I don't know" answers, recall improves with prompting
Hypothyroidism: cold intolerance, constipation, elevated TSH
Untreated OSA: snoring, obesity, sleepiness → **mood disorder due to medical condition**, not MDD
Anorexia nervosa: fear of weight gain, distorted body image

table.title: Distinguishing persistent sadness
rows: Waves tied to reminders; self-esteem usually preserved
Pervasive worthlessness; bereavement does not exclude diagnosis
Stressor within 3 months; MDD criteria absent

drug-eruptions.name: Drug eruptions
drug-eruptions.scope: Morbilliform drug eruption, fixed drug eruption, DRESS syndrome, drug discontinuation, antihistamines, topical corticosteroids
drug-eruptions.core: New medication followed by rash: distinguish uncomplicated delayed hypersensitivity from a systemic reaction requiring admission and organ monitoring.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Antibiotics, sulfonamides, anticonvulsants, allopurinol, NSAIDs; prior sensitization accelerates recurrence
Aminopenicillin exposure during EBV infection often produces an exanthem; not automatically lifelong penicillin allergy

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus common in benign eruptions; uncomplicated disease lacks organ dysfunction
★ **Skin pain, blistering, mucosal erosions, hypotension** → severe reaction; urgent hospital evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: T-cell-mediated delayed hypersensitivity; tissue-resident memory cells explain localized recurrence
DRESS: systemic immune activation, sometimes associated with herpesvirus reactivation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Medication timeline**, including OTC agents and recently stopped drugs; examine entire skin and mucosa
Possible systemic reaction → CBC/differential, AST/ALT, bilirubin, creatinine, urinalysis; trend abnormalities
DRESS: compatible exposure, skin/blood/organ abnormalities; RegiSCAR scoring supports diagnosis
Biopsy when morphology uncertain; no routine rechallenge or skin testing during acute illness

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Discontinue culprit drug**; stop nonessential agents if severe reaction and culprit uncertain
Mild exanthem/localized fixed eruption → **topical triamcinolone**, emollients; cetirizine for itching
★ DRESS with substantial organ injury → **systemic prednisone**, specialist-supervised slow taper over weeks to months
Anaphylaxis features → IM epinephrine; DRESS requires inpatient assessment, not antihistamines alone

rows.label: Complications
items: DRESS: hepatitis/liver failure, nephritis, myocarditis, pneumonitis; relapse after rapid steroid withdrawal
Delayed autoimmune thyroiditis or diabetes → follow-up organ testing for several months
Localized fixed eruption often leaves persistent hyperpigmentation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Document culprit, timing, phenotype, severity; provide written avoidance instructions
After severe reactions: avoid culprit/cross-reactive drugs; uncertain allergy labels → specialist evaluation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Viral exanthem: infectious prodrome/exposures; no convincing drug timeline
SJS/TEN: epidermal necrosis and prominent painful mucositis
Urticaria: migratory wheals, individual lesions disappear within 24 h

table.title: Timing and morphology
rows: Usually 1–2 weeks; long-term use does not exclude
Sharply demarcated dusky plaque; identical site

early-pregnancy-loss.name: Early pregnancy loss
early-pregnancy-loss.scope: Threatened abortion, inevitable abortion, incomplete abortion, complete abortion, missed abortion, anembryonic pregnancy
early-pregnancy-loss.core: First-trimester bleeding requires pregnancy location and viability assessment before labeling miscarriage or choosing expectant, medical, or surgical management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Embryonic aneuploidy most common; maternal age, prior losses, uterine anomalies, antiphospholipid syndrome

rows.label: Clues
items: Cramping, vaginal bleeding, passage of tissue; symptoms may be absent with retained nonviable pregnancy
★ Hypotension, syncope, peritoneal signs → **hemorrhage or ruptured ectopic**
Fever, uterine tenderness, foul discharge → septic abortion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Embryonic/fetal demise or failed embryonic development → decidual separation and variable cervical dilation
Corpus luteum progesterone sustains pregnancy until ~10 weeks; removal earlier → **progesterone supplementation**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Transvaginal ultrasound** plus quantitative β-hCG; CBC, blood type, pelvic examination
Definitive nonviability: CRL ≥7 mm without heartbeat or mean sac diameter ≥25 mm without embryo
Absent embryo/heartbeat on repeat: ≥11 days after yolk sac, ≥14 days after sac-only → nonviable
No intrauterine pregnancy → serial hCG/ultrasound; tissue passage alone cannot exclude ectopic

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable, infected, or uncontrolled hemorrhage → **urgent uterine aspiration**; sepsis → IV broad-spectrum antibiotics
Confirmed stable loss → patient choice: observation, mifepristone followed by misoprostol, or aspiration
Threatened loss → expectant follow-up; bed rest does not prevent miscarriage
Stable, unlocated pregnancy, falling hCG → serial hCG until negative; no methotrexate
★ Rh-negative loss **≥12 weeks → RhIg**; ACOG omits routine testing earlier; older exam questions may expect Rh typing

rows.label: Complications
items: Retained products, infection, hemorrhage; intrauterine adhesions after instrumentation; grief/depression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking/alcohol avoidance, optimize diabetes; most isolated chromosomal losses unpreventable
Recurrent clinical losses → assess uterine anatomy, antiphospholipid antibodies and selected genetic causes

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: extrauterine implantation, adnexal mass/free fluid
Gestational trophoblastic disease: very high hCG, abnormal cystic intrauterine tissue
Subchorionic hematoma: bleeding without cramping; viable intrauterine pregnancy, perichorionic collection
Normal early pregnancy: spotting, 5-week sac, hCG ~1,000, simple corpus luteum cyst; embryo not yet expected

eating-disorders.name: Eating disorders
eating-disorders.scope: Anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, binge eating disorder, refeeding syndrome, medical complications, hospitalization criteria
eating-disorders.core: Disordered intake or compensatory behaviors require assessment of medical instability, suicidality, and malnutrition at any body size.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Adolescence, dieting, weight stigma, perfectionism, trauma; psychiatric comorbidity and family history

rows.label: Clues
items: Restrictive disease: cold intolerance, lanugo, bradycardia, orthostasis, menstrual suppression; amenorrhea not required
Purging: parotid hypertrophy, **raised amylase**, enamel erosion, knuckle calluses; hypokalemic hypochloremic alkalosis
★ **Syncope, arrhythmia, hypothermia or severe electrolyte abnormalities** → urgent stabilization

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Starvation suppresses gonadal axis and reduces cardiac mass; vomiting causes chloride/volume depletion
Refeeding insulin surge shifts phosphate, potassium and magnesium intracellularly

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical interview plus weight trajectory, vitals/orthostatics, **ECG, electrolytes, Mg, phosphate**
Binge: loss of control plus unusually large intake; bulimia/BED require episodes ≥weekly for 3 months
Assess suicide risk, substance use, exercise, laxatives; normal BMI does not exclude severe disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Medical admission for instability: e.g., HR <50, BP <90/60, severe electrolyte disturbance or acute food refusal
★ Refeeding → **thiamine**, nutritional rehabilitation, serial phosphate/K/Mg and cardiac monitoring
Adolescent anorexia → family-based treatment; adults → eating-disorder-focused psychotherapy; medication alone insufficient
Bulimia → CBT plus fluoxetine; avoid bupropion because of seizures
BED → CBT; lisdexamfetamine for selected adults, monitor misuse/cardiovascular risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → osteoporosis, infertility; cardiac failure, arrhythmic death; purging → arrhythmias, esophageal injury
Refeeding → hypophosphatemia, respiratory failure, edema, delirium; high suicide mortality
Severe starvation → **hypoalbuminemia** with pitting edema

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early recognition of growth/weight-trajectory changes; reduce weight-based stigma; relapse follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hyperthyroidism: increased appetite with tremor and heat intolerance
GI malabsorption: involuntary weight loss without weight/shape-driven restriction

eating-disorders.evidence: Guideline framework checked 2026-10-30: [APA eating disorders guideline, 2023](https://www.psychiatry.org/psychiatrists/practice/clinical-practice-guidelines/eating-disorders); thresholds: established clinical teaching.

table.title: Diagnostic distinction
rows: Restriction or purging + weight-gain fear/distorted self-image

erectile-dysfunction.name: Erectile dysfunction
erectile-dysfunction.scope: Psychogenic vs organic (nocturnal penile tumescence), diabetes mellitus, vascular insufficiency, drug-induced, PDE-5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, nitrate contraindication), vacuum devices, penile prosthesis
erectile-dysfunction.core: Persistent difficulty obtaining or maintaining an erection warrants assessment of vascular health, medication effects, endocrine function, and psychological context.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Diabetes, atherosclerosis, smoking, hypertension, pelvic surgery or radiation, spinal injury
SSRIs, thiazides, some beta-blockers, antipsychotics, heavy alcohol, daily cannabis; depression and performance anxiety

rows.label: Clues
items: Low libido and reduced spontaneous erections suggest androgen deficiency
Claudication or diminished peripheral pulses suggest vascular disease; penile curvature suggests Peyronie disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Nitric oxide → cGMP → cavernosal smooth-muscle relaxation and arterial inflow; venous occlusion maintains rigidity

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Sexual/medical history, medication review, genital/vascular examination; assess cardiovascular risk
★ **Morning total testosterone**, glucose/A1c, lipids; repeat low testosterone before diagnosing hypogonadism
Nocturnal tumescence testing or penile Doppler only if uncertainty or selected procedural planning

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Sildenafil or tadalafil** first-line oral options; sexual stimulation required
★ **Never combine PDE-5 inhibitors with nitrates or riociguat** → profound hypotension
**Stop culprits before PDE-5** (drugs, alcohol, cannabis); counseling, exercise; testosterone for confirmed hypogonadism
Oral failure → vacuum device or intracavernosal/intraurethral alprostadil; refractory cases → penile prosthesis
Unstable cardiac disease → stabilize before resuming sexual activity; alpha-blockers increase hypotension risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Relationship distress, depression; ED may precede symptomatic cardiovascular disease
Alprostadil: priapism; erection >4 hours → emergency evaluation; prosthesis infection or mechanical failure

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation; optimize glycemia, BP, lipids; reduce excess alcohol

rows.label: Mimics
items: Low libido alone: desire impaired without necessarily impaired erectile mechanics
Premature ejaculation: erection obtained but ejaculation earlier than desired

table.title: Etiologic clues
rows: Gradual, consistent, also with masturbation; nocturnal erections reduced
Heavy drinking, high GGT; nocturnal erections may persist

esophageal-perforation.name: Esophageal perforation
esophageal-perforation.scope: Boerhaave syndrome, iatrogenic perforation, mediastinitis, gastrografin esophagography, emergent surgical repair
esophageal-perforation.core: Severe chest pain after vomiting or esophageal instrumentation, with systemic toxicity or mediastinal air, is an esophageal emergency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Endoscopy, dilation, foreign bodies, caustic injury; forceful emesis causes spontaneous Boerhaave rupture
Underlying stricture or malignancy increases instrumentation-related injury risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Tachycardia, fever, dyspnea, odynophagia; neck swelling or palpable crepitus
★ **Left pleural effusion**, pneumomediastinum or subcutaneous emphysema after retching
Hypotension, rising lactate, organ dysfunction → uncontrolled contamination and sepsis
Classic vomiting–pain–emphysema triad often incomplete; absence does not exclude rupture

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Full-thickness tear releases saliva, gastric contents and bacteria into mediastinum/pleura
Boerhaave typically affects distal posterolateral esophagus; contamination causes chemical then infectious mediastinitis

rows.label: Dx
items: **Upright chest x-ray first** for mediastinal/pleural air; normal early film does not exclude → contrast study
★ Stable suspected leak → **CT chest with water-soluble oral contrast** or water-soluble esophagram
Gastrografin study negative with persistent suspicion → thin barium study to detect small leaks
Avoid routine diagnostic endoscopy when insufflation could enlarge an uncontained tear

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **NPO**, IV fluids, IV piperacillin–tazobactam, urgent thoracic/general surgery consultation
★ Free pleural/mediastinal leak (even stable) or shock → **operative repair + drainage**; chest tube inadequate
Contained leak without sepsis → antibiotics, drainage ± endoscopic closure/stent; older questions may expect surgery
IV proton-pump inhibitor; enteral feeding distal to leak or parenteral nutrition
Avoid blind nasogastric placement; decompression, if needed, under specialist guidance

rows.label: Complications
items: Mediastinitis, empyema, septic shock, multiorgan failure; delay markedly worsens outcomes
Persistent fistula, esophageal stricture and malnutrition after healing

rows.label: Prevention
items: Careful procedural technique; prompt evaluation of new pain following esophageal instrumentation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mallory–Weiss: mucosal tear causing hematemesis without mediastinal contamination
ACS: ischemic ECG/troponin pattern; no contrast leak
Acute aortic syndrome: vascular abnormality on CT angiography

esophageal-perforation.evidence: Not checked online; established emergency esophageal management.

extremity-vascular-injury.name: Extremity vascular injury
extremity-vascular-injury.scope: Hard signs (pulsatile bleeding, expanding hematoma, absent pulses, thrill/bruit, pallor), soft signs (diminished pulse, proximity), surgical exploration vs CT angiography
extremity-vascular-injury.core: After limb trauma, active arterial bleeding or threatened perfusion requires immediate intervention; stable equivocal findings require objective vascular assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Penetrating wounds near major vessels; blunt crush or traction injury
Knee dislocation, supracondylar humeral fracture, open fractures; spontaneous joint reduction may conceal mechanism

rows.label: Clues
items: Pain, pallor, coolness, paresthesia, paralysis indicate worsening ischemia; motor deficit is late
★ **Normal distal pulses do not exclude injury**, especially intimal tears after knee dislocation
Examine both limbs and document pulses, motor function, sensation before and after reduction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transection causes hemorrhage; intimal disruption → thrombosis and delayed ischemia
Contained arterial leak → pseudoaneurysm; artery–vein communication → traumatic AV fistula

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Hard signs → immediate **operative exploration**; imaging must not delay limb-saving treatment
Stable without hard signs → ABI/API; **<0.9** or abnormal examination → CT angiography
Normal examination + index ≥0.9 → serial examinations/follow-up; observe high-risk blunt injuries
Duplex ultrasound alternative in selected stable patients; CTA localizes injury for repair

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Direct pressure; uncontrolled hemorrhage → proximal tourniquet; avoid blind clamping
Resuscitate hemorrhagic shock with blood products; urgent vascular surgery consultation
★ Restore arterial flow rapidly, ideally within 6 hours; primary repair or vein graft
Temporary shunt when definitive repair delayed; coordinate fracture stabilization and revascularization
Prolonged ischemia, crush injury, marked swelling → early fasciotomy; monitor reperfusion hyperkalemia

rows.label: Complications
items: Amputation, persistent neuropathy, compartment syndrome; rhabdomyolysis and AKI after reperfusion
Delayed thrombosis, pseudoaneurysm, AV fistula, graft infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Repeat neurovascular checks after splinting, reduction, and repair; promptly loosen constrictive dressings
Discharge follow-up essential for delayed swelling, recurrent bleeding, bruit, or new ischemic symptoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: Compartment syndrome: pain with passive stretch, tense compartments; pulses often remain palpable
Isolated nerve injury: focal deficits without objective perfusion abnormality

table.title: Trauma signs
rows: Absent pulses; bruit/thrill; overt distal ischemia
Diminished pulse; stable hematoma; prior bleeding

fetal-alcohol-syndrome.name: Fetal alcohol syndrome
fetal-alcohol-syndrome.scope: Facial dysmorphism (smooth philtrum, thin vermilion border, small palpebral fissures), prenatal/postnatal growth restriction, microcephaly, intellectual disability, neurobehavioral deficits, maternal alcohol screening
fetal-alcohol-syndrome.core: A child with growth restriction, characteristic facial features, and persistent central nervous system dysfunction may have prenatal alcohol-related injury.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prenatal alcohol exposure, especially binge/heavy use; injury possible throughout pregnancy
Maternal alcohol use disorder, limited prenatal care; individual susceptibility and timing modify severity

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Facial pattern: **smooth philtrum, thin upper vermilion, short palpebral fissures**; flat nasal bridge possible
Prenatal/postnatal growth deficiency, small head circumference
Executive/attention deficits, poor impulse control, impaired adaptive behavior; intellectual disability variable
Normal intelligence or absent facial features does not exclude broader fetal alcohol spectrum disorder

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alcohol crosses placenta → disrupted neuronal migration, proliferation, survival and craniofacial development

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical multidisciplinary assessment**: growth, dysmorphology, neurodevelopment and prenatal exposure history
Obtain collateral prenatal records sensitively; no laboratory test confirms remote fetal exposure
FAS diagnosis can be possible without confirmed exposure when defining phenotype present; diagnostic systems differ
Evaluate hearing/vision, congenital anomalies and competing genetic diagnoses

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Early developmental intervention**, individualized education, speech/occupational therapy, behavioral supports
Stable structured caregiving, predictable routines, caregiver education; coordinate social services
Treat diagnosed ADHD, mood or sleep disorders individually; no drug reverses prenatal injury
Assess feeding/growth and provide nutritional support; manage congenital heart or other structural disease

rows.label: Complications
items: Lifelong learning/adaptive impairment, mental illness, substance misuse, disrupted schooling and legal difficulties
Cardiac septal defects and other congenital anomalies may coexist

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **No known safe amount or timing of alcohol** during pregnancy or attempted conception
Universal nonjudgmental maternal screening with AUDIT-C/T-ACE; brief intervention and treatment referral
Alcohol dependence → supervised withdrawal/treatment planning; offer contraception counseling when pregnancy not desired

rows.label: Mimics
items: Down syndrome: macroglossia, hypotonia, upslanting fissures; palmar crease, epicanthal folds occur in both
Fragile X: long face, large ears, macroorchidism; no smooth philtrum
Isolated ADHD: no defining growth/facial phenotype; may coexist
Environmental deprivation: developmental deficits without characteristic embryopathy

fetal-alcohol-syndrome.evidence: Prevention checked 2026-10-30: [CDC FASD](https://www.cdc.gov/fasd/about/); established developmental assessment.

fetal-growth-restriction.name: Fetal growth restriction
fetal-growth-restriction.scope: Symmetric vs asymmetric FGR, uteroplacental insufficiency, chromosomal anomalies, congenital infections, umbilical artery Doppler surveillance, oligohydramnios
fetal-growth-restriction.core: Estimated fetal weight or abdominal circumference below the 10th percentile requires evaluation for placental dysfunction and fetal disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Maternal hypertension, preeclampsia, renal/vascular disease, smoking, cocaine, malnutrition, prior affected pregnancy
Aneuploidy, structural anomalies, CMV; multiple gestation

rows.label: Clues
items: Fundal height lag >3 cm, decreased movement, oligohydramnios; sometimes abnormal maternal placental disease markers
★ **EFW <3rd percentile** indicates severe disease; normal-size parents do not establish constitutional smallness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental resistance reduces oxygen/nutrients; redistribution preserves cerebral over abdominal growth
Low fetal renal perfusion reduces urine production and fluid volume

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Ultrasound biometry using reliable dating → detailed anatomy; serial growth generally every 3–4 weeks
★ **Umbilical artery Doppler every 1–2 weeks**; absent (AEDV)/reversed (REDV) diastolic velocity → intensified surveillance
Weekly NST after viability; increase frequency with Doppler deterioration or maternal comorbidity
Early <32 weeks, unexplained or anomalous → offer amniocentesis/microarray; CMV PCR if amniocentesis chosen
Do not order indiscriminate TORCH panels without exposure or suggestive findings

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Reversed flow → **hospitalization**, corticosteroids, frequent cardiotocography, delivery planning
Anticipated preterm birth → betamethasone; magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection before 32 weeks
Nonreassuring testing/maternal deterioration → earlier delivery; absent/reversed flow may favor cesarean
Bed rest, sildenafil, and LMWH solely to treat/prevent FGR provide no established benefit

rows.label: Complications
items: Stillbirth, intrapartum intolerance, neonatal hypoglycemia, hypothermia, polycythemia; later metabolic/cardiovascular risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Tobacco/drug cessation, maternal disease control; low-dose aspirin when preeclampsia-risk criteria met

rows.label: Mimics
items: Incorrect dates: early ultrasound establishes gestational age
Constitutionally small fetus: reassuring interval growth and normal Doppler without placental disease

table.title: Patterns and delivery in otherwise stable disease
rows: Often later placental insufficiency; patterns overlap

gallstone-disease.name: Gallstone disease
gallstone-disease.scope: Biliary colic, acute cholecystitis, choledocholithiasis, cholangitis, gallstone pancreatitis
gallstone-disease.core: Gallstone location determines the syndrome: transient cystic obstruction, gallbladder inflammation, common-duct obstruction/infection, or pancreatic inflammation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, female sex, pregnancy, obesity, rapid weight loss, ileal disease/resection
Hemolysis/cirrhosis → pigment stones; critical illness/TPN → acalculous cholecystitis

rows.label: Clues
items: Postprandial RUQ/epigastric discomfort radiating to back or right shoulder; assess fever and jaundice
★ **Fever + RUQ pain + jaundice** → cholangitis; hypotension/confusion → severe infection
Pancreatitis: persistent epigastric pain radiating to back, vomiting; ALT >150 supports biliary cause

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cholesterol supersaturation or pigment precipitation creates calculi; obstruction location dictates organ injury
Infected obstructed bile ducts require drainage because antibiotics cannot reliably sterilize a closed system

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **RUQ ultrasound first**; CBC, bilirubin/alkaline phosphatase, AST/ALT, lipase
Suspected cholecystitis with equivocal ultrasound → HIDA; nonvisualized gallbladder supports cystic-duct obstruction
Intermediate common-duct stone probability → MRCP or EUS; ERCP reserved primarily for treatment
★ Direct intervention: **stone seen, cholangitis, or bilirubin >4 mg/dL plus dilated duct**
Post-cholecystectomy jaundice + dilated ducts → retained stone/duct injury → **ERCP**; HIDA only for bile leak

rows.label: Tx
items: Analgesia, fluids, antiemetics; infection → ceftriaxone/metronidazole or piperacillin/tazobactam
★ **Cholangitis → urgent biliary drainage**, immediately after stabilization if shock; do not await antibiotic response
Poor surgical candidate with acute cholecystitis → percutaneous cholecystostomy
★ Gallstone pancreatitis → supportive care, early oral feeding; **no urgent ERCP without cholangitis/persistent obstruction**

rows.label: Complications
items: Empyema, gangrene, perforation, abscess, septic shock; pancreatitis → necrosis/organ failure
Cholecystoenteric fistula → gallstone ileus; imaging: bowel obstruction, pneumobilia, ectopic stone
ERCP → pancreatitis/bleeding/perforation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain healthy weight; avoid rapid weight loss; selected bariatric patients → ursodiol prophylaxis
After duct clearance → cholecystectomy; after mild biliary pancreatitis → same-admission cholecystectomy
Asymptomatic uncomplicated stones → observation; no routine prophylactic surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hepatitis: marked aminotransferase elevation, no obstructing stone
PUD: burning epigastric pain, ulcer on endoscopy
Inferior MI: ischemic ECG/troponin changes, cardiovascular risk

table.title: Localizing obstruction
rows: Persistent >6 hours, Murphy sign, wall thickening
Cholestatic labs, duct stone/dilation; no infection
ERCP extraction or operative duct clearance
Inflamed gallbladder without stones; critically ill

gestational-diabetes-mellitus.name: Gestational diabetes mellitus
gestational-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Screening (50g oral glucose challenge at 24-28 weeks), diagnostic 3-hour 100g test, glycemic targets, nutritional therapy, insulin, fetal and neonatal complications (macrosomia, hypoglycemia, RDS, polycythemia)
gestational-diabetes-mellitus.core: Pregnancy-induced insulin resistance unmasks hyperglycemia, increasing fetal insulin secretion and growth; screen routinely at 24–28 weeks.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, prior GDM/macrosomia, family history of type 2 diabetes, PCOS
High-risk patients need early assessment for previously unrecognized overt diabetes

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; excessive fetal growth or polyhydramnios may prompt evaluation
Early marked hyperglycemia suggests preexisting diabetes rather than typical later-onset GDM

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental hormones increase maternal insulin requirements; inadequate beta-cell compensation causes dysglycemia
Maternal glucose crosses placenta; insulin does not; fetal hyperinsulinemia persists briefly after birth
Fetal hyperinsulinemia → macrosomia; antagonizes cortisol → less surfactant, **RDS**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Two-step screen: **nonfasting 50 g challenge**, 1-hour threshold 130–140 mg/dL by local protocol
Positive challenge → fasting 100 g, 3-hour OGTT; **≥2 abnormal values** diagnose GDM
Alternative one-step 75 g OGTT: fasting ≥92, 1-hour ≥180, or 2-hour ≥153 mg/dL
HbA1c alone does not replace pregnancy glucose testing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First: **individualized nutrition, activity, home glucose monitoring**; avoid severe carbohydrate restriction
★ Targets: fasting **<95**, 1-hour <140, or 2-hour <120 mg/dL
Above targets despite lifestyle → **insulin preferred**; metformin crosses placenta, counsel if used
Medication need or poor control → fetal surveillance; delivery timing depends on control and obstetric findings
Suspected fetal weight ≥4,500 g with diabetes → discuss planned cesarean

rows.label: Complications
items: Maternal: preeclampsia, cesarean delivery, future type 2 diabetes
Fetal: macrosomia, shoulder dystocia, birth trauma; poor control increases stillbirth risk
Neonate: **hypoglycemia**, RDS, polycythemia, jaundice; congenital anomalies mainly reflect pregestational diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Postpartum **75 g OGTT at 4–12 weeks**; lifelong diabetes testing every 1–3 years
Breastfeeding, weight management, activity; most GDM insulin needs resolve after placental delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pregestational diabetes: overt diagnostic-range hyperglycemia early in pregnancy
Physiologic glycosuria: lower renal threshold without diagnostic blood glucose abnormalities
