Renal function, TSH, calcium; valproate CBC/LFTs; carbamazepine CBC, sodium, LFTs
Carbamazepine: HLA-B*1502 testing with relevant Asian ancestry; agranulocytosis, SIADH, severe rash

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Lithium toxicity: coarse tremor, ataxia, confusion → stop lithium, IV saline
**Hemodialysis**: seizures/coma, life-threatening arrhythmia, or renal impairment with lithium >4 mEq/L
Consider dialysis: >5 mEq/L, confusion, or clearance >36 hours to <1; monitor rebound

multiple-myeloma.name: Multiple myeloma
multiple-myeloma.scope: CRAB features (hypercalcemia, renal insufficiency, anemia, bone lytic lesions), SPEP/UPEP M-spike, serum free light chains, bone marrow biopsy (>10% plasma cells), MGUS, smoldering myeloma
multiple-myeloma.core: A clonal plasma-cell malignancy causes monoclonal protein production and organ damage; modern biomarkers can establish treatment-requiring disease before symptoms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, Black ancestry, male sex, preexisting MGUS; usually no identifiable preventable exposure

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **CRAB**: hypercalcemia, renal impairment, anemia, lytic bone lesions
Back/rib pain, pathologic fracture, recurrent bacterial infection, high total protein, rouleaux
Acute weakness/back pain → cord compression; proteinuria or restrictive cardiomyopathy → consider AL amyloid

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Marrow expansion suppresses blood formation; osteoclast activation without osteoblast response causes bone destruction
Light chains injure renal tubules; low polyclonal immunoglobulins → **encapsulated bacteria**, e.g., pneumococcus

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **SPEP/immunofixation + free light chains**, urine studies; light-chain disease may lack serum spike
★ **Bone marrow biopsy** quantifies clonal plasma cells; whole-body low-dose CT/MRI assesses bone disease
Active disease: ≥10% clonal marrow cells/plasmacytoma plus attributable CRAB or myeloma-defining biomarker
SLiM: marrow ≥60%; involved/uninvolved FLC ratio ≥100 with involved FLC ≥100 mg/L
MRI >1 focal lesion ≥5 mm defines active disease; bone scan may miss lytic lesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Bortezomib-based combination** ± daratumumab/lenalidomide/dexamethasone; selected patients → autologous transplant
Hypercalcemia → saline plus antiresorptive; AKI → hydration, avoid NSAIDs/contrast and rapidly reduce light chains
Cord compression → dexamethasone and urgent MRI/radiation or surgery; treat infections promptly
MGUS/smoldering disease generally monitored; high-risk smoldering disease merits specialist assessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Cast nephropathy, vertebral collapse, hyperviscosity, AL amyloidosis; treatment-related neuropathy, infections and thrombosis
Urine dipstick detects albumin, misses light chains; negative dipstick does not exclude cast nephropathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Vaccines, bisphosphonates; proteasome inhibitors → antiviral prophylaxis; immunomodulators → thromboprophylaxis by risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Metastatic carcinoma: destructive lesions without clonal plasma-cell findings
Waldenström macroglobulinemia: IgM, hyperviscosity/lymphadenopathy, usually no lytic lesions

multiple-myeloma.evidence: Criteria checked 2026-10-30: [IMWG diagnostic criteria](https://www.myeloma.org/newly-diagnosed/multiple-myeloma-diagnostic-criteria); treatment: established generalist teaching.

myelodysplastic-syndromes.name: Myelodysplastic syndromes
myelodysplastic-syndromes.scope: Cytopenias, macrocytic anemia, dysplastic neutrophils (Pelger-Huet anomaly), bone marrow biopsy, cytogenetics, progression to acute myeloid leukemia, transfusions
myelodysplastic-syndromes.core: Persistent unexplained cytopenias with an often cellular but ineffective marrow suggest a clonal myeloid neoplasm rather than simple nutrient deficiency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age; prior alkylating chemotherapy, topoisomerase inhibitors, radiation or benzene exposure
Usually acquired de novo; prior cytotoxic exposure raises concern for treatment-related myeloid neoplasm

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Macrocytic anemia with additional cytopenias**, despite adequate B12/folate
Fatigue/dyspnea, recurrent infections, bruising or mucosal bleeding; some cases discovered on routine CBC
Smear: hypogranular neutrophils, bilobed **pseudo-Pelger-Huët** nuclei, abnormal platelets
Circulating blasts or rapidly worsening counts → high-risk disease/transformation concern

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Clonal stem-cell abnormalities produce dysplastic maturation and intramedullary cell death
Peripheral cell scarcity despite commonly hypercellular marrow; selected cases hypocellular

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Exclude reversible causes → **bone marrow aspirate/biopsy with cytogenetics** and molecular testing
CBC, reticulocytes, smear, B12/folate, copper and iron assessment; review drugs/alcohol
≥10% dysplasia in a lineage or defining genetic findings supports diagnosis after excluding mimics
★ Usually **<20% blasts**; ≥20% generally AML, with genetic classification exceptions
Risk score combines blasts, cytogenetics/mutations and cytopenias; guides treatment intensity

rows.label: Tx
items: Symptomatic anemia → RBC transfusions; selected lower-risk anemia → erythropoiesis-stimulating agent or luspatercept
Isolated del(5q), lower-risk transfusion-dependent anemia → lenalidomide
★ Higher-risk disease → **azacitidine or decitabine**; fit candidates → allogeneic stem-cell transplant
Platelets for severe bleeding/thrombocytopenia; febrile neutropenia → prompt IV cefepime
Repeated transfusions with substantial overload → consider iron chelation in suitable long-surviving patients

rows.label: Complications
items: AML progression, serious infections, hemorrhage; transfusion iron overload and alloimmunization
Hypomethylating treatment initially worsens cytopenias; transplant → graft-versus-host disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: B12/folate deficiency: hypersegmented neutrophils, biochemical deficiency and response to replacement
Copper deficiency: cytopenias/dysplasia with zinc excess or malabsorption; reversible with copper

table.title: Morphologic terms
rows: Inherited hyposegmentation without acquired marrow failure

narcolepsy.name: Narcolepsy
narcolepsy.scope: Excessive daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, hypnagogic and hypnopompic hallucinations, sleep paralysis, polysomnography and MSLT, hypocretin (orexin) deficiency, modafinil, sodium oxybate
narcolepsy.core: Irresistible sleep attacks despite sufficient nighttime sleep, with emotion-triggered loss of muscle tone strongly suggesting type 1 narcolepsy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Usually adolescent/young-adult onset; genetic susceptibility with probable autoimmune hypothalamic neuron loss

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Cataplexy**: seconds to minutes of weakness, preserved consciousness; laughter or surprise trigger
Vivid hallucinations at sleep onset or awakening; transient inability to move at sleep transitions
Short naps refreshing; disrupted nighttime sleep; daytime automatic behaviors

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Type 1: deficient hypothalamic hypocretin/orexin → unstable wakefulness and REM intrusion
Type 2: no cataplexy, no demonstrated orexin deficiency

rows.label: Dx
items: Daily sleepiness ≥3 months; sleep diary/actigraphy first to document sufficient sleep
★ Overnight **polysomnography → next-day MSLT**; exclude untreated OSA and sleep deprivation
Mean sleep latency ≤8 minutes plus ≥2 sleep-onset REM periods; preceding PSG can contribute one
Low CSF hypocretin supports type 1; usually unnecessary with characteristic cataplexy and diagnostic testing
Coordinate stimulant/REM-suppressing drug washout before testing; abrupt withdrawal can confound results

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Daytime sleepiness → **modafinil**; alternatives methylphenidate, pitolisant, solriamfetol
★ Prominent cataplexy → **sodium oxybate**; venlafaxine can suppress attacks
Oxybate: avoid alcohol, opioids, benzodiazepines because of respiratory/CNS depression
Scheduled naps, regular nighttime sleep, workplace/school accommodations

rows.label: Complications
items: Motor vehicle crashes, impaired school/work performance, depression
Modafinil reduces hormonal contraceptive effectiveness; review pregnancy planning

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid driving or hazardous work until sleepiness controlled; reassess driving safety during follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: OSA: snoring, witnessed apneas, abnormal respiratory PSG
Idiopathic hypersomnia: long unrefreshing sleep, fewer sleep-onset REM periods
Syncope/seizure: loss of consciousness or postictal confusion rather than isolated cataplexy

nephrolithiasis.name: Nephrolithiasis
nephrolithiasis.scope: Renal colic, calcium oxalate, uric acid, struvite, cystine, drug-induced stones, noncontrast CT, medical expulsive therapy, surgical indications
nephrolithiasis.core: Sudden colicky flank pain radiating toward the groin with hematuria suggests a ureteral stone; infection plus obstruction is an emergency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Low urine volume, high sodium intake, family history, obesity, gout
Hyperparathyroidism, malabsorption, recurrent urinary infection; low citrate, genetic defects

rows.label: Clues
items: Restlessness, nausea/vomiting, CVA tenderness; hematuria may be absent
★ **Fever, pyuria, hypotension, AKI, anuria** → infected or function-threatening obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Urinary supersaturation → crystal formation; obstruction raises ureteral pressure and provokes spasm
Ileal resection/Crohn → fatty acids bind calcium → **colonic oxalate absorption** → calcium oxalate stones

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis + culture if infection suspected**, creatinine, pregnancy test when relevant
★ Nonpregnant adult → **low-dose noncontrast CT**; pregnancy/children → renal ultrasound first
KUB misses radiolucent uric acid stones; radiographic invisibility does not exclude ureteral obstruction
Analyze passed stone; recurrent/high-risk disease → serum evaluation and 24-hour urine

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Ketorolac** for analgesia, ondansetron for nausea, normal hydration; avoid forced high-volume fluids during obstruction
Small uncomplicated stones, pain controlled, afebrile → discharge, oral fluids, analgesia; distal 5–10 mm → consider tamsulosin
★ Infection + obstruction → **urgent stent or nephrostomy + IV antibiotics**; delay definitive stone removal
Intervene for uncontrolled pain, persistent obstruction, renal deterioration, large stone, or failed passage
Ureteroscopy/shock-wave lithotripsy selected by stone; >2 cm/staghorn → percutaneous nephrolithotomy

rows.label: Complications
items: Hydronephrosis, pyelonephritis/urosepsis, recurrent stones, renal loss
Procedures → bleeding, infection, ureteral injury; tamsulosin → orthostasis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Aim **urine volume ≥2–2.5 L/day**, normal dietary calcium, low sodium, moderate animal protein
Recurrent calcium stones/hypercalciuria → chlorthalidone; hypocitraturia → potassium citrate
Do not restrict dietary calcium routinely; calcium with meals reduces enteric oxalate absorption

rows.label: Mimics
items: AAA: older patient, hemodynamic instability, aortic dilation
Pyelonephritis: fever/constant pain; torsion/ectopic pregnancy: genital/pelvic findings

table.title: Stone clues and targeted prevention
rows: Indinavir CT-occult; atazanavir CT-visible; topiramate promotes alkaline urine

nephrolithiasis.evidence: Not checked online; established stone evaluation and prevention principles.

neural-tube-defects.name: Neural tube defects
neural-tube-defects.scope: Anencephaly, spina bifida occulta, meningocele, myelomeningocele, Chiari II malformation, maternal serum AFP, amniotic acetylcholinesterase, lemon and banana signs, folic acid prevention
neural-tube-defects.core: Neural tube closure failure by approximately 4 weeks after conception produces cranial or spinal defects; prevention must begin before pregnancy recognition.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Low folate, prior affected pregnancy, maternal diabetes/obesity, valproate/carbamazepine, early-pregnancy hyperthermia

rows.label: Clues
items: Midline lumbosacral sac, lower-limb weakness, absent reflexes, bladder dysfunction with neural involvement
★ **Lemon skull and banana cerebellum** on fetal ultrasound suggest open spina bifida/Chiari II
Occult lesions: hair tuft, atypical deep dimple, hemangioma; normal skin does not guarantee normal cord

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Failed neurulation leaves neural tissue unprotected; CSF leakage contributes to hindbrain herniation
Folate supports nucleotide synthesis during rapid embryonic cell division

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Maternal serum **AFP at 15–22 weeks**; elevation → verify dating/number, detailed ultrasound
Open defects elevate AFP; closed occulta may not; cfDNA does not screen neural tube defects
★ Uncertain imaging → amniotic fluid **AFP and acetylcholinesterase**; target anatomy scan at 18–22 weeks
Postnatal spinal ultrasound in young infant or MRI for suspected occult dysraphism/tethered cord

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Open spinal lesion: **prone positioning, sterile saline dressing**, avoid pressure/contamination; neonatal neurosurgery
Early closure; assess hydrocephalus, renal function and bladder emptying; intermittent catheterization when neurogenic
Selected prenatal myelomeningocele repair can improve motor outcomes/reduce shunting, with maternal and prematurity risks
Anencephaly → counseling, pregnancy options, and palliative neonatal care; no curative treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Hydrocephalus (Chiari II obstructs CSF), meningitis, orthopedic deformities, neurogenic bowel/bladder, recurrent UTI, kidney injury
Tethered cord may cause progressive weakness or continence changes during growth
Osteopenic insensate legs: new swelling → **X-ray** for occult fracture

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Folic acid 400–800 µg/day** before conception through early pregnancy for average risk
Prior NTD pregnancy → **4 mg/day**, starting ≥1 month before conception through first 3 months
Optimize diabetes, review antiseizure drugs before pregnancy; avoid prolonged overheating

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sacrococcygeal teratoma: solid/cystic mass, not exposed neural placode
Abdominal wall defect: elevated AFP but bowel outside abdomen on ultrasound

table.title: Lesions
rows: Meninges/CSF herniate; cord remains within canal

neural-tube-defects.evidence: Folate checked 2026-10-30: [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/folic-acid/hcp/clinical-overview/), [USPSTF 2023](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/document/ClinicalSummaryFinal/folic-acid-for-the-prevention-of-neural-tube-defects-preventive-medication); remaining content established teaching.

neuromuscular-junction-disorders.name: Neuromuscular junction disorders
neuromuscular-junction-disorders.scope: Myasthenia gravis, Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome, botulism, repetitive nerve stimulation, autoantibodies
neuromuscular-junction-disorders.core: Fluctuating or descending weakness with preserved sensation localizes to neuromuscular transmission; reflexes, pupils, and exercise response separate major causes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: MG: autoimmune disease, thymoma; LEMS: smoking/small-cell lung carcinoma
Botulism: improperly canned foods, injection wounds, infant honey or environmental spores

rows.label: Clues
items: MG: diplopia, ptosis, nasal speech, chewing fatigue; worse late day or repeated activity
LEMS: proximal leg weakness, dry mouth, constipation; transient strength/reflex improvement after exertion
Botulism: cranial palsies → symmetric descending paralysis, autonomic dysfunction; infant constipation and floppy weakness
★ **Bulbar weakness or declining ventilation** → impending respiratory failure even with normal oxygen saturation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: MG: postsynaptic receptor/MuSK autoimmunity; LEMS: presynaptic voltage-gated calcium-channel autoimmunity
Botulinum toxin cleaves SNARE proteins → impaired acetylcholine release

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **AChR antibodies**, then MuSK if negative; repetitive nerve stimulation or single-fiber EMG
MG → chest CT for thymoma; bedside ice-pack improvement supports ocular disease
LEMS → P/Q calcium-channel antibodies and chest CT for cancer
★ Suspected crisis → serial **forced vital capacity/negative inspiratory force**; not pulse oximetry alone
Botulism → serum/stool/toxin testing via public health; treatment before confirmation

rows.label: Tx
items: MG → pyridostigmine, steroid-sparing immunosuppression; thymectomy for thymoma or selected generalized AChR-positive disease
★ Myasthenic crisis → **airway support + IVIG or plasma exchange**, treat precipitant
LEMS → amifampridine and treatment of malignancy; immunotherapy for persistent autoimmune disease
★ Botulism → **heptavalent antitoxin**; infants → human botulism immune globulin; ventilatory support
Wound botulism → debridement/antibiotics; avoid aminoglycosides and magnesium with impaired junctional transmission

rows.label: Complications
items: Aspiration, respiratory arrest; MG immunosuppression → infection; steroids may initially worsen weakness

rows.label: Prevention
items: Review MG-exacerbating drugs; safe food preservation; no honey before age 1 year
LEMS → ongoing cancer surveillance if initial evaluation negative

rows.label: Mimics
items: Guillain-Barré: usually ascending weakness and areflexia, possible sensory symptoms
Brainstem stroke: abrupt focal signs; motor neuron disease: fasciculations/UMN signs

neuromuscular-junction-disorders.evidence: Botulism checked 2026-10-30: [CDC clinical guidelines](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/70/rr/rr7002a1.htm); MG/LEMS: established teaching.

normal-pediatric-variants.name: Normal pediatric variants
normal-pediatric-variants.scope: Thymic sail sign on chest radiograph, physiologic genu varum and valgum, tibial torsion, infantile hemangioma
normal-pediatric-variants.core: Age-appropriate anatomy and growth can resemble disease; symmetry, normal function, and expected evolution support reassurance instead of unnecessary intervention.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Normal skeletal alignment changes with development; familial rotational profiles are common
Infantile hemangiomas more frequent with prematurity, low birth weight and female sex

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Symmetric painless findings with normal growth/function** favor physiologic variation
Asymmetry, pain, progression, short stature or abnormal neurologic examination → pathologic evaluation
Hemangiomas appear in first weeks, proliferate rapidly during infancy, then gradually involute
Periocular, airway/beard-distribution, ulcerating or large segmental lesions are high-risk, not simple cosmetic variants

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Growth remodels lower-limb alignment/rotation; normal thymic tissue may silhouette against the lung
Hemangioma is a benign vascular tumor with proliferative and involution phases, distinct from vascular malformation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical symmetric limb variant → **clinical examination**, growth review and rotational profile
Imaging for red flags, atypical age or suspected metabolic bone disease; not routine physiologic bowing
Typical hemangioma → clinical diagnosis; ≥5 cutaneous lesions → hepatic ultrasound
Large segmental facial/lumbosacral lesion → evaluate associated structural anomalies with specialist guidance

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Reassurance and observation** for physiologic alignment, thymic appearance, toddler genital self-touching without abuse signs
Special shoes/braces do not correct internal tibial torsion; persistent severe functional deformity → orthopedics
★ High-risk hemangioma → **early referral, oral propranolol**; selected superficial lesions → topical timolol
Give propranolol with feeds, hold during poor intake/vomiting; monitor bradycardia and hypoglycemia

rows.label: Complications
items: Unnecessary imaging, bracing or surgery; hemangioma → ulceration, amblyopia, airway obstruction or residual skin change
Multiple hepatic hemangiomas → high-output heart failure or consumptive hypothyroidism

rows.label: Mimics
items: Blount disease: progressive asymmetric tibial bowing; rickets: widened wrists, abnormal mineralization
Mediastinal mass: mass effect/distortion rather than soft thymic contour

normal-pediatric-variants.evidence: Hemangioma guidance checked 2026-10-30: [AAP 2019 guideline](https://publications.aap.org/pediatrics/article/143/1/e20183475/37268/Clinical-Practice-Guideline-for-the-Management-of); skeletal variants: established teaching.

table.title: Expected developmental patterns
rows: Varum to toddler; valgum peaks age 3–4
Yellow papules on erythematous base; trunk, well neonate
Resolves in days; reassure, no cultures
Bilateral nocturnal calf pain; normal exam, massage relieves
Blue hands, feet, perioral; pink mucosa, normal SpO2
Benign, first 24–48 hours; warmer if cold

nutritional-deficiencies.name: Nutritional deficiencies
nutritional-deficiencies.scope: Vegan diet nutrient risks, tea-and-toast diet, vitamin and mineral supplementation, clinical manifestations
nutritional-deficiencies.core: Restricted intake, malabsorption, or increased requirements produce characteristic mucocutaneous, neurologic, hematologic, and skeletal findings; identify the missing nutrient and its cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Unsupplemented vegan diet: B12, iron, calcium, vitamin D, iodine, zinc risks
Tea-and-toast diet, alcohol misuse, food insecurity, restrictive eating, institutionalization
Bariatric surgery, pancreatic insufficiency, cholestasis, bowel disease → specific or fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption

rows.label: Clues
items: Poor wound healing, bruising, oral changes, neuropathy, bone pain; mixed deficiencies commonly coexist
★ **Confusion, ophthalmoplegia, ataxia** in malnutrition → thiamine deficiency; complete triad often absent
Night blindness → vitamin A; bleeding with prolonged PT → vitamin K
Dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia → niacin; periorificial/acral dermatitis, alopecia, dysgeusia → zinc (TPN, penicillamine)

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Insufficient cofactors impair energy metabolism, collagen formation, hematopoiesis, or mineralization
Low intake differs from malabsorption: replacement route and lasting supplementation must match the mechanism
Vitamin D deficiency → ↓calcium absorption → **secondary hyperparathyroidism**: normal calcium at bone's expense

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Diet and supplement history**, weight trend, oral/skin/neurologic examination; assess GI disease
CBC/ferritin, B12 ± methylmalonic acid, 25-OH vitamin D chosen by findings; avoid indiscriminate panels
Albumin is altered by inflammation/fluid status; not a stand-alone nutrition diagnostic test
Severely undernourished → baseline phosphate, Mg, K before nutritional rehabilitation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected Wernicke syndrome → **parenteral thiamine promptly**; do not await laboratory confirmation
B12 deficiency with neurologic signs/malabsorption → parenteral replacement; folate only after B12 assessment
Vitamin D/calcium for deficient intake or osteomalacia; iron replacement with evaluation for blood loss
Vitamin C for scurvy; oral balanced nutrition plus cause-directed supplementation and dietitian support
★ Severe malnutrition → **slow refeeding + thiamine**, close phosphate/K/Mg monitoring and replacement

rows.label: Complications
items: Irreversible B12 neurologic injury, fractures, anemia, infection susceptibility
Refeeding → hypophosphatemia, arrhythmia, respiratory failure; excess vitamin A → hepatotoxicity/teratogenicity

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Vegans → **reliable B12 supplementation**; fortified foods, calcium/vitamin D and iodine adequacy
Diversified diet, food access support, lifelong bariatric follow-up; avoid megadose supplementation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Scurvy versus vasculitis: perifollicular hemorrhage/corkscrew hairs, swollen bleeding gums, restricted produce intake
Hypothyroidism: fatigue and macrocytosis with elevated TSH

nutritional-deficiencies.evidence: Not checked online; established nutritional deficiency and refeeding principles.

obstructive-sleep-apnea.name: Obstructive Sleep Apnea
obstructive-sleep-apnea.scope: risk factors, clinical features (excessive daytime sleepiness, snoring), polysomnography, CPAP, cardiovascular complications
obstructive-sleep-apnea.core: Recurrent upper-airway obstruction during sleep causes intermittent hypoxemia and arousals, often presenting as loud snoring and excessive daytime sleepiness.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, large neck circumference, male sex, aging, retrognathia and upper-airway crowding
Alcohol/sedatives worsen collapse; children often have adenotonsillar hypertrophy; risk rises after menopause

rows.label: Clues
items: Witnessed apneas, gasping/choking, unrefreshing sleep, morning headache, nocturia
Resistant hypertension, atrial fibrillation, secondary polycythemia or recurrent drowsy-driving episodes raise suspicion
Children may show hyperactivity, learning problems, enuresis or poor growth rather than sleepiness
Normal awake oxygen saturation does not exclude severe nocturnal disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Sleep-related reduction in pharyngeal tone collapses vulnerable airway despite persistent respiratory effort
Intermittent hypoxia and sympathetic surges drive hypertension; fragmentation impairs attention and vigilance
Sleep-related hypoventilation with nocturnal hypercapnia → morning headaches

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Polysomnography** confirms; screening tools such as STOP-BANG estimate risk, not diagnosis
Uncomplicated high-risk adults → home sleep apnea test acceptable; negative/inconclusive → in-laboratory study
★ AHI **≥5/hour with symptoms/comorbidity**, or ≥15 regardless of symptoms, establishes adult OSA
AHI 5–14 mild, 15–29 moderate, ≥30 severe; pediatric thresholds differ
Cardiorespiratory disease, suspected hypoventilation, chronic opioids or neuromuscular weakness → laboratory polysomnography

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **CPAP** for symptomatic OSA and most moderate/severe disease; optimize mask fit/adherence
Weight loss, exercise, lateral sleep positioning; avoid bedtime alcohol and sedatives
★ CPAP-intolerant or selected mild/moderate disease → **mandibular advancement device**
Child adenotonsillar hypertrophy → adenotonsillectomy, even with pulmonary hypertension; selected adults → surgery, hypoglossal stimulation
Counsel sleepy patients to avoid driving until controlled; do not rely on stimulants before treating obstruction

rows.label: Complications
items: Systemic hypertension, arrhythmias, stroke risk, pulmonary hypertension in selected patients
Motor vehicle/work accidents, impaired cognition, mood disturbance
Awake postoperative hypercapnia → **CPAP/BiPAP**; reintubate only if obtunded or failing noninvasive support

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain healthy weight, reassess after major weight change; continue PAP around surgery with monitoring

rows.label: Mimics
items: Central apnea: absent respiratory effort during pauses
Narcolepsy: cataplexy and sleep-onset REM features
OHS: persistent daytime hypercapnia

osteoarthritis.name: Osteoarthritis
osteoarthritis.scope: Clinical diagnosis (Heberden/Bouchard nodes, activity-related pain), radiographic findings, nonpharmacologic therapy, oral and topical NSAIDs, injections
osteoarthritis.core: Activity-related joint pain with brief morning stiffness, crepitus and bony enlargement suggests degenerative joint disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, **obesity** (strongest modifiable), prior trauma, malalignment, repetitive occupational loading
Family history, particularly hand disease; obesity affects both mechanical and metabolic risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Morning stiffness generally **<30 minutes**; pain improves with rest early in disease
Knees, hips, first carpometacarpal, DIP and PIP commonly involved; MCP usually spared
Heberden nodes: DIP; Bouchard nodes: PIP; reduced motion and varus/valgus deformity
Hip disease: groin pain with restricted internal rotation; referred pain can localize to knee

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Articular cartilage loss, subchondral remodeling and osteophytes; low-grade synovial inflammation
Joint pain arises from innervated surrounding structures rather than aneural cartilage itself

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical presentation → **clinical diagnosis**; imaging unnecessary for straightforward mild disease
Weight-bearing radiographs if uncertain, severe or worsening: asymmetric joint-space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis/cysts
★ Hot acutely swollen joint → **arthrocentesis**; not an OA flare; mild cool effusion → x-ray, simple analgesic
OA fluid noninflammatory: usually WBC <2000/µL; inflammatory markers generally normal

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First-line **exercise, strengthening, weight loss**; cane contralateral to painful hip/knee
★ Knee/hand pain → **topical diclofenac**; oral NSAID if insufficient and renal/GI/CV risks acceptable
Acetaminophen if unable to use NSAIDs (older exam questions may expect it first); duloxetine for persistent pain
Intra-articular glucocorticoid for short-term relief; avoid routine opioids and hyaluronic acid injections
Severe pain/function loss despite conservative treatment → **joint replacement**

rows.label: Complications
items: Functional limitation, falls, reduced activity and secondary deconditioning
NSAIDs → GI bleeding, AKI, fluid retention; arthroplasty → infection or VTE

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Weight loss** best prevents knee OA, beyond exercise alone; conditioning, injury prevention; no complete joint rest

rows.label: Mimics
items: Rheumatoid arthritis: prolonged stiffness, boggy symmetric MCP/wrist synovitis, marginal erosions, DIP spared
CPPD: acute inflammatory flares, chondrocalcinosis
Septic arthritis: fever, severe painful passive motion, positive synovial culture
Trochanteric bursitis: lateral hip pain over greater trochanter, not groin pain

osteoarthritis.evidence: Not checked online; established ACR/Arthritis Foundation principles.

paget-disease-of-bone.name: Paget disease of bone
paget-disease-of-bone.scope: Osteolytic and osteoblastic phases, elevated alkaline phosphatase, skull and long bone deformities, hearing loss, osteosarcoma risk, bisphosphonates
paget-disease-of-bone.core: An older adult with enlarged or deformed bones and isolated alkaline phosphatase elevation suggests disordered focal bone remodeling.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age >50 years, family history, European ancestry; male predominance
Usually affects pelvis, spine, skull, femur, or tibia; monostotic or polyostotic

rows.label: Clues
items: Often incidental; deep bone pain, local warmth, bowed legs, increasing hat size
★ **Hearing loss** from skull involvement; headache or cranial nerve symptoms
New severe focal pain or enlarging mass in established disease → assess malignant transformation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Excess osteoclast resorption → compensatory disorganized osteoblast activity; lytic, mixed, then sclerotic phases
★ **Mosaic lamellar bone** with cement lines; structurally weak, enlarged, hypervascular tissue

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ALP elevated with normal calcium/phosphate**; GGT helps exclude hepatobiliary source
Plain radiographs: cortical thickening, coarse trabeculae, expansion; skull cotton-wool or long-bone blade-of-grass pattern
★ Confirmed disease → **radionuclide bone scan** maps extent; ALP tracks activity/response
Normal total ALP does not exclude limited disease; bone-specific ALP may help
Biopsy reserved for atypical destructive lesions or suspected sarcoma, not routine diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pain attributable to active disease → **IV zoledronic acid**; oral alendronate alternative
Ensure calcium/vitamin D adequacy and renal assessment before bisphosphonate; avoid with severe renal impairment
Asymptomatic disease → individualized assessment; do not chase ALP normalization without clinical benefit
NSAIDs for coexisting mechanical pain; severe secondary arthritis → joint replacement
Neural compression or unstable fracture → orthopedic/neurosurgical evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Pathologic fractures, secondary osteoarthritis, spinal stenosis or nerve compression
Rare osteosarcoma; extensive hypervascular disease may cause high-output heart failure
Bisphosphonate → acute flu-like reaction, hypocalcemia; rare jaw osteonecrosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: No established primary prevention; fall reduction, mobility support, monitor symptoms and biochemical activity
Reassess unexplained worsening pain rather than assuming persistent benign remodeling

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteomalacia: diffuse pain, low phosphate/vitamin D, insufficiency fractures
Bone metastases: cancer context, focal destructive/sclerotic deposits without typical expansion
Acromegaly: generalized acral/soft-tissue enlargement and elevated IGF-1

palliative-and-hospice-care.name: Palliative and hospice care
palliative-and-hospice-care.scope: Hospice eligibility, pain control, goals of care, surrogate requests
palliative-and-hospice-care.core: Palliative care relieves suffering at any illness stage; hospice centers care on comfort when prognosis and patient goals support a terminal-care benefit.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ **Patient goals and informed consent** guide intervention burdens; symptom relief remains an obligation
Proportionate opioids for pain/dyspnea permissible despite risks; reassess sedation/respiration
Codeine fails → morphine/oxycodone; pain mimics depression; wears off early → shorten interval

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Ask understanding/values → discuss prognosis → recommend a goal-concordant plan
Assess capacity; use advance directive, then authorized surrogate: substituted judgment/best interests
★ Titrate **opioids**, short-acting for breakthrough; constipation → keep dose, add stimulant laxative

rows.label: Don't
items: DNR ≠ no antibiotics, fluids, nutrition or other desired treatment
Capable patient’s informed wishes override surrogate requests
No nonbeneficial interventions; explain reasoning, offer alternatives, seek ethics review for conflict

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Refractory terminal suffering → proportional palliative sedation, specialist review and consent
Emergency, unknown preferences → stabilize while clarifying wishes; honor documented refusals
Advanced dementia refusing intake → comfort hand-feeding by mouth; no tubes or IV

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Hospice: **≤6-month prognosis** if usual course; longer survival permits recertification
Hospice: unrelated conditions remain treatable; no DNR requirement; enrollment revocable if goals change
Cancer pain: escalating requests → tolerance/progression, not addiction; past OUD never limits analgesia

palliative-and-hospice-care.evidence: Eligibility checked 2026-10-30: [CMS hospice benefit](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/payment/fee-for-service-providers/hospice); clinical ethics: established teaching.

table.title: Care settings
rows: Adjust with hospice team; avoid readmission

pancreatitis.name: Pancreatitis
pancreatitis.scope: Acute pancreatitis, chronic pancreatitis, exocrine and endocrine insufficiency
pancreatitis.core: Epigastric pain radiating to the back with pancreatic inflammation may be acute; repeated injury produces irreversible chronic insufficiency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Gallstones (prior postprandial biliary colic), heavy alcohol, triglycerides >1,000 mg/dL, ERCP, hypercalcemia, medications
Chronic: prolonged alcohol/tobacco exposure, genetic disease, duct obstruction, autoimmune disease
Blunt abdominal trauma + epigastric mass/raised enzymes → contrast CT for pancreatic/duodenal injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Severe constant pain, vomiting, tenderness, ileus; chronic disease adds steatorrhea and weight loss
★ **Hypoxemia, hypotension, oliguria, persistent SIRS** → early monitored/ICU assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Premature intrapancreatic enzyme activation → autodigestion and systemic inflammation
Chronic fibrosis destroys acinar/islet tissue: ↓insulin, ↓glucagon, normal insulin sensitivity; lipase may normalize

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Acute diagnosis: **2 of 3**—typical pain, lipase or amylase ≥3× ULN, characteristic imaging
RUQ ultrasound evaluates gallstones; triglycerides, calcium, liver tests identify cause
Contrast CT: diagnostic doubt, high fever/marked leukocytosis (necrosis?), deterioration, no improvement by 48–72 hours; not routine early
Chronic: CT/MRCP shows calcification/duct changes; fecal elastase <200 supports exocrine insufficiency
Recurrent, no gallstones/alcohol → EUS or MRCP for ductal anatomy; older exam questions may expect ERCP

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute: **moderate lactated Ringer resuscitation**, reassessment, IV opioid analgesia, electrolyte correction; avoid overload
★ **Early oral low-fat feeding** by 48 hours if tolerated; else enteral; older exam questions may expect initial bowel rest
Biliary with cholangitis → urgent ERCP; mild gallstone disease → cholecystectomy before discharge
Uncomplicated/sterile: no antibiotics; infected necrosis: penetrating antibiotics, delayed step-up drainage/debridement
Chronic: stop alcohol/tobacco; pancrelipase, fat-soluble vitamins, pain control; islet-loss diabetes → **insulin**, not sulfonylureas

rows.label: Complications
items: ARDS, AKI, shock, hypocalcemia; necrosis, hemorrhage; **splenic vein thrombosis** → isolated gastric varices, normal liver
Pseudocyst after >4 weeks; infected collection, obstruction; chronic disease → pancreatic cancer and brittle diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Treat cause**: gallbladder removal, triglyceride control, avoid culprit drug and alcohol
Post-ERCP rectal indomethacin in eligible patients; selected pancreatic duct stenting

rows.label: Mimics
items: Perforated ulcer: rigid abdomen/free air
Mesenteric ischemia: pain-exam mismatch; MI: ischemic ECG/troponin pattern

table.title: Severity and collections
rows: Transient dysfunction ≤48 hours or local complication

panic-disorder.name: Panic disorder
panic-disorder.scope: Panic attack criteria, unexpected recurrent attacks, agoraphobia, acute abortive therapy, maintenance therapy, medical rule-outs
panic-disorder.core: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks followed by at least 1 month of fear of recurrence or maladaptive behavioral change establish panic disorder.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young adulthood, family history, trauma, anxiety sensitivity
Caffeine, stimulants, cannabis, decongestants, hyperthyroidism, withdrawal can provoke paniclike symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Abrupt intense fear peaks within minutes; palpitations, dyspnea, chest pain, paresthesias, derealization
Attack requires ≥4 characteristic symptoms; fear of dying/losing control common
★ **Syncope, exertional onset, hypoxemia, focal findings**, sustained arrhythmia → medical cause until evaluated
Agoraphobia: fear/avoidance of ≥2 situations where escape/help seems difficult, persisting ≥6 months

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Threat-circuit overactivation and catastrophic interpretation of benign sensations amplify autonomic symptoms
Hyperventilation lowers CO₂ → lightheadedness, perioral/distal tingling; avoidance reinforces anticipatory fear
**Sodium lactate infusion** provokes attacks: heightened panic sensitivity

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis after medical/substance review**; unexpected episodes distinguish disorder from predictable triggers
Vital signs, examination, ECG for cardiopulmonary symptoms; glucose/TSH or toxicology guided by history
Chest pain risk → ACS/PE evaluation rather than automatic psychiatric attribution
Assess depression, suicidality, substance use; agoraphobia may be diagnosed separately

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ During attack → **calm reassurance, slow breathing**, reduce stimulation after excluding danger
Severe acute episode → short-term lorazepam when needed; avoid with sedatives or substance-use risk
★ Maintenance → **CBT with interoceptive exposure and/or SSRI**, such as sertraline
Start SSRI low, titrate slowly; benefit takes weeks; venlafaxine alternative
Continue effective treatment after remission, then gradual taper; benzodiazepines not preferred long-term

rows.label: Complications
items: Agoraphobic avoidance, impaired function, depression, self-medication with alcohol
Benzodiazepine dependence/withdrawal; alprazolam → **between-dose rebound anxiety**; SSRIs may initially increase anxiety

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Reduce caffeine/stimulants**, regular sleep/exercise, practice exposure and relapse-prevention skills
Paper-bag rebreathing discouraged (hypoxemia risk); older exam questions may expect it if SpO₂ normal

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hyperthyroidism: persistent tremor, heat intolerance, low TSH
SVT: documented abrupt regular tachycardia, not solely subjective palpitations
Social anxiety: fear tied to scrutiny rather than unexpected attacks
Mitral valve prolapse: incidental click/murmur; doesn't explain recurrent attacks with fear of recurrence

panic-disorder.evidence: Not checked online; established DSM-5-TR and anxiety treatment teaching.

parasitic-infections.name: Parasitic infections
parasitic-infections.scope: Strongyloidiasis, giardiasis, amebiasis, cryptosporidiosis, ascariasis, schistosomiasis, pinworm (enterobiasis), cysticercosis, eosinophilia workup, antiparasitic therapy
parasitic-infections.core: Exposure, organ pattern, and immune status identify the parasite; eosinophilia favors tissue-invasive helminths rather than intestinal protozoa.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Contaminated food/water, endemic travel, freshwater contact, barefoot soil exposure, household crowding
Steroids/HTLV-1 predispose to Strongyloides hyperinfection; advanced HIV predisposes to persistent cryptosporidiosis

rows.label: Clues
items: Ascariasis: transient cough/eosinophilic infiltrates during larval migration; later intestinal or biliary obstruction
Pinworm: nocturnal perianal/vulvar itch, dysuria with normal UA; household clustering
Cysticercosis: seizures or hydrocephalus; ingestion of **T. solium eggs**, not pork cysts
Cutaneous larva migrans: soil contact; pruritic **serpiginous tracks**; animal hookworm larvae → albendazole or ivermectin

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Giardia blunts microvilli → **fat/carbohydrate malabsorption**; invasive protozoa can affect liver, urinary tract, or CNS
Strongyloides autoinfection permits lifelong persistence and dissemination after immunosuppression

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Unexplained **eosinophilia** → travel/drug history, serial stool O&P, targeted Strongyloides serology
★ Steroids + eosinophilia or infiltrates → **Strongyloides hyperinfection**: **duodenal aspirate** larvae; stool O&P often misses
Diarrhea → stool antigen/PCR for protozoa; single routine O&P can miss infection
★ Pinworm → **morning tape test** before washing; stool testing insensitive
Brain MRI/CT for cysticercosis; eye examination before antiparasitics; assess lesion viability and location

rows.label: Tx
items: Rehydrate; ascariasis → albendazole; bowel obstruction → surgical evaluation before deworming
Pinworm → albendazole, mebendazole, or pyrantel; repeat after **2 weeks**, treat household simultaneously
★ Viable parenchymal cysticercosis → albendazole ± praziquantel with corticosteroids; seizures → levetiracetam
Calcified brain lesions → no antiparasitic; hydrocephalus → neurosurgical control before cysticidal treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Strongyloides hyperinfection → gram-negative sepsis, respiratory failure; eosinophilia may disappear
Amebic liver abscess; schistosomiasis → portal hypertension or bladder squamous carcinoma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Screen/treat Strongyloides before **immunosuppression** after endemic exposure
Safe water, sanitation, handwashing, footwear; avoid endemic freshwater and untreated swimming water
Neurocysticercosis household contacts → **stool O&P** to find egg-shedding T. solium tapeworm carrier

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBD: chronic inflammatory diarrhea after infection excluded
Drug hypersensitivity: eosinophilia linked to new medication, rash or organ injury

table.title: Exposure → diagnosis and treatment
rows: Camping; greasy stool, bloating; stool antigen
Dysentery, flask-shaped ulcers; stool PCR; abscess → serology
Soil; larva currens, larvae in stool
Ivermectin; hyperinfection requires prolonged daily treatment
Freshwater; hematuria (haematobium), portal fibrosis (mansoni/japonicum); eggs, serology
Confirmed E. histolytica without invasive disease

penile-cancer.name: Penile cancer
penile-cancer.scope: Squamous cell carcinoma of the penis, risk factors (uncircumcised, HPV, smoking, poor hygiene), painless ulcer, inguinal lymphadenopathy, biopsy, staging and penectomy
penile-cancer.core: A persistent penile ulcer or exophytic lesion warrants tissue diagnosis; local invasion and inguinal nodal status determine treatment and prognosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **HPV**, smoking, phimosis, chronic inflammation, poor genital hygiene
Uncircumcised status, older age, lichen sclerosus; circumcision lowers risk but is not complete protection

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually painless, nonhealing ulcer, plaque, or fungating growth on glans/prepuce
Bleeding, malodorous discharge, lesion hidden beneath phimotic foreskin
★ Palpable **inguinal nodes** may be metastatic or reactive; persistent suspicion requires sampling
Advanced disease: corporal invasion, urinary obstruction, fixed groin masses

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Usually squamous cell carcinoma; HPV-associated and chronic-inflammatory pathways
Lymphatic spread → superficial/deep inguinal nodes → pelvic nodes → distant organs

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Biopsy** suspicious lesion for histology and depth; inspect entire penis and both groins
MRI when corporal invasion or feasibility of organ preservation uncertain
Suspicious nodes → ultrasound-guided FNA/core biopsy; negative result with persistent concern → repeat evaluation
High-risk clinically node-negative disease → sentinel node biopsy; CT misses micrometastases
Clinically positive nodes → CT/PET-CT for pelvic and distant staging; nodes strongest prognostic factor

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Superficial/localized lesions → organ-preserving excision or glansectomy when clear margins achievable
Biopsy-confirmed in situ disease → topical 5-fluorouracil/imiquimod or selected laser/excision
★ Cavernosal invasion → **partial penectomy**; extensive unresectable local preservation → total penectomy
Regional metastases → inguinal lymphadenectomy; bulky/fixed nodes → cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy
Do not delay suspicious-node staging with empiric antibiotics unless clinical infection present

rows.label: Complications
items: Local recurrence, metastatic progression, fistula, urinary obstruction
Surgery: sexual dysfunction, body-image distress; lymphadenectomy: lymphedema, wound complications

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **HPV vaccination**; stop tobacco use; clean beneath foreskin; treat chronic inflammatory lesions
Post-treatment examination of penis and groins; teach self-examination and prompt reporting of changes

rows.label: Mimics
items: Primary syphilis: chancre plus positive serology; may still require biopsy if atypical
Genital herpes: painful grouped vesicles/ulcers
Condyloma: verrucous HPV wart without invasive histology

penile-disorders.name: Penile disorders
penile-disorders.scope: Phimosis, paraphimosis, balanitis and posthitis, priapism (ischemic vs nonischemic), Peyronie disease, penile fracture (tunica albuginea rupture, emergent surgical repair)
penile-disorders.core: Trapped foreskin, painful rigid erection lasting over 4 hours, or a snap with immediate detumescence → urologic emergency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Paraphimosis after catheterization or examination. Balanoposthitis with diabetes, irritants, poor hygiene
Ischemic priapism: sickle cell disease, trazodone, intracavernosal vasoactive drugs. Nonischemic: perineal trauma

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Paraphimosis: **edematous glans** distal to a constricting ring. Dusky glans → threatened perfusion
Ischemic priapism: rigid corpora with relatively soft glans. Nonischemic: partial rigidity, little pain
Peyronie: palpable plaque, acquired curvature on erection. Fracture: rapid swelling and ecchymosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Ischemic priapism: trapped venous blood. Nonischemic: unregulated arterial inflow through fistula
Peyronie: tunical fibrosis. Penile fracture: **tunica albuginea rupture**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Priapism → **cavernosal blood gas**: hypoxia, hypercapnia, acidosis in ischemia. Unclear subtype → duplex
Equivocal fracture → US. Meatal blood, gross hematuria or retention → urethrogram or cystoscopy
Recurrent balanoposthitis → assess for diabetes. Persistent atypical erosion or plaque → biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Paraphimosis → compress edema and manually reduce. Failure → **dorsal slit**
★ Ischemic → **aspiration plus intracavernosal phenylephrine** with BP/pulse monitoring. Refractory → distal shunt
Nonischemic → observe initially. Persistent and bothersome → selective arterial embolization
★ Penile fracture → **immediate surgical exploration and repair**
Peyronie → NSAID for active pain. Stable bothersome curvature → selected collagenase or surgery

rows.label: Complications
items: Paraphimosis → glans necrosis. Delayed ischemic priapism or fracture repair → erectile dysfunction

rows.label: Prevention
items: Replace foreskin after catheter placement or hygiene. Avoid forced retraction in children
Balanoposthitis recurrence: gentle cleansing with water, avoid irritant soaps

rows.label: Mimics
items: Dorsal penile vein rupture: ecchymosis with gradual detumescence
Congenital penile curvature: lifelong curvature without palpable plaque

penile-disorders.evidence: Checked AUA priapism, urotrauma and Peyronie guidance, EAU foreskin guidance and IUSTI balanoposthitis guidance, Nov 2026.

perioperative-care.name: Perioperative care
perioperative-care.scope: Preoperative cardiac risk, pulmonary evaluation, surgical antibiotic prophylaxis, medication management, pain control
perioperative-care.core: Optimize active disease, estimate procedural and patient risk, and order testing only when the result could change perioperative management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **MI within 60 days**, decompensated HF → highest perioperative cardiac risk; older exam questions may expect MI within 6 months
Emergency, vascular or intrathoracic surgery; ischemic heart disease, heart failure, CKD, diabetes
Smoking, COPD, OSA, frailty, malnutrition and prior anesthesia complications

rows.label: Clues
items: Chest pain, new dyspnea, syncope or decompensated fluid overload require targeted evaluation
Poor functional capacity: inability to climb stairs or perform activities around 4 METs

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Surgical stress raises myocardial oxygen demand; anesthesia can lower perfusion pressure
Sedation, pain and recumbency reduce ventilation and promote atelectasis and venous stasis
Surgical stress, pain, opioids → nonosmotic **ADH** release → transient oliguria with normal renal function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **RCRI/NSQIP** plus functional assessment; no routine stress test for low-risk surgery
Elevated risk, poor/unknown capacity → stress test if management changes; cannot exercise → **pharmacologic stress imaging**
ECG for cardiovascular symptoms; echo for new/worsening HF or suspected significant valve disease
No routine chest radiograph/spirometry without respiratory findings; assess airway and OSA history
Lung resection: **predicted postoperative FEV1** best predictor of complications; predicted postoperative FEV1 <30–40% → high risk, exercise testing before deciding

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Active ACS, decompensated HF or unstable arrhythmia → defer elective surgery and stabilize
★ Continue chronic **beta blockers/statins**; do not start beta blockade on surgery day
Hold **SGLT2 inhibitors 3–4 days**; individualize GLP-1 drugs by aspiration risk; continue reduced basal insulin
★ **Cefazolin within 60 minutes** before incision; MRSA or severe beta-lactam allergy → vancomycin within 120 minutes
Multimodal analgesia: acetaminophen, regional block, selective NSAID; add opioid by severity, respiratory monitoring

rows.label: Complications
items: Myocardial injury, AKI, delirium, pneumonia, VTE and surgical-site infection
Opioids aggravate OSA; excessive fluids can worsen pulmonary edema
New postoperative dyspnea, ↓basal breath sounds → chest radiograph first, before PE imaging or heparin

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, lung expansion exercises, early mobilization, mechanical/pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis
Anticoagulation interruption individualized; bridging reserved for highest thrombotic risk
Chronic steroid exposure with adrenal suppression → perioperative glucocorticoid coverage
Usable gut → **enteral feeding**, including distal jejunostomy, over TPN

rows.label: Mimics
items: Anxiety-related dyspnea: normal cardiopulmonary evaluation
Stable chronic disease: baseline symptoms alone do not mandate cancellation

table.title: Postoperative pain
rows: Severe pain after major abdominal surgery

personality-disorders.name: Personality disorders
personality-disorders.scope: Cluster A (paranoid, schizoid, schizotypal), Cluster B (borderline, antisocial, histrionic, narcissistic), Cluster C (avoidant, dependent, OCPD), dialectical behavior therapy
personality-disorders.core: Enduring, inflexible patterns of cognition, affect, relationships, or impulse control cause impairment across settings beginning by adolescence or early adulthood.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Temperament, genetic susceptibility, early adversity and disrupted attachment; avoid attributing diagnosis to trauma alone
Traits must exceed cultural expectations; diagnose cautiously during acute illness or developmental transitions

rows.label: Clues
items: Cluster A: paranoid—distrust; schizoid—detachment; schizotypal—magical thinking, odd speech/perceptions, social discomfort
Cluster B: antisocial—violations of rights; histrionic—attention seeking; narcissistic—grandiosity/entitlement
Cluster C: avoidant—fears rejection/embarrassment, avoids new activities; dependent—clinging; OCPD—rigid perfectionism, control
★ Borderline: **splitting, unstable identity/relationships, self-harm**, abandonment fear, chronic emptiness, impulsivity

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Maladaptive trait patterns impair emotion regulation and interpersonal functioning; no diagnostic biomarker
Impulsive aggression, violent suicide → **low CSF 5-HIAA** (serotonin metabolite)

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Longitudinal clinical assessment** across contexts; obtain collateral with consent
Exclude mood episodes, psychotic illness, substances, neurodevelopmental disorders and acquired brain disease
★ Antisocial diagnosis requires **age ≥18 plus conduct disorder before 15**
Borderline may cause brief stress-related paranoia/dissociation; sustained psychosis requires broader evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Borderline → **dialectical behavior therapy**; structured psychotherapy and consistent team boundaries
Trait-matched psychotherapy, e.g., avoidant → **CBT**, assertiveness training; clear expectations, empathic, nonpunitive tone
No medication treats personality disorder globally; target comorbid depression/anxiety or limited severe symptoms
Self-harm threats → assess intent, plan, access and safety; imminent risk → emergency psychiatric care
Avoid staff splitting through shared care plans; avoid reflexive long-term benzodiazepines in impulsive patients

rows.label: Complications
items: Self-injury/suicide, substance misuse, impaired work/relationships; antisocial traits → legal or violence consequences
Stigma and inconsistent treatment worsen engagement; therapeutic ruptures require careful repair

rows.label: Mimics
items: Autism: early developmental social-communication differences and restricted interests
Delusional disorder: fixed delusion rather than generalized suspicious personality style

personality-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

table.title: Common diagnostic confusions
rows: Reactive hours-long shifts vs sustained mood episodes
Odd beliefs vs persistent frank psychosis

physician-patient-communication.name: Physician-patient communication
physician-patient-communication.scope: Medical interpreters, limited English proficiency, delivering bad news, empathetic communication, family requests to withhold information
physician-patient-communication.core: Respect autonomy through understandable, honest, empathic dialogue; identify what patients understand and want before sharing decisions or sensitive information.

rows.label: Principle
items: Confidentiality, cultural humility, informed choice; language barriers never imply impaired capacity
Patient preferences determine family involvement and desired level of disclosure
**Comprehensive, contextual care**: whole-person, longitudinal; tailored to culture, family, goals

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Qualified medical interpreter**, free to patient; speak directly to patient in short segments
★ Bad news: privacy → understanding/preferences → warning → plain disclosure → empathy → plan
Validate emotion; open questions, silence, teach-back; explore beliefs before correcting misinformation

rows.label: Don't
items: Avoid jargon, false reassurance, interrupting, arguing, blaming, or premature advice
Avoid routine reliance on children/family for interpreting consent or sensitive discussions
Avoid promising cure or confidentiality beyond legal limits

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ **Family requests nondisclosure → ask patient privately**; patient preferences control disclosure
Capable patient may decline details or designate another recipient; document preference
Emergency without interpreter → temporary available help while securing qualified interpretation

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Therapeutic privilege is narrow**; anticipated distress alone never justifies withholding diagnosis
Anger → acknowledge concern, clarify cause, establish boundaries if threatening; no reflex discharge
Requested adult-family interpreter → verify suitability/privacy/voluntariness; offer professional

table.title: Difficult conversations
rows: Pause; allow feelings; schedule prompt follow-up
Voice openly in patient's presence; no covert action
Capable patient hides news from family
Encourage support; respect privacy; never lie to family
Child asks prognosis, parents forbid disclosure
Explore understanding; encourage talking with parents; never lie
Negotiate adherence contract; punitive control backfires
Fluent bilingual staff acceptable; never a child

physician-patient-communication.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [HHS interpreter guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/civil-rights/for-individuals/faqs/may-an-lep-person-use-a-family-member-as-an-interpreter/index.html); established autonomy and bad-news communication principles.

pleural-effusion.name: Pleural effusion
pleural-effusion.scope: Transudate vs exudate (Light criteria), parapneumonic effusion, empyema, malignant effusion
pleural-effusion.core: Fluid in the pleural space causes dyspnea, dullness, and reduced breath sounds; classify by mechanism and identify infection requiring drainage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Heart failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome; pneumonia, malignancy, pulmonary embolism, TB
Recent thoracic surgery, pancreatitis, esophageal rupture, autoimmune disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Pleuritic pain, reduced fremitus; large effusion shifts mediastinum away; unilateral + cancer history → malignant
Fever or persistent sepsis despite antibiotics suggests complicated parapneumonic fluid/empyema
Bloody fluid: malignancy (prior cancer, mediastinal mass), embolism, trauma; milky → chyle
Foul-smelling pus after aspiration → **anaerobic empyema**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transudate: altered hydrostatic/oncotic pressure; exudate: increased permeability or impaired lymphatic drainage
Heart-failure transudate: pleural protein <3 g/dL, low LDH and cell count; **glucose equals serum**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Chest radiograph → **ultrasound-guided thoracentesis** for new unexplained, unilateral, or atypical effusion
Classic bilateral heart-failure effusions → diuresis first; sample if fever, asymmetry, or treatment failure
★ **Exudate if any Light criterion** positive; compare paired pleural and serum measurements
Pleural pH, glucose, cell differential, Gram stain/culture; cytology if cancer suspected
Diuresis can create pseudoexudate; serum–pleural albumin gradient >1.2 g/dL supports transudate

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat systemic cause; therapeutic thoracentesis for significant symptoms; avoid rapid excessive drainage
★ Pus, positive Gram stain/culture, **pH <7.20** or glucose <60 → empyema/complicated: chest tube, antibiotics
Loculated infected fluid → intrapleural tPA/DNase; persistent sepsis → VATS evaluation
★ Recurrent symptomatic malignancy → **indwelling pleural catheter** or pleurodesis; trapped lung favors catheter

rows.label: Complications
items: Empyema, loculation, trapped lung, respiratory compromise
Thoracentesis → pneumothorax, bleeding, reexpansion pulmonary edema

rows.label: Prevention
items: Heart-failure control, prompt pneumonia treatment; ultrasound guidance reduces procedural injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atelectasis: mediastinal shift toward volume loss
Consolidation: increased fremitus, bronchial breath sounds
Pneumothorax: hyperresonance rather than dullness

pleural-effusion.evidence: Not checked online; established pleural disease teaching.

pneumonia.name: Pneumonia
pneumonia.scope: Community-acquired, hospital-acquired, ventilator-associated, aspiration, atypical pneumonia (Legionella, Mycoplasma)
pneumonia.core: Acute lower respiratory infection with a new infiltrate; severity, acquisition setting, and resistance risks determine disposition and empiric antibiotics.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, COPD, age, immunosuppression
Dysphagia, absent gag/cough (stroke, dementia, Parkinson), impaired consciousness → aspiration
HAP ≥48 hours hospitalized; VAP ≥48 hours after intubation
Prior MRSA/Pseudomonas isolation or recent hospitalization with IV antibiotics → resistant pathogens

rows.label: Clues
items: Fever, cough, sputum, focal crackles; older adults: confusion; children: lower-lobe disease may refer abdominal pain
★ Severe: **hypoxemia, hypotension, tachypnea**, multilobar disease; ventilation or pressors → ICU
Legionella: water exposure, diarrhea, hyponatremia; Mycoplasma: school-age/young adult, indolent dry cough, cold agglutinins
Immunocompromised, diffuse bilateral interstitial/alveolar infiltrates, exertional hypoxemia → **Pneumocystis**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alveolar inflammation/exudate → shunt and impaired oxygenation
Chemical aspiration pneumonitis: sterile gastric injury; severity tracks **volume and acidity**; rapid improvement possible

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CXR** first; CT if strong suspicion despite nondiagnostic radiograph
**CURB-65** 0–1 or low PSI → outpatient; severe CAP → blood/sputum cultures, Legionella antigen ± PCR
Low procalcitonin alone does not justify withholding initial antibiotics in radiographically confirmed bacterial CAP
Gram-positive lancet diplococci → **S pneumoniae**: commonest CAP; lobar consolidation, high fever, often post-viral URI
Small gram-negative coccobacilli, smoker/COPD → **H influenzae**

rows.label: Tx
items: Oxygen, fluids for hypoperfusion; drain empyema; narrow antibiotics to cultures
★ Aspiration pneumonia: usual CAP coverage; **add anaerobic coverage only for abscess/empyema**
Anaerobes: **ampicillin-sulbactam**; older exam questions may expect **clindamycin**, even without abscess
Stable nonsevere CAP: ATS 2025 permits 3–4 days; classic ≥5-day rule remains for severe disease
★ Severe noninfluenza CAP → consider **systemic corticosteroids**; nonsevere CAP → avoid routine steroids

rows.label: Complications
items: Parapneumonic effusion, empyema, bacteremia, respiratory failure, sepsis
S aureus: postinfluenza necrotizing pneumonia; child failing amoxicillin, dense consolidation/effusion
Aspiration (alcoholism, intubation) → **lung abscess**: dependent-segment cavity, air-fluid level, foul sputum
Antibiotic exposure → C difficile

rows.label: Prevention
items: Influenza/pneumococcal vaccination, smoking cessation, swallowing evaluation
Aspiration/VAP prevention: head elevation 30–45°, oral care, early liberation from ventilation

rows.label: Mimics
items: PE: thrombotic risk, pleuritic pain, no infectious source
HF: bilateral edema, elevated JVP, cardiac dysfunction

table.title: Empiric adult regimens
rows: Amoxicillin/clavulanate + azithromycin; doxycycline alternative; or levofloxacin
Antipseudomonal: cefepime, ceftazidime, or piperacillin/tazobactam; usually 7 days

population-health-and-quality-improvemen.name: Population health and quality improvement
population-health-and-quality-improvemen.scope: Program evaluation, outcome and process measures, health equity, PDSA cycles
population-health-and-quality-improvemen.core: Improve care for a defined population through measurable aims, iterative system changes, and attention to unequal access and outcomes.

rows.label: Principle
items: Population denominator includes eligible people missing visits, not only those receiving care
Equity: stratify outcomes by language, race/ethnicity, geography, disability, insurance, deprivation
Greater relative **primary care investment** improves population health, reduces disparities

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Define **measurable aim**, population, baseline, timeframe; engage patients/frontline staff
★ **PDSA**: plan small change → do → study results → act/adapt before scaling
Stratify measures, address interpreter/transport/cost barriers, monitor unintended consequences

rows.label: Don't
items: Do not assume a favorable outcome proves causation without comparison and context
Avoid blaming individuals for failures created by unreliable workflows

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Run/control charts distinguish routine common-cause variation from special-cause signals over time
Program evaluation: reach, fidelity, effectiveness, cost, sustainability versus original goals
Education program → measure knowledge/behavior change; small cohort cannot detect morbidity/mortality

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Process success ≠ patient benefit**; assess both and choose valid denominators
★ **Risk adjustment** improves comparison; also report disparities so adjustment cannot conceal inequity
Before–after improvement may reflect secular trends, case-mix change, regression to mean

population-health-and-quality-improvemen.evidence: Established quality-improvement and program-evaluation principles; no guideline-dependent thresholds.

post-traumatic-stress-disorder.name: Post-traumatic stress disorder
post-traumatic-stress-disorder.scope: PTSD diagnostic criteria (>1 month: intrusion, avoidance, negative mood/cognition, hyperarousal), acute stress disorder (<1 month), trauma-focused psychotherapy (CBT, EMDR), SSRIs, prazosin for nightmares
post-traumatic-stress-disorder.core: Persistent trauma-linked reexperiencing and avoidance with altered mood and heightened arousal cause functional impairment beyond the immediate stress response.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Exposure to actual/threatened death, serious injury or sexual violence; direct, witnessed, or qualifying indirect exposure
Prior trauma, psychiatric illness, repeated exposure, poor social support

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Intrusion**: nightmares, flashbacks, distress with reminders; avoidance of internal/external cues
Negative beliefs, guilt, detachment or trauma amnesia; hypervigilance, exaggerated startle, sleep disturbance
Dissociative subtype: depersonalization or derealization; severe distress may coexist with suicidality

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Persistent dysregulated threat response and impaired contextual extinction of traumatic fear

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical: ≥1 intrusion, ≥1 avoidance, ≥2 negative mood/cognition, ≥2 arousal symptoms
**>1 month**, impairment, and not better explained by substances or another illness
Assess ongoing danger, self-harm risk, substance use, depression and traumatic brain injury

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First-line **trauma-focused psychotherapy**: prolonged exposure, cognitive processing therapy, or EMDR
★ If medication preferred/needed → **sertraline, paroxetine, or venlafaxine**; premature ejaculation → paroxetine (delays ejaculation)
Prazosin for persistent trauma nightmares; monitor orthostatic hypotension, not an overall PTSD treatment
Avoid benzodiazepines; no established benefit and increased dependence risk
Immediate safety planning and psychiatric hospitalization when imminent self-harm or inability to remain safe

rows.label: Complications
items: Depression, substance use disorders, suicide risk, relationship and occupational impairment

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early practical support, **psychoeducation normalizing trauma reactions**; symptomatic acute stress → trauma-focused CBT
Avoid compulsory single-session psychological debriefing; maintain supportive follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: Adjustment disorder: stress-related distress without required trauma or full PTSD syndrome
Panic disorder: unexpected attacks without obligatory trauma-linked symptoms

table.title: Time course
rows: Full criteria first met ≥6 months later

postpartum-care.name: Postpartum care
postpartum-care.scope: Normal puerperal changes, lochia, uterine involution, perineal and cesarean wound healing, breastfeeding, postpartum depression screening, routine postpartum visit
postpartum-care.core: Postpartum care is an ongoing assessment of recovery, mood, infant feeding, contraception, and chronic disease after every birth.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ All postpartum patients; assess support, sleep, safety, sexual health, and reproductive goals

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Contact within **3 weeks**; comprehensive visit by **12 weeks**, with earlier risk-based review
Hypertensive disorder → BP within 7–10 days; severe hypertension → within 72 hours

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Edinburgh or PHQ-9 depression screen; assess suicidality directly after positive self-harm response
BP, bleeding, fundal tenderness; inspect perineum/incision for erythema, drainage, separation
Observe latch/milk transfer; frequent feeds, lactation support; cracked nipples → correct positioning

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Heavy bleeding (pad soaked <1 hour), fever, dyspnea, severe headache → urgent evaluation
Mood screen positive → diagnostic interview, psychotherapy/SSRI; psychosis → emergency hospitalization
Increasing wound pain/purulence → evaluate infection; breast fluctuance → ultrasound for abscess

rows.label: Traps
items: Ovulation may precede first period; discuss contraception before discharge
Lactational contraception: amenorrhea, exclusive frequent breastfeeding, infant <6 months
Postpartum hypertension and cardiomyopathy can first appear after discharge

table.title: Expected recovery
rows: Red rubra → pink serosa → white/yellow alba
Descends daily; near prepregnancy size by 6 weeks
Pain improves; pulling normal if intact; keep clean
Early cramping and fluid loss; breastfeeding intensifies cramping

postpartum-care.evidence: Visit timing checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG postpartum care](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2018/05/optimizing-postpartum-care); normal physiology established teaching.

postpartum-hemorrhage.name: Postpartum hemorrhage
postpartum-hemorrhage.scope: Primary postpartum hemorrhage (uterine atony, lacerations, retained placenta, coagulopathy), secondary postpartum hemorrhage (retained products of conception, endometritis), barrier methods, surgical management
postpartum-hemorrhage.core: Excessive bleeding after delivery demands simultaneous resuscitation and cause-directed control: Tone, Trauma, Tissue and Thrombin.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Uterine overdistention, prolonged/augmented labor, chorioamnionitis, magnesium, prior PPH → atony
Operative delivery → trauma; placenta accreta/retention → tissue; abruption/sepsis → coagulopathy

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Boggy enlarged uterus** → atony; firm uterus with bleeding → laceration or other cause
Jagged/incomplete placenta, vessels to membrane edge (**succenturiate lobe**) → retained tissue; oozing → coagulopathy
Shock exceeding visible loss → concealed hematoma; post-cesarean distention, hematocrit drop → **intra-abdominal hemorrhage**
Delayed bleeding >24 hours to weeks postpartum → retained products, endometritis or subinvolution

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Myometrial contraction compresses placental-bed vessels; failed contraction or disrupted tissue prevents hemostasis
Vulvar hematoma: **pudendal artery** branch, often operative delivery; vaginal/uterine arteries → deep or retroperitoneal

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Quantify blood loss; US definition **≥1000 mL or hypovolemia within 24 hours**, regardless of route
WHO 2025 earlier treatment trigger: ≥500 mL, or ≥300 mL with abnormal hemodynamic signs
Assess uterine tone, inspect birth canal/placenta; CBC, coagulation studies, fibrinogen and crossmatch
Ultrasound for suspected retained products; avoid delaying control in active unstable bleeding
Inversion: round fleshy introitus mass after cord traction, absent abdominal fundus, shock

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Hemorrhage team, two large IVs, warmed balanced blood resuscitation; massage, empty bladder, **oxytocin**
★ **Tranexamic acid within 3 hours** alongside first-response treatment
Refractory atony → **balloon/vacuum**, embolization if stable; compression sutures/arterial ligation or hysterectomy
Laceration → repair; retained tissue → evacuation; inversion → manual replacement before uterotonics
Endometritis → **clindamycin + gentamicin**

rows.label: Complications
items: DIC, AKI, shock, death; severe ischemia → Sheehan syndrome
Transfusion complications and hysterectomy-related fertility loss; delayed anemia impairs recovery

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Prophylactic **oxytocin after delivery**, active third-stage management and antenatal anemia treatment
Risk assessment, blood availability and team readiness; routine prophylactic TXA not recommended for vaginal birth

rows.label: Mimics
items: Amniotic fluid embolism: sudden hypoxia/collapse with DIC
Pulmonary embolism: hypoxia/chest pain without primary uterine blood loss

prelabor-rupture-of-membranes.name: Prelabor rupture of membranes
prelabor-rupture-of-membranes.scope: Term PROM (induction vs expectant), PPROM (<34 weeks), latency antibiotics, antenatal corticosteroids, magnesium sulfate neuroprotection, complications (chorioamnionitis, placental abruption, pulmonary hypoplasia)
prelabor-rupture-of-membranes.core: Membrane rupture before labor: term PROM favors induction; stable early PPROM favors monitored pregnancy prolongation with infection prevention and fetal maturation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Previous PPROM/preterm birth, genital infection, smoking, short cervix, uterine overdistension

rows.label: Clues
items: Sudden gush or persistent watery leakage; reduced fluid volume may develop
★ Fever, uterine tenderness, fetal tachycardia → **intra-amniotic infection**; pain/bleeding → possible abruption

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Membrane weakening permits fluid loss and ascending infection; latency inversely related to gestational age

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Sterile speculum examination**: pooling or fluid leaking from cervical os
Nitrazine alkaline pH and ferning support diagnosis; blood, semen, vaginitis cause false-positive pH
Equivocal → amniotic protein assay; ultrasound supports, never independently confirms rupture
★ Avoid **digital cervical examinations** unless delivery imminent; assess fetal status and presentation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Infection, fetal compromise, significant abruption, or prolapsed cord → **deliver regardless of gestational age**
Expectant <34 weeks → 7-day latency antibiotics: IV ampicillin/erythromycin then oral amoxicillin/erythromycin
Azithromycin may replace erythromycin; avoid amoxicillin-clavulanate because neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis risk
Preterm birth expected → complete **betamethasone ×2, 24 hours apart**; magnesium sulfate if birth <32 weeks
GBS-positive/unknown-risk labor → penicillin; avoid late-preterm latency antibiotics and prolonged tocolysis

rows.label: Complications
items: Maternal/neonatal infection, prematurity, placental abruption, cord compression/prolapse
Early prolonged rupture → pulmonary hypoplasia and limb contractures

rows.label: Prevention
items: Stop smoking, treat identified infections, manage short cervix/prior preterm birth risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Urinary leakage: urine odor, no pooling/ferning
Physiologic leukorrhea: nonwatery discharge without amniotic-fluid markers

table.title: Stable PROM without delivery indication
rows: Oxytocin induction; brief expectant option after counseling
Delivery or expectant management; stop expectance by 37
Individualized counseling: termination versus expectance, maternal risks

primary-immunodeficiencies.name: Primary immunodeficiencies
primary-immunodeficiencies.scope: Selective IgA deficiency, common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), X-linked agammaglobulinemia, severe combined immunodeficiency, hyper-IgE syndrome, Wiskott-Aldrich, chronic granulomatous disease
primary-immunodeficiencies.core: Recurrent, unusually severe, persistent, or opportunistic infections; organism pattern and age of onset localize the immune defect.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Consanguinity, affected relatives, male relatives dying in infancy; absent family history does not exclude disease

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Failure to thrive, chronic diarrhea, persistent thrush, or infections across multiple organ systems
Deep abscesses suggest phagocyte dysfunction; recurrent encapsulated bacteria suggest impaired antibody function

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Selective IgA deficiency: impaired mucosal defense; respiratory infections, giardiasis, atopy, or no symptoms
Antibody disorders impair opsonization; T-cell defects permit viral, fungal, and protozoal opportunists
DiGeorge: 3rd/4th **pharyngeal pouch** failure → absent thymus, hypocalcemia, conotruncal defects, T-cell infections
ADA deficiency: autosomal recessive SCID; toxic deoxyadenosine destroys T and B cells

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Start **CBC with differential, quantitative immunoglobulins**, HIV testing; assess vaccine antibody responses
Lymphocyte subsets distinguish B-cell and T-cell deficiencies; abnormal results → genetic confirmation
IgA deficiency: isolated IgA <7 mg/dL after age 4 years; normal IgG and IgM
★ Newborn **TREC screen** detects impaired T-cell production before symptomatic SCID

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Profound combined immune failure → isolation, irradiated CMV-negative blood products, urgent **transplant evaluation**
Acute infections: organism-directed antimicrobials; immunoglobulin replacement not useful for isolated IgA deficiency

rows.label: Complications
items: Bronchiectasis, chronic enteropathy, autoimmune disease; CVID additionally increases lymphoma risk
