Anti-IgA antibodies can cause anaphylaxis to blood products

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Avoid **live vaccines** in major T-cell defects; immunize household contacts with safe vaccine choices
IgA-related transfusion reactions → washed cellular products or IgA-deficient plasma
CGD: TMP-SMX + itraconazole prophylaxis; genetic counseling for inherited defects

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vertical HIV: bacterial infections + zoster, nodes, maternal opportunistic infection; low CD4, positive virologic testing
Secondary hypogammaglobulinemia: nephrotic protein loss, B-cell malignancy, or rituximab exposure

table.title: Defect fingerprints
rows: Adolescent/adult; low IgG, poor vaccine response
Boy after 6 months; absent tonsils/B cells
Infant; absent thymic shadow, profound lymphopenia
Cold abscesses, eczema, retained teeth, pneumatoceles

primary-immunodeficiencies.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical immunology teaching.

prostate-carcinoma.name: Prostate carcinoma
prostate-carcinoma.scope: Adenocarcinoma, Gleason score, osteoblastic bone metastases, androgen deprivation therapy, radical prostatectomy, radiation
prostate-carcinoma.core: Older man with an abnormal PSA or hard prostatic nodule; risk stratification separates indolent localized disease from potentially lethal systemic cancer.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, Black ancestry, first-degree family history, BRCA2/Lynch-associated predisposition

rows.label: Clues
items: Often asymptomatic; urinary obstruction or hematuria usually later; peripheral-zone tumors may spare early urinary flow
★ Persistent back/bone pain, **osteoblastic lesions**, elevated alkaline phosphatase → metastatic disease
New weakness, saddle anesthesia, urinary retention → possible spinal cord/cauda equina compression

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Gland-forming adenocarcinoma; androgen-receptor signaling promotes growth; spread to pelvic nodes and axial skeleton

rows.label: Dx
items: Newly elevated PSA without urgent findings → repeat after transient causes resolve; PSA not cancer-specific
★ **Prostate MRI → targeted plus systematic core biopsy** when suspicion warrants; histology confirms
Negative MRI plus high clinical risk → systematic biopsy; no single PSA threshold excludes cancer
★ **Gleason = primary + secondary patterns**; 4+3 worse than 3+4; Grade Group 1–5
Stage using PSA, biopsy grade, clinical extent; high-risk/metastatic suspicion → PSMA PET/CT or conventional bone/CT imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Metastatic hormone-sensitive disease → **ADT + abiraterone/prednisone or enzalutamide**
Selected fit metastatic cases → add docetaxel; castration-resistant progression → continue ADT, add other agents
GnRH agonist leuprolide → initial flare; short antiandrogen cover; antagonist degarelix avoids flare
Suspected cord compression → **dexamethasone + urgent spinal MRI**, then radiation/surgical decompression

rows.label: Complications
items: Surgery: urinary incontinence, erectile dysfunction; radiation: proctitis, cystitis, erectile dysfunction
ADT: hot flashes, sexual dysfunction, osteoporosis, metabolic/cardiovascular toxicity; assess fracture risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: No proven primary prevention; PSA screening requires benefit/overdiagnosis discussion
USPSTF: shared decision age **55–69**; no routine screening ≥70; AUA offers earlier risk-based discussion

rows.label: Mimics
items: BPH: smooth symmetric enlargement, transition zone; lower urinary symptoms predominate
Prostatitis: tender/boggy gland, dysuria, fever; PSA may transiently rise

psoriasis.name: Psoriasis
psoriasis.scope: Plaque psoriasis, nail pitting and onycholysis, Auspitz sign, Koebner phenomenon, psoriatic arthritis, topical and systemic therapy
psoriasis.core: Sharply demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale, usually on extensor surfaces or scalp; inspect nails and screen for inflammatory arthritis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, obesity, smoking, alcohol; stress, trauma, streptococcal infection
Lithium, beta blockers, antimalarials; systemic glucocorticoid withdrawal can trigger severe rebound

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Nail pitting, onycholysis**, oil-drop discoloration support diagnosis
Auspitz sign: pinpoint bleeding after scale removal; Koebner phenomenon: lesions at trauma sites
Psoriatic arthritis: morning stiffness, DIP disease, dactylitis, enthesitis, asymmetric or axial involvement
Generalized pustules, erythroderma, fever, hemodynamic disturbance → urgent evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Immune-mediated TNF/IL-23/Th17 activation → accelerated keratinocyte turnover

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; biopsy if atypical; assess body surface area and functional impact
KOH scraping if fungal infection possible; inflammatory joint symptoms warrant rheumatology assessment
Before biologics: TB, hepatitis screening; before methotrexate: CBC, liver and renal tests, pregnancy assessment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized plaques → **topical corticosteroid + calcipotriene**; choose potency by site
Face/folds: low-potency steroid briefly or tacrolimus; emollients and scale removal aid penetration
★ Extensive/refractory disease → **narrowband UVB**, methotrexate, or targeted biologic; arthritis requires systemic control
Methotrexate contraindicated in pregnancy and significant liver disease; cyclosporine useful for rapid short-term control
Avoid routine systemic steroids; unstable erythrodermic/pustular disease → hospital support and specialist treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Joint destruction, depression, cardiometabolic disease; severe skin failure → fluid loss and infection
Systemic immunosuppression → infections; methotrexate → hepatotoxicity, marrow suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, weight management, limit alcohol; screen BP, lipids, diabetes, depression; reduce skin trauma

rows.label: Mimics
items: Tinea corporis: annular advancing edge, positive KOH
Seborrheic dermatitis: greasy scale in sebaceous areas
Atopic dermatitis: flexural eczema with marked pruritus

psoriasis.evidence: Not checked online; established dermatology and psoriatic arthritis teaching.

pulmonary-hypertension.name: Pulmonary hypertension
pulmonary-hypertension.scope: WHO groups 1-5 (PAH, left heart disease, lung disease/hypoxia, CTEPH, multifactorial), cor pulmonale, echocardiography, right heart catheterization, endothelin receptor antagonists, PDE-5 inhibitors
pulmonary-hypertension.core: Progressive exertional dyspnea, syncope or right-heart failure with elevated pulmonary pressures requires hemodynamic classification before vasodilator treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Connective-tissue disease, congenital shunts, portal hypertension, HIV, methamphetamine → PAH
Left-heart disease, chronic lung disease/hypoxia or prior pulmonary embolism are common secondary contexts

rows.label: Clues
items: Loud P2, RV heave, tricuspid regurgitation murmur; exertional chest pain or presyncope
JVD, hepatomegaly and edema → right-heart failure/cor pulmonale
Severe dyspnea with relatively preserved spirometry or low DLCO suggests pulmonary vascular disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pulmonary vascular resistance or elevated left filling pressure increases RV afterload
Sustained pressure overload → RV hypertrophy, dilation, reduced output and systemic venous congestion
Chronic alveolar hypoxia (COPD, OSA) → **pulmonary vasoconstriction** and remodeling → raised vascular resistance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Echocardiography** estimates probability and evaluates RV/left-heart function; not definitive pressure diagnosis
★ **Right-heart catheterization: mean PAP >20 mm Hg** at rest confirms PH
Precapillary: wedge ≤15 mm Hg and **PVR >2 Wood units**; postcapillary: wedge >15
★ **V/Q scan** screens CTEPH; normal perfusion essentially excludes chronic thromboembolic disease
PFT/DLCO, chest CT, sleep evaluation, HIV/autoimmune testing by history; vasoreactivity testing in selected PAH

rows.label: Tx
items: Oxygen for hypoxemia, diuresis for congestion; treat underlying disease and refer confirmed PAH/CTEPH
★ PAH → specialist **endothelin antagonist + PDE-5 inhibitor**; high-risk disease → parenteral prostacyclin
Vasoreactive idiopathic/heritable/drug-associated PAH → selected high-dose calcium-channel blocker; not empiric treatment
CTEPH → lifelong anticoagulation and pulmonary endarterectomy if operable; selected balloon angioplasty or riociguat
Do not routinely use PAH vasodilators for left-heart/lung-disease PH; PDE-5 drugs cannot combine with nitrates/riociguat

rows.label: Complications
items: RV failure, arrhythmia, syncope and death; pregnancy carries substantial maternal risk in PAH
Endothelin antagonists are teratogenic; some require liver monitoring

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid methamphetamine, address thromboembolic risk; vaccination, supervised exercise, pregnancy/contraception counseling

rows.label: Mimics
items: HFpEF: elevated wedge pressure identifies postcapillary cause
Deconditioning/anemia: no catheter-confirmed pulmonary pressure elevation

rosacea.name: Rosacea
rosacea.scope: Erythematotelangiectatic rosacea, papulopustular rosacea, phymatous rosacea (rhinophyma), ocular rosacea, triggers (heat, alcohol, spicy foods), topical metronidazole, oral doxycycline
rosacea.core: Adult with recurrent flushing progressing to persistent central facial redness, sometimes with inflammatory bumps or gritty eyes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Middle adulthood, family history, UV exposure
★ Flares with **heat, alcohol, spicy foods**, exertion, or emotional stress

rows.label: Clues
items: Facial burning or stinging, sensitive skin
★ Ocular disease may precede skin findings. Recurrent **chalazia** support diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Neurovascular dysregulation and innate immune inflammation. Phyma from sebaceous and connective tissue overgrowth

rows.label: Dx
items: Clinical by distribution and phenotype. Erythema may appear violaceous or subtle in darker skin
★ Eye pain, photophobia, or blurred vision → **urgent ophthalmology** for corneal involvement

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Papulopustular → **topical metronidazole**, azelaic acid, or ivermectin
★ Extensive or refractory inflammatory disease → **oral doxycycline**
Fixed erythema → topical brimonidine or oxymetazoline. Telangiectasias → vascular laser
Ocular → warm compresses, lid hygiene, artificial tears. Persistent → doxycycline
Established rhinophyma → laser or surgical debulking. Avoid facial topical steroids for rosacea

rows.label: Complications
items: Keratitis → corneal ulceration, scarring, vision loss. Severe rhinophyma may obstruct nasal airflow

rows.label: Prevention
items: Identify and limit individual triggers. Broad-spectrum SPF ≥ 30, gentle cleanser, moisturizer

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acne vulgaris: **comedones**, often truncal lesions
Seborrheic dermatitis: greasy scale in nasolabial folds, eyebrows, scalp
Cutaneous lupus: photosensitive malar eruption sparing nasolabial folds, usually without pustules

table.title: Classic phenotypes
rows: Inflammatory papules and pustules on convex face

rosacea.evidence: Checked AAD diagnosis, phenotype-directed treatment and trigger guidance, Nov 2026.

routine-prenatal-care.name: Routine prenatal care and early pregnancy
routine-prenatal-care.scope: Pregnancy diagnosis (beta-hCG), initial prenatal assessment, routine first-trimester screening, aneuploidy screening
routine-prenatal-care.core: Confirm and date pregnancy, assess maternal risks, offer one aneuploidy-screening strategy or diagnostic testing, and arrange time-sensitive prenatal studies.

rows.label: Who
items: All pregnancies; review obstetric history, drugs, illness, substance use, violence, family history
Offer carrier screening and genetic counseling; discuss patient preferences and right to decline

rows.label: Start/stop
items: Early visit: urine hCG confirms pregnancy; serum quantitative hCG for uncertain/complicated cases
★ First-trimester **ultrasound crown–rump length** best establishes gestational age
Serum screen 10–13 6/7 weeks; NT 11–13 6/7; cfDNA from 10 weeks

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Initial **CBC, ABO/Rh, antibody screen, urine culture**; HIV, syphilis, HBsAg, HCV, rubella immunity
GC/chlamydia by age/risk; offer one aneuploidy strategy regardless of maternal age
Anatomy ultrasound 18–22 weeks; AFP for open neural tube defects when not otherwise assessed

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Abnormal screen → counseling, ultrasound, **CVS/amniocentesis** before irreversible decisions
CVS: 10–13 weeks; amniocentesis: ≥15 weeks; neither automatically required after negative screening
Rh-negative, unsensitized → anti-D prophylaxis at 28 weeks and after sensitizing events

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **cfDNA is screening**, not diagnostic; does not screen open neural tube defects
Single hCG value cannot establish viability or location; pain/bleeding → ectopic evaluation
Folate before conception/early gestation; avoid alcohol, tobacco, teratogens; no live vaccines

table.title: Early and routine pregnancy calls
rows: Nausea, irregular bleeding or amenorrhea, even premenarche
Missed menses, urinary frequency, friable cervix, enlarged uterus
Brief sharp movement-triggered lower-quadrant pain, normal vitals
No added preterm, fluid, or placental risk

schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.name: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders
schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.scope: Brief psychotic disorder, schizophreniform disorder, schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, mesolimbic dopamine
schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.core: Psychosis with impaired reality testing: distinguish schizophrenia-spectrum disorders by duration, functional decline, and the relationship between mood episodes and psychosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, neurodevelopmental vulnerability; adolescent cannabis exposure increases risk
Typical onset late adolescence/early adulthood; exclude stimulant, hallucinogen, medication, and neurologic causes

rows.label: Clues
items: Delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech/behavior; negative symptoms: avolition, alogia, flat affect
★ At least **two core symptoms**, including delusions, hallucinations, or disorganized speech, for active-phase diagnosis
Suicidality, dangerous commands or inability to eat → urgent safety assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **↑Mesolimbic dopamine** → positive symptoms; mesocortical → negative symptoms, early working-memory deficits
D2 blockade reduces psychosis but nigrostriatal/tuberoinfundibular effects cause EPS and hyperprolactinemia
Structural correlate: **enlarged lateral and third ventricles**, reduced cortical volume

rows.label: Dx
items: Clinical history, collateral information, mental status; assess mood timeline and substance exposure
First episode → CBC/CMP, TSH, toxicology; HIV/syphilis or neuroimaging for relevant risks/atypical neurologic findings
★ **Schizoaffective**: ≥2 weeks psychosis without mood episode; mood episodes occupy most illness duration

rows.label: Tx
items: Safety crisis → hospitalization; acute agitation → de-escalation, then medication if needed
★ **Risperidone, aripiprazole or olanzapine** + coordinated specialty care, family education, CBT, supported employment
Schizoaffective depressive/bipolar subtype → add antidepressant or mood stabilizer according to mood syndrome
★ Failure of two adequate antipsychotic trials or persistent substantial suicide risk → **clozapine**
Adherence difficulty → long-acting injectable (haloperidol decanoate); catatonia → lorazepam, then ECT if refractory

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, homelessness, substance use, cardiometabolic disease; antipsychotics → metabolic syndrome, tardive dyskinesia, NMS
Clozapine → neutropenia, myocarditis, severe constipation; monitor ANC and symptoms

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid cannabis/stimulants; maintenance medication, relapse planning reduce recurrence
Monitor weight, BP, glucose, lipids; address tobacco use and cardiovascular risk
**High expressed emotion** (family criticism, hostility) → relapse; family therapy reduces recurrence

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mood disorder with psychosis: psychosis occurs exclusively during mood episodes
Delirium: fluctuating attention/awareness and acute medical cause
Delusional disorder: ≥1 month delusions with otherwise relatively preserved function, limited other psychotic symptoms
Substance/medication-induced psychosis: recent stimulants (mydriasis, tremor) or corticosteroids, intact orientation

septic-arthritis.name: Septic arthritis
septic-arthritis.scope: Nongonococcal, gonococcal, prosthetic joint infection, IV drug use, empiric coverage (vancomycin + cefepime), contiguous osteomyelitis
septic-arthritis.core: Acutely painful swollen joint with restricted passive motion → urgent aspiration and drainage; delayed treatment rapidly destroys cartilage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prosthesis, recent surgery/injection, rheumatoid arthritis, immunosuppression, diabetes, bacteremia
IV drug use → S aureus and gram-negative risk, including Pseudomonas
Young sexually active adults → disseminated gonorrhea; adjacent ulcers/osteomyelitis → contiguous spread
RA joint with new febrile monoarthritis → infection until aspirated, not flare

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually acute monoarthritis, often knee; fever may be absent, especially in older/immunocompromised adults
★ **Severe pain with both active and passive motion**; inability to bear weight; child's hip held flexed, abducted, externally rotated
Gonococcal dissemination: migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis, sparse pustules; may progress to purulent monoarthritis
Prosthetic infection: persistent pain, loosening, wound drainage or sinus tract, sometimes minimal systemic illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hematogenous seeding or direct inoculation → neutrophilic enzymes damage articular cartilage
Implant biofilm limits antibiotic eradication without surgical source control
★ **S aureus** most common, including RA-damaged joints: gram-positive cocci in clusters
Asplenia or recent pharyngitis → **streptococci**: gram-positive cocci in chains

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Arthrocentesis before antibiotics** when stable: cell count/differential, Gram stain, culture, crystals
Synovial WBC >50,000/µL, neutrophil predominance supports infection; lower counts or negative Gram stain never exclude
★ **Crystals do not exclude infection**; send cultures even when gout seems likely
Blood cultures; gonococcal: aspirate on **chocolate/Thayer-Martin agar** plus mucosal NAAT; MRI for suspected contiguous osteomyelitis
New warmth/effusion in OA joint → aspirate before any intra-articular steroid

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ After cultures → **IV vancomycin + cefepime or piperacillin-tazobactam** for severe disease, IV drug use, gram-negative risk
Stable low-risk adult: vancomycin ± ceftriaxone based on exposure; narrow to organism/susceptibility
Sepsis → immediate antibiotics without delaying for aspiration; large joints: arthroscopic washout; **hip → operative drainage**, not serial aspiration
Persistent symptoms → repeat drainage, seek abscess/osteomyelitis; mobilize after infection controlled

rows.label: Complications
items: Irreversible joint destruction, avascular necrosis, osteomyelitis, bacteremia, sepsis
Prolonged antibiotics → renal injury, line complications, C difficile; prolonged immobility → stiffness

rows.label: Prevention
items: Sterile procedures, treat skin infections, injection-harm reduction
Gonorrhea: treat partners, screen other STIs, abstain until treatment completed and partners treated

rows.label: Mimics
items: Crystal arthritis: polarized crystals; infection still possible concurrently
Bursitis: localized periarticular swelling, passive joint motion relatively preserved
Reactive arthritis: sterile inflammatory arthritis after GI/GU infection
Transient synovitis (child): afebrile, bears weight, ESR <40, WBC <12,000

table.title: Special treatment branches
rows: Debridement, implant retention, prolonged pathogen-directed antibiotics

sexual-dysfunction.name: Sexual dysfunction
sexual-dysfunction.scope: Female orgasmic disorder, female sexual interest/arousal disorder, genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder, premature ejaculation, SSRI-induced sexual dysfunction
sexual-dysfunction.core: Persistent, distressing impairment of desire, arousal, orgasm, ejaculation, or penetration; classify the affected phase before choosing treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Depression, anxiety, relationship conflict, sexual trauma, menopause
Diabetes, neurologic disease, pelvic surgery; SSRIs, antipsychotics, opioids

rows.label: Clues
items: Interest/arousal: ↓interest, fantasies, initiation, pleasure, cue response, genital sensations; assess adequate stimulation
★ Penetration pain/fear, pelvic-floor spasm blocking tampon/speculum → genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder (**vaginismus**)
Low lubrication, vaginal dryness, postcoital spotting → assess estrogen deficiency

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Serotonergic inhibition of sexual response; hypoestrogenism → mucosal atrophy
Performance anxiety and pain avoidance reinforce dysfunction
Bilateral oophorectomy → ↓**ovarian androgens** → low libido despite estrogen replacement, normal vaginal mucosa

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Symptoms usually ≥6 months + personal distress; frequency criteria depend on disorder
Private sexual/relationship history; review drugs, coercion, mood, and medical causes
Pelvic examination for pain; TSH, prolactin, glucose only when history suggests abnormality
Low desire without distress → normal variation; inadequate stimulation alone ≠ orgasmic disorder

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Education, couples/sex counseling, CBT; treat underlying disease and relationship contributors
Penetration disorder → pelvic-floor physical treatment, graded dilators; vaginal estrogen for menopausal atrophy
★ SSRI-induced: reduce dose if feasible, switch to or augment with **bupropion**
Acquired generalized HSDD: flibanserin in women <65, including postmenopause; separate from alcohol
Flibanserin: avoid hepatic impairment and moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors; not for drug-induced low desire

rows.label: Complications
items: Avoidance, relationship strain, reduced quality of life
Flibanserin: syncope; topical penile anesthetics: partner numbness

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vulvodynia: localized provoked vestibular tenderness
Major depression: pervasive anhedonia beyond sexual situations
Normal aging: slower response without clinically significant distress

sexual-dysfunction.evidence: FDA label checked 2026-10-30: [flibanserin, 2025](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/022526s013lbl.pdf); other content established teaching.

shock.name: Shock
shock.scope: Hypovolemic, cardiogenic, distributive (septic, anaphylactic, neurogenic), obstructive, fluid resuscitation, vasopressors
shock.core: Circulatory failure causing tissue hypoperfusion; normal blood pressure does not exclude early shock.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hemorrhage, GI losses, MI, infection, allergen exposure, spinal injury, thromboembolism
Recent surgery, immunosuppression, indwelling devices increase occult infection risk
Procedure bleeding: thoracentesis → intercostal artery, hemothorax; splenectomy → hemoperitoneum, left shoulder pain

rows.label: Clues
items: Tachycardia, altered mentation, oliguria, cool mottled skin; distributive forms may initially feel warm
★ **Anaphylaxis**: rapid airway swelling, wheezing, hypotension; skin findings may be absent
Neurogenic: **lost sympathetic tone** → hypotension, bradycardia or no tachycardia, warm skin after spinal cord injury

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Oxygen delivery falls below demand → anaerobic metabolism, lactate accumulation
Distributive vasodilation → relative hypovolemia despite normal total body fluid
Warm sepsis: high output, **high mixed venous O2**; pump failure: low contractility, congestion; hypovolemia: low preload

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Bedside ultrasound**: cardiac function, pericardial fluid, RV dilation, lung sliding, volume assessment
**Serial lactate**: hypoperfusion, best predicts course and mortality; trend with capillary refill, urine output
Septic shock: vasopressors for MAP ≥65 plus lactate >2 despite volume resuscitation
CBC, chemistry, ECG, troponin; cultures if infection suspected

rows.label: Tx
items: Airway, IV access; **isotonic crystalloid** (balanced, 0.9% saline) before imaging; restrict with pulmonary congestion
★ Hemorrhage → **control bleeding + blood products** (emergency O-negative); crystalloid as bridge; no vasopressors
★ Septic shock → antibiotics within 1 hour, drainage/debridement; crystalloid 30 mL/kg within 3 hours
★ Persistent septic hypotension → **norepinephrine**, MAP ≥65; add vasopressin, then epinephrine; refractory → hydrocortisone
Pulmonary edema after fluids → stop boluses, **inotrope**; children: epinephrine preferred, older exams may expect dopamine

rows.label: Complications
items: AKI, ischemic hepatitis, DIC, ARDS, bowel ischemia, multiorgan failure
Excess fluids → edema; vasopressors → digital/mesenteric ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early infection treatment, catheter hygiene, VTE prophylaxis, hemorrhage control
After anaphylaxis: trigger avoidance, epinephrine autoinjector, allergy referral

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vasovagal syncope: transient bradycardia, rapid recovery supine
Hypoglycemia: low bedside glucose, improvement with dextrose
Isolated head injury: hypertension + bradycardia (Cushing); trauma hypotension + tachycardia → assume hemorrhage

table.title: Hemodynamics and cause-directed rescue
rows: Decompress pneumothorax; drain tamponade; reperfuse PE

skin-cancer.name: Skin cancer
skin-cancer.scope: Actinic keratosis, squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, melanoma, photoprotection and sunscreen
skin-cancer.core: Changing pigmented lesions or persistent keratinizing, pearly, or ulcerated growths require examination and tissue diagnosis rather than empiric reassurance.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: UV exposure, fair skin, sunburns, tanning beds, older age; immunosuppression particularly increases SCC
Melanoma: numerous/atypical nevi, family/personal melanoma history; may arise without a preexisting nevus
Chronic wounds/scars predispose SCC; acral melanoma occurs regardless of skin pigmentation

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Melanoma: **ABCDE**—asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter, evolution; ugly-duckling lesion
Diameter >6 mm concerning, but smaller evolving lesions still require biopsy
Amelanotic melanoma may be pink; inspect soles, palms, nail beds; nail pigment extending onto fold concerning
Rapid growth, bleeding, nonhealing ulcer, fixation, neurologic symptoms, nodes → aggressive or advanced disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: UV-induced DNA damage → keratinocyte malignancy; melanocyte transformation causes melanoma
AK represents dysplastic keratinocytes with potential progression to invasive SCC

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious melanoma → **full-thickness excisional biopsy with narrow margins** to measure Breslow depth
Partial biopsy acceptable when complete excision impractical; avoid superficial sampling that prevents staging
Suspected keratinocyte carcinoma → deep shave or punch biopsy; <1 cm → **narrow-margin excisional biopsy**
AK persisting after topical fluorouracil → **excisional biopsy** to exclude invasive SCC
Breslow thickness/ulceration guide melanoma staging; sentinel-node discussion generally at ≥0.8 mm or ulceration

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized invasive cancers → **surgical excision**; high-risk/recurrent facial BCC/SCC → Mohs
Low-risk BCC → **excision with narrow margins (≤1 cm)**; no sentinel node biopsy
Positive margin on BCC/SCC → **reexcision** or Mohs, not observation
★ Melanoma → **wide local excision after diagnostic biopsy**; margins depend on depth
Advanced melanoma → specialist immunotherapy, selected BRAF-targeted drugs; avoid destructive treatment before diagnosis

rows.label: Complications
items: BCC: extensive local destruction, rare metastasis; SCC: nodal metastasis, especially high-risk sites/immunosuppression
Melanoma: distant metastases, including brain; immunotherapy → colitis, endocrinopathies, pneumonitis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Broad-spectrum SPF ≥30**, reapply every 2 hours/outdoors after swimming; shade, protective clothing, no tanning
Infants <6 months → **shade, protective clothing**; avoid sunscreen
Self-examination, postcancer follow-up; suspicious lesions require evaluation despite uncertain population-screening benefit

rows.label: Mimics
items: Seborrheic keratosis: waxy stuck-on plaque; atypical lesions still biopsy
Dermatofibroma: firm papule with dimple sign
Benign nevus: stable symmetric uniform, <6 mm → **observation**, even with melanoma family history
Congenital melanocytic nevus: brown lesion from birth, may darken or grow coarse hair

table.title: Nonmelanoma patterns
rows: Nonhealing scaly indurated plaque/ulcer/nodule; lip/ear common
Assess high-risk features and regional nodes
Pearly rolled edge, telangiectasia, central ulcer
Treat despite slow growth; local invasion

skin-cancer.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AAD melanoma guidance](https://www.aad.org/member/clinical-quality/guidelines/melanoma); established keratinocyte-cancer and photoprotection teaching.

study-designs.name: Study designs
study-designs.scope: Case-control, cohort, cross-sectional, RCT, control selection, bias, internal and external validity
study-designs.core: Study design determines how participants are selected, when exposure/outcome are measured, and which associations can be estimated without avoidable bias.

rows.label: Definition
items: Internal validity: credible within-study inference; external validity: applicability elsewhere
**Selection/ascertainment bias**: institutional or already-ill sample misrepresents target population
Subjective scoring by different raters → **interobserver variability**; standardize criteria

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **Randomization balances confounders on average**; concealed allocation prevents enrollment bias
Blinding reduces behavior/assessment bias; intention-to-treat retains original randomized groups
Loss to follow-up can bias estimates when related to exposure and outcome

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Case-control controls → **same source population** that produced cases, independent of exposure
Prospective measurement improves temporality but does not eliminate confounding in observational research
Life table: poorest 1-year survival → steepest interval drop, not lowest cumulative point

rows.label: Compare
items: Confounding: third-variable distortion; randomize, restrict, match, stratify, or adjust
Effect modification: association differs across strata; report rather than remove it
Clinician-chosen treatment → **selection bias/confounding by indication**; randomization prevents it

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Case-control sampling cannot directly estimate incidence or risk** without additional population data
★ Cross-sectional data lack reliable **temporal sequence**; prevalent cases favor longer survivors
Random selection supports generalizability; random assignment supports causal inference

study-designs.evidence: Established epidemiologic definitions; no clinical guideline involved.

subarachnoid-hemorrhage.name: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
subarachnoid-hemorrhage.scope: Ruptured saccular aneurysm, thunderclap headache, noncontrast head CT, lumbar puncture and xanthochromia, nimodipine, complications
subarachnoid-hemorrhage.core: Sudden headache maximal within seconds, often during exertion, with possible meningismus or collapse: presume subarachnoid hemorrhage until excluded.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, hypertension, family history, prior aneurysm; autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
**Saccular aneurysm rupture**: most common nontraumatic cause, exceeds AVM; circle-of-Willis branch points; cocaine ↑ risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Vomiting, photophobia, neck stiffness, transient loss of consciousness; sentinel headache may precede major hemorrhage
★ **Painful pupil-involving CN III palsy** → posterior communicating artery aneurysm
Sudden stupor, focal deficits, Cushing response, seizures → raised ICP/herniation; normal exam does not exclude hemorrhage

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Blood enters subarachnoid space → meningeal irritation, ↑ICP, impaired CSF resorption
Blood-breakdown products and vascular injury contribute to delayed cerebral ischemia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Noncontrast head CT immediately**: hyperdense basal cisterns/sulci; sensitivity declines with elapsed time
★ Negative CT >6 hours after onset or neurologic deficit → **LP**, assessing xanthochromia and RBCs
High-quality CT within 6 hours, neurologically intact, expert interpretation → may exclude SAH without routine LP
Confirmed blood → **CT angiography**; negative/inconclusive CTA with suspected aneurysm → catheter angiography
Traumatic tap may show falling RBCs; clearing alone cannot reliably exclude SAH

rows.label: Tx
items: Support airway, reverse anticoagulation, analgesia; severe hypertension → IV nicardipine; avoid hypotension/BP swings
★ **Urgent aneurysm coiling or clipping**, preferably within 24 hours, prevents rebleeding
★ **Enteral nimodipine for 21 days**, maintain euvolemia; no prophylactic hypervolemia
Acute symptomatic hydrocephalus → external ventricular drainage
Secured aneurysm + delayed ischemia → induced hypertension; refractory → endovascular vasodilator/angioplasty

rows.label: Complications
items: Early rebleeding, hydrocephalus, seizures; delayed ischemia typically days 3–14
Hyponatremia from SIADH or cerebral salt wasting; stress cardiomyopathy, arrhythmias, pulmonary edema
ACom aneurysm rupture/clipping → **frontal lobe injury**: abulia, apathy, reduced spontaneous speech without depressed mood

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation and BP control; specialist screening discussion for ≥2 affected first-degree relatives or high-risk ADPKD

rows.label: Mimics
items: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction: recurrent thunderclap headaches; segmental angiographic narrowing
Meningitis: fever and inflammatory CSF rather than aneurysmal bleeding
Migraine: usually slower onset, recurrent stereotyped episodes; first thunderclap still needs hemorrhage evaluation

substance-use-disorders.name: Substance use disorders
substance-use-disorders.scope: Diagnostic criteria (mild, moderate, severe), cocaine use disorder, amphetamine use disorder, cannabis use disorder, motivational interviewing, cognitive behavioral therapy, 12-step programs
substance-use-disorders.core: A problematic pattern causing impaired control, risky use, social impairment or physiologic adaptation defines substance use disorder; severity follows criterion count.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, trauma, psychiatric comorbidity, early exposure, unstable housing and peer availability
Persistent psychosocial stress and limited treatment access worsen trajectory

rows.label: Clues
items: Tolerance/withdrawal not required; physiologic adaptation during prescribed use alone does not establish disorder
Stimulant withdrawal: fatigue, hypersomnia, depression and craving; assess suicide risk
Cannabis withdrawal: irritability, anxiety, insomnia and reduced appetite after sustained use
Caffeine withdrawal: diffuse headache 12–48 h after stopping intake, including NPO surgery; normal neurologic exam

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reward learning and neuroadaptation strengthen cue-driven behavior while impairing control
Cocaine blocks monoamine reuptake; amphetamines increase release; cannabinoids act mainly at CB1 receptors
THC lipophilic, adipose-stored: urine positive for weeks in chronic use; other drugs clear in days

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **≥2 of 11 DSM-5 criteria in 12 months**; severity **mild 2–3, moderate 4–5, severe ≥6**
Control/social: larger/longer use, failed cutdown, time spent, craving, role failure, social problems, abandoned activities
Risk/pharmacologic: hazardous use, continued despite physical/psychological harm, tolerance, withdrawal
Clinical interview establishes disorder; urine drug testing documents exposure, not severity or current impairment
Screen co-occurring depression, psychosis, HIV/hepatitis risk and polysubstance use; confirm unexpected immunoassay positives

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Motivational interviewing**: explore ambivalence, elicit personal goals, support autonomy; avoid confrontation
★ Stimulant disorder → **contingency management**, CBT/community reinforcement; no FDA-approved maintenance drug
Cannabis disorder → motivational enhancement, CBT and contingency management; no established approved medication
Peer/12-step programs as adjuncts; tailor outpatient versus residential intensity to safety/support and impairment
Stimulant agitation → benzodiazepines/cooling; uncomplicated cannabis intoxication, mild paranoia → observe, no drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Cocaine/amphetamine → MI, stroke, arrhythmia, psychosis; chronic methamphetamine → cardiomyopathy and dental injury
Cannabis → impaired driving, hyperemesis (cessation, fluids, capsaicin/haloperidol), anxiety or psychosis
Stimulant crash can precipitate severe depression/suicidality; withdrawal usually lacks alcohol-like autonomic danger
Older adults: new benzodiazepine (temazepam) → subacute ataxia, dysarthria, confusion, falls

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Harm reduction: **naloxone** for possible opioid contamination, avoid using alone, offer fentanyl testing access
Treat comorbid illness, relapse planning, overdose education and regular follow-up; recurrence prompts reassessment
Adolescent experimentation without impairment → counsel teen and family; no formal treatment program

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bipolar mania: episodes persist independently of intoxication
Primary psychosis: symptoms outside substance exposure periods
ADHD: longstanding childhood-onset pattern, not episodic intoxication

substance-use-disorders.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ASAM/AAAP stimulant guideline 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11105801/); DSM-5 criteria established definitions.

table.title: Intoxication by substance
rows: Mydriasis, hypertension, hyperreflexia, paranoia, pressured speech
Violent agitation, hyperthermia; formication with excoriations; MDMA empathic
Red conjunctivae, dry mouth, tachycardia, hunger, slowed time
**Nystagmus**, analgesia, hypertension, myoclonus; violent-catatonic fluctuation, mutism
Perioral/perinasal rash, solvent odor, ataxia/slurring; clears <1 hour
Coma, apnea, hypotension, bradycardia, sluggish pupils

surgical-wound-complications.name: Surgical wound complications
surgical-wound-complications.scope: Superficial wound separation, fascial dehiscence (profuse serosanguineous drainage, emergent reclosure), evisceration (sterile saline dressings, emergency surgery), wound hematoma, wound seroma, surgical site infection
surgical-wound-complications.core: Postoperative wound drainage or separation requires determining whether fascia is intact; fascial failure is a surgical emergency even without exposed bowel.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, diabetes, malnutrition, smoking, glucocorticoids, wound infection, emergency/contaminated surgery
Vomiting, coughing, ileus or strenuous activity increase abdominal pressure on healing closure

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Sudden profuse serosanguineous drainage**, popping sensation, or new bulge → suspect deep disruption
Erythema, warmth, worsening pain, purulence → infection; systemic toxicity may precede visible skin changes
★ Pain out of proportion, crepitus, bullae, rapid progression → **necrotizing infection**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Early wound tensile strength depends on sutures; collagen remodeling later restores tissue support
Dead space permits fluid/blood accumulation; infection and poor perfusion impair collagen deposition

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Inspect/probe separated incision gently using sterile technique to assess **fascial integrity**
CBC, culture purulent drainage; systemic illness → blood cultures/lactate
Uncertain deep collection, stable patient → ultrasound/CT; obvious emergency → surgery without imaging delay

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Evisceration: sterile saline-moistened dressing**, supine, NPO, IV fluids, antibiotics, emergency operating room
Never force exposed bowel back through wound; surgical exploration determines viability and closure
Cellulitis alone → cefazolin/cephalexin; purulence → drainage, add antibiotics for cellulitis/systemic illness
Polymicrobial deep infection → piperacillin-tazobactam; add vancomycin for MRSA risk
Necrotizing infection → immediate debridement + broad IV antibiotics; antibiotics alone insufficient

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess, sepsis, bowel ischemia, incisional hernia; delayed healing and recurrent separation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Preincision antibiotic prophylaxis, sterile technique, glucose control, smoking cessation, adequate protein/calories

rows.label: Mimics
items: Contact dermatitis: pruritic geometric rash matching adhesive, no purulent drainage
Normal healing ridge: firm linear swelling without progressive pain, erythema, or systemic illness

table.title: Stable localized findings
rows: Observe; aspirate/drain if symptomatic or persistent
Small stable: observe; expanding: evacuate, control bleeding
Open/drain if needed, dressings, secondary closure/healing

surgical-wound-complications.evidence: Not checked online; established postoperative wound and emergency surgical management.

systemic-vasculitis.name: Systemic vasculitis
systemic-vasculitis.scope: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (c-ANCA/PR3), microscopic polyangiitis (p-ANCA/MPO), eosinophilic GPA, polyarteritis nodosa, giant cell arteritis, Takayasu arteritis, immunosuppressive therapy
systemic-vasculitis.core: Vessel inflammation presenting as unexplained multisystem ischemia: vessel size, organ pattern, antibodies and tissue distinguish the syndromes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autoimmune predisposition; hydralazine/propylthiouracil can induce ANCA disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Constitutional symptoms, palpable purpura, skin ulcers, mononeuritis multiplex
★ **Hemoptysis + falling hemoglobin + RBC casts** → pulmonary–renal emergency

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ANCA disease → pauci-immune necrotizing injury; larger-vessel inflammation → stenosis, thrombosis, aneurysms
Granulomas: GPA/EGPA, GCA/Takayasu; PAN: necrotizing medium-artery inflammation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis, creatinine, CBC/differential, ESR/CRP**, chest imaging, hepatitis serologies
PR3/MPO supports diagnosis; negative ANCA cannot exclude, isolated positive cannot confirm
★ **Biopsy involved tissue**, especially kidney with GN; do not delay emergency therapy
GCA → temporal artery biopsy/expert ultrasound; **steroids before confirmation**
Takayasu → CTA/MRA; PAN → biopsy or visceral angiography showing microaneurysms

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Organ-threatening disease → **urgent immunosuppression**; stabilize bleeding, renal failure, ischemia
GPA/MPA maintenance → rituximab/azathioprine; methotrexate if renal function permits
Plasma exchange not routine in ANCA; consider severe renal disease/anti-GBM overlap
GCA steroid sparing → tocilizumab; elective vascular reconstruction after inflammation controlled
HCV cryoglobulinemia → **direct-acting antivirals**, not immunosuppression alone; older questions may expect interferon-alfa

rows.label: Complications
items: Blindness, renal failure, stroke, bowel infarction, aortic aneurysm
Cyclophosphamide → infertility/cystitis/malignancy; rituximab → HBV reactivation; steroids → infection/osteoporosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **TMP-SMX** with cyclophosphamide/rituximab induction; HBV/TB testing before biologics
Vaccination, bone protection, fertility counseling; follow clinical findings, not ANCA titers alone

rows.label: Mimics
items: Endocarditis: positive blood cultures/vegetations; ANCA sometimes positive
Anti-GBM: linear IgG on renal biopsy
Cholesterol emboli: vascular procedure, blue toes, eosinophilia, preserved pulses

table.title: Disease signatures
rows: PR3/c-ANCA; destructive sinonasal/ear disease, cavitary lungs, GN
Severe disease: same induction as GPA
Steroids; severe → cyclophosphamide; nonsevere relapsing → mepolizumab
Age >50; jaw claudication, visual symptoms, PMR
Young women; pulse/BP discrepancy, arm claudication

testicular-cancer.name: Testicular cancer
testicular-cancer.scope: Seminoma, nonseminomatous germ cell tumors, sex cord-stromal tumors (Leydig cell, Sertoli cell), tumor markers (AFP, beta-hCG, LDH), scrotal ultrasound, radical inguinal orchiectomy
testicular-cancer.core: A solid intratesticular lesion requires urgent evaluation for malignancy; an inguinal approach preserves proper staging and lymphatic drainage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Cryptorchidism**, prior contralateral germ cell tumor, family history, testicular dysgenesis
Most germ cell tumors arise in young adults; older men also require consideration of lymphoma

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually painless firm enlargement or heaviness; pain does not exclude malignancy
Gynecomastia from hormone production; back pain may indicate retroperitoneal nodes
Cough/dyspnea, supraclavicular nodes suggest dissemination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Most adult tumors germ cell-derived; mixed tumors managed as nonseminomatous
Lymphatic spread follows gonadal vessels to retroperitoneal para-aortic nodes rather than initial inguinal drainage

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Scrotal ultrasound with Doppler** first distinguishes intratesticular from extratesticular lesions
★ **AFP, β-hCG, LDH before orchiectomy**; repeat afterward for staging and response
CT abdomen/pelvis + chest imaging for metastases; normal markers do not exclude cancer
Avoid transscrotal needle biopsy or scrotal orchiectomy; disrupted lymphatics complicate treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Radical inguinal orchiectomy** for suspicious solid mass; discuss sperm banking before gonadotoxic treatment
Stage I seminoma: surveillance preferred when reliable; carboplatin or radiation selected alternatives
Stage I nonseminoma: surveillance, cisplatin-based chemotherapy, or retroperitoneal node dissection according to risk
★ Metastatic germ cell tumor → cisplatin-based **BEP**; residual nonseminomatous mass may require resection
Sex cord-stromal tumors: surgery; monitor endocrine manifestations and malignant features

rows.label: Complications
items: Infertility, hypogonadism; assess contralateral function
BEP: bleomycin pulmonary toxicity; cisplatin nephrotoxicity/ototoxicity; etoposide-associated leukemia
Retroperitoneal node surgery may cause retrograde ejaculation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Orchiopexy reduces cryptorchid-associated risk but does not eliminate it; no routine population screening
Strict stage-specific surveillance with examination, markers, and imaging after treatment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hydrocele: transilluminates; ultrasound needed if testis not palpable
Epididymitis: tender epididymis, urinary/infectious symptoms
Torsion: abrupt severe pain, absent cremasteric reflex; immediate exploration when strongly suspected

testicular-torsion.name: Testicular torsion
testicular-torsion.scope: Testicular torsion, absent cremasteric reflex, bell-clapper deformity, Doppler ultrasound, surgical detorsion and bilateral orchiopexy
testicular-torsion.core: Sudden unilateral scrotal pain with vomiting in an adolescent is spermatic cord torsion until excluded; salvage depends on immediate action.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Bell-clapper deformity permits excessive intravaginal rotation; often bilateral anatomic predisposition
Pubertal peak; may follow sleep, activity, or minor trauma; neonates can have extravaginal torsion

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **High-riding horizontal testis, absent cremasteric reflex**, diffuse tenderness and swelling
Pain may present as lower abdominal discomfort without volunteered scrotal symptoms
Prior self-resolving attacks suggest intermittent torsion; symptom resolution does not eliminate recurrence risk
Delayed fever/erythema can occur; no single examination finding reliably excludes torsion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cord rotation obstructs venous drainage then arterial inflow → progressive ischemia
Viability falls rapidly with delay; greatest salvage when detorsion occurs within about 6 hours

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ High clinical suspicion → **immediate urologic exploration**, no imaging delay
Equivocal presentation → **color Doppler ultrasound**, comparing perfusion with opposite testis
Reduced/absent flow or twisted cord supports diagnosis; preserved flow possible in partial/intermittent torsion
Urinalysis for infection if uncertain; pyuria does not automatically exclude simultaneous torsion
Examine both testes in boys with unexplained acute abdominal pain; ultrasound cannot overrule compelling clinical findings

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Urgent surgical detorsion + bilateral orchiopexy**; orchiectomy only if nonviable
NPO, IV analgesia, fluids as needed; call urology while preparing operation
★ If surgical delay unavoidable → **manual outward detorsion** as bridge; direction sometimes reversed
Pain relief after manual detorsion still requires operative confirmation and fixation; residual twisting possible

rows.label: Complications
items: Infarction, testicular loss, later atrophy, reduced fertility; endocrine function often maintained by opposite testis
Reperfusion does not guarantee long-term viability; follow-up for atrophy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Contralateral fixation addresses shared anatomy; evaluate recurrent episodic scrotal pain promptly
Teach adolescents to report sudden pain immediately despite embarrassment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Epididymitis: gradual pain, urinary/STI symptoms, increased epididymal Doppler flow
Appendix testis torsion: focal superior-pole tenderness, blue-dot sign, preserved testicular flow
Incarcerated hernia: irreducible inguinoscrotal mass, possible bowel obstruction

testicular-torsion.evidence: Not checked online; established urologic emergency assessment and salvage principles.

urinary-incontinence.name: Urinary incontinence
urinary-incontinence.core: Involuntary urine leakage is classified by triggers, urgency, bladder emptying, and ability to reach a toilet; reversible contributors often coexist.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Childbirth, pelvic surgery, aging, obesity; diabetes, neurologic disease, prostate enlargement
Diuretics, sedatives, anticholinergics, constipation, infection, impaired mobility/cognition worsen control

rows.label: Clues
items: History: timing, volume, dysuria, weak stream, nocturia, fluid intake, obstetric/surgical and neurologic history
★ **New saddle anesthesia, leg weakness, retention** → urgent cauda equina evaluation
Continuous leakage after pelvic surgery/radiation suggests fistula; recurrent UTIs/hematuria require further investigation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stress: aging/multiparity weaken pelvic floor → **urethral hypermobility**, low sphincter tone
Urge: **uninhibited detrusor contractions** (detrusor instability), worsened by caffeine; MS lesion → low residual
Overflow: **detrusor underactivity/acontractile bladder** (MS, diabetes, stroke) or outlet obstruction → high residual
Functional impairment can prevent continence despite intact lower urinary tract function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis + voiding diary**, focused pelvic/prostate and neurologic examination; review medications
Cough stress test with reasonably full bladder; assess prolapse, atrophy, fecal impaction
**Q-tip excursion >30°** on Valsalva → urethral hypermobility (urethrocele)
★ Suspected retention/emptying symptoms → **postvoid residual**; persistent >200 mL suggests inadequate emptying
No routine initial urodynamics/cystoscopy; uncertainty, hematuria, refractory symptoms → additional testing

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat reversible contributor; mixed incontinence → target most bothersome component
★ **Pelvic floor training/bladder training** underpin conservative care; weight loss, reduce caffeine, timed voiding
Urgency drugs: mirabegron or antimuscarinic (oxybutynin); discuss cognitive risk and avoid antimuscarinics with retention
Mirabegron may increase BP; avoid severe uncontrolled hypertension; refractory urgency → botulinum toxin or neuromodulation
Genitourinary syndrome of menopause → local vaginal estrogen when suitable; not systemic estrogen for leakage

rows.label: Complications
items: Dermatitis, falls from rushing, social isolation, sleep disruption
Overflow → hydronephrosis/renal injury; bladder botulinum toxin → retention, UTI

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication review, accessible toilet, mobility aids; bowel regularity, maintain strength and weight

rows.label: Mimics
items: Polyuria: high urine volume from hyperglycemia/diuresis rather than primary storage failure
Vaginal fistula: constant leakage unrelated to voiding urge or exertion

urinary-tract-infections.name: Urinary tract infections
urinary-tract-infections.scope: Asymptomatic bacteriuria, acute cystitis, pyelonephritis, catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI), catheter removal, empiric antibiotics
urinary-tract-infections.core: Symptoms localize urinary infection: bladder disease lacks systemic illness; renal involvement causes fever or flank pain; bacteriuria alone is insufficient.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual activity, spermicides, pregnancy, obstruction/stones, urinary retention, instrumentation
Catheter duration, diabetes, prior resistant isolates or antibiotics increase complicated-course risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, frequency, urgency, suprapubic discomfort; absent vaginal discharge supports urinary source
★ **Rigors, CVA tenderness, vomiting, hypotension** → pyelonephritis or urosepsis
Catheterized patients: new urinary/systemic symptoms; cloudy urine or pyuria alone insufficient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Usually ascending enteric bacteria, predominantly E coli; catheter biofilm maintains colonization
Urease-producing Proteus alkalinizes urine → struvite calculi and persistent infection
Pregnancy: progesterone ureteral relaxation + uterine compression → **stasis**; physiologic right-sided ureteral dilation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis**: pyuria, leukocyte esterase, nitrites; pyelonephritis → heavy pyuria, WBC clumps/casts; negative nitrites don't exclude
Culture: pyelonephritis, pregnancy, CAUTI, recurrence/resistance; classic cystitis often clinical
Persistent fever after 48–72 hours, sepsis, or suspected obstruction → renal imaging
Asymptomatic bacteriuria: usually ≥100,000 CFU/mL; delirium alone → seek other causes without automatic antibiotics
Febrile non-toilet-trained child → **catheterized** urinalysis/culture; bag/clean-catch contaminate

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Treat asymptomatic bacteriuria only in pregnancy or before urologic mucosal trauma** in routine adult scenarios
★ CAUTI → **remove unnecessary catheter**; if needed and present >2 weeks, replace before culture/treatment
★ Infected obstructed collecting system → **urgent drainage + IV antibiotics**; antibiotics alone insufficient
Improving nonpregnant pyelonephritis: fluoroquinolone 5–7 days, other active drugs 7 days; high-risk cases individualized
Febrile infant → **cefotaxime/ceftriaxone**; first-generation cefazolin inadequate

rows.label: Complications
items: Bacteremia, septic shock, renal/perinephric abscess; pregnancy → preterm birth
Antibiotics → resistance, C difficile; fluoroquinolones → tendon injury, QT prolongation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid unnecessary catheters; closed drainage, daily removal assessment
Postmenopausal recurrence → vaginal estrogen
Recurrence ≥3/year or ≥2 in 6 months → postcoital or daily nitrofurantoin/TMP-SMX
Sporadic postcoital cystitis → **void before/after intercourse**; stop diaphragm/spermicide; condoms don't prevent

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vaginitis: discharge, pruritus, external burning
Urethritis: sexual exposure, discharge, positive gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT
Bladder pain syndrome: chronic symptoms, repeatedly negative cultures

table.title: Initial antibiotics; tailor to culture/resistance
rows: Ciprofloxacin/levofloxacin; initial ceftriaxone if resistance risk
IV fluids + ceftriaxone; cefepime/piperacillin-tazobactam if Pseudomonas risk
Avoid nitrofurantoin/fosfomycin: inadequate renal tissue levels

valvular-heart-disease.name: Valvular heart disease
valvular-heart-disease.scope: Aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation, mitral stenosis, mitral regurgitation, mitral valve prolapse, physical exam, echocardiography, surgical and transcatheter replacement
valvular-heart-disease.core: Murmur timing, location, radiation, and loading maneuvers localize valve disease; symptoms and ventricular response determine intervention.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Trileaflet calcification, age >70 → AS; rheumatic disease → MS
Bicuspid valve: murmur from youth, premature calcific AS (40s–60s); childhood **endocarditis**; adult aortic dissection
AR: endocarditis, dissection, **root dilation** (Marfan, hypertension; murmur along right sternal border)
MR: ischemia, myxomatous prolapse (connective tissue laxity), chamber dilation

rows.label: Clues
items: Exertional dyspnea, pulmonary edema, reduced exercise tolerance; abrupt deterioration suggests acute regurgitation
★ **Exertional syncope, angina, or HF** with obstruction → severe symptomatic disease
Squatting/handgrip increase regurgitant murmurs; standing/Valsalva → earlier MVP click, squatting → later

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stenosis produces upstream pressure overload; regurgitation produces chamber volume overload
Acute regurgitation lacks compensatory dilation, rapidly elevating filling pressures and reducing forward output
Mitral stenosis: ↑LA pressure, ↑PCWP, ↑pulmonary artery pressure; **LVEDP normal**; AF abolishes presystolic accentuation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TTE Doppler** defines anatomy, severity, EF, chamber dimensions, pulmonary pressures
Severe AS: velocity ≥4 m/s, mean gradient ≥40, or valve area ≤1 cm²; discordance requires reassessment
Severe MS: valve area ≤1.5 cm²; TEE for thrombus before balloon intervention or uncertain anatomy
★ Acute murmur with shock → **urgent echocardiography**; TEE if endocarditis/dissection suspected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute severe AR/MR → **urgent surgery**, stabilize with afterload reduction/diuresis if BP permits
Severe primary MR: **EF ≤60% or LVESD ≥40 mm** triggers intervention even without symptoms
Secondary MR → optimize HF treatment first; selected persistent severe cases benefit from transcatheter edge-to-edge repair
Avoid excessive preload reduction in severe AS; symptomatic relief never replaces needed valve intervention

rows.label: Complications
items: Heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, AF, systemic embolism, endocarditis
Mechanical prosthesis: thrombosis/bleeding; bioprosthesis: structural degeneration
Prosthetic dysfunction/paravalvular leak → new murmur, **schistocytes**, hemolytic anemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Warfarin for mechanical valves**; no DOAC substitution; rheumatic MS with AF also requires warfarin
Prosthetic valve or prior endocarditis → selected dental prophylaxis; native isolated MVP does not qualify
Periodic echo and symptom review; treat rheumatic fever to prevent recurrent valve injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: HCM: systolic murmur increases with Valsalva/standing
Aortic sclerosis: ejection murmur without significant gradient; flow murmur: normal valve anatomy

table.title: Valve signatures and definitive options
rows: Crescendo-decrescendo, carotids; soft A2; pulsus parvus et tardus
Early diastolic decrescendo; wide pulse pressure
Loud S1, opening snap, apical mid-diastolic rumble
Suitable symptomatic rheumatic valve → balloon commissurotomy
LLSB holosystolic, louder on inspiration; right HF

valvular-heart-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established echo thresholds and intervention framework.

venous-thromboembolism.name: Venous thromboembolism
venous-thromboembolism.core: Unilateral swollen leg or sudden unexplained dyspnea with pleuritic pain; pulmonary embolism severity determined by hemodynamics, not clot size.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Immobilization, surgery, malignancy, estrogen, pregnancy/postpartum, inherited thrombophilia
**Previous VTE** is the strongest predictor of recurrence; remote surgery months ago adds little
**Central venous catheter** → main cause of upper-extremity DVT

rows.label: Clues
items: DVT: asymmetric calf tenderness, warmth; PE: tachycardia, hypoxemia, hemoptysis, sometimes normal oxygen saturation
Syncope, elevated JVP, cool extremities → impending RV failure; normal chest radiograph does not exclude PE

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stasis/endothelial injury/hypercoagulability → venous clot; pulmonary obstruction → V/Q mismatch, RV pressure overload
Massive PE: high RA/PA pressure, low PCWP, low output; RV infarct: PA pressure normal/low

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Wells/pretest probability** first; very low-risk + PERC-negative → no testing
★ Low/intermediate probability → **D-dimer**; negative excludes; positive/high probability → **CT pulmonary angiography**
Age >50: D-dimer threshold age × 10 ng/mL FEU; contrast contraindication → V/Q scan
DVT → compression US; negative proximal scan + persistent suspicion → repeat in 1 week
Low-probability V/Q + high clinical suspicion is nondiagnostic → **CT angiography**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Oxygen/support circulation; unstable and unsafe for CT → bedside **echo**; high suspicion/delayed imaging → anticoagulate
★ Stable VTE → **apixaban/rivaroxaban**; cancer → LMWH/DOAC; pregnancy → LMWH; severe renal failure → UFH
Lysis contraindicated/fails → catheter thrombectomy/surgical embolectomy; active intracranial bleeding precludes lysis
Acute proximal DVT/PE + absolute anticoagulation contraindication → temporary **IVC filter**, remove when feasible
Acute proximal DVT/PE without DOAC → immediate **heparin**; warfarin alone never initial; inferior in cancer

rows.label: Complications
items: Postthrombotic syndrome; persistent dyspnea → evaluate chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
Anticoagulation/thrombolysis → bleeding; heparin → HIT

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Major transient trigger → **3 months** anticoagulation; unprovoked/persistent risk → extended course if low bleeding risk
Aspirin or 1 month inadequate; DOACs now preferred, older exam questions may expect warfarin 3–6 months
Hospital prophylaxis: LMWH; active bleeding → intermittent pneumatic compression; early mobilization
Hip arthroplasty → LMWH, warfarin or DOAC; aspirin now accepted, older exam questions may expect anticoagulant

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cellulitis: predominantly skin erythema, portal of entry
Ruptured Baker cyst: posterior knee symptoms, cyst on US
Pneumonia: focal infiltrate and infectious prodrome
Amniotic fluid embolism: peripartum collapse with **DIC/low fibrinogen**

table.title: Treatment branches; 2026 PE guidance uses categories A–E
rows: Stable; low PESI/sPESI; no RV injury
Normotensive + RV dysfunction and/or troponin elevation
Sustained SBP <90 mm Hg or shock
